name: Aether
desc: Adds air to the top of a sound with two amounts, mid air and high air, plus an exciter. An arc meter shows the output peak.

wiki.intro: Aether is an air effect for the insert mixer. It combines a broad high shelf with a harmonic exciter, and is normally used to brighten vocals, mixes or a whole bus. The editor is built around two large knobs and an output peak meter.
controls: Amount of the presence exciter, scaled from 0 to 100.
Amount of the air shelf, scaled from 0 to 15 dB.
Moves the two air knobs together.
Switches the effect on and off.
Selects the dynamic air model, which is on by default.
Dry and wet balance, shown in the status line.
tips: Raise high air first and add mid air only if the top still sounds thin.
With Link on, one knob drags the other, which gives a quick single-control setting.

name: Apex Limiter
desc: Mastering limiter with look-ahead, a true-peak ceiling, selectable styles, an optional levelling stage, oversampling, dither and a loudness meter, shown over a scrolling level display.

wiki.intro: Apex Limiter is a look-ahead limiter for the last slot of a track or the master. You set how much gain to push into it and where the output ceiling sits, and the display shows the level history and the gain reduction.
controls: Input gain pushed into the limiter. Drag the Gain handle on the left of the display.
Output ceiling. Drag the red line in the display.
Limiting character: Clean, Glue, Punch, Dynamic, Dense, Loud, Bus or Safe.
In the Advanced panel. Holds the level at a threshold under the ceiling with a slow attack, and the ceiling catches the rest. Off by default.
Under Levelling: the level that is held, and how much of a transient passes before the level is held.
Limits inter-sample peaks as well as sample peaks.
Off or a higher factor for the limiter.
Fast, Slow, Slow down, Infinite or Off for the level display.
Shows a loudness meter with a target.
tips: The editor shows the latency in samples in the top left corner.
Turn true-peak limiting on when the file will be converted to a lossy format.
Open the knob panel at the lower left of the display, then Advanced, to reach Levelling. Switching it off and on again keeps the threshold you set.

name: Atrium
desc: Room and chamber reverb with separate early and late sections, bass and high decay multipliers, and twelve room types.

wiki.intro: Atrium is a room and chamber reverb with separate early and late sections and a three-band decay. Six faders set the overall reverb, the Early and Late tabs switch the dials on the right between the two sections, and the Reverb mode menu picks one of twelve room types.
controls: Balance between the dry signal and the reverb.
How long the reverb takes to die away.
Removes the reverb's lows below this frequency.
Removes the reverb's highs above this frequency.
Balance between the early reflections, which sound close, and the tail, which sounds far.
Early tab: length of the early reflections. Late tab: size of the tail's space.
How much the left and right sides of that section feed each other.
Speed and amount of the modulation of that section.
Early tab. How much of the early reflections feed the tail.
Early tab. Density of the reflections: low is grainy, high is smooth.
Early tab. Feeds the early reflections back for a bigger, longer space.
Late tab. Decay of the lows relative to the mids (above 1 is longer) and the frequency where the lows end.
Late tab. Decay of the highs relative to the mids (below 1 is shorter) and the frequency where the highs start.
The kind of space: Large Room, Medium Room, Bright Room, Large Chamber, Dark Room, Dark Chamber, Dark Space, Deep Space, Mirror Space, Vast Space, Distant Space or Dense Room.

Measured is the reverb engine of 0.1.27: the decay is set per octave band, a tone corrector follows the reverb network and a diffusion network shapes the onset. It uses less CPU than Classic. New instances start on Measured. Projects and presets saved before 0.1.27 load on Classic and sound as before.
tips: The status line under the editor describes the chosen reverb mode.
Size, Cross, Mod rate and Mod depth exist once per section, so check which tab is open before turning them.

name: Audio Effect Rack
desc: Ableton Live-style rack in a mixer slot. Parallel chains of effects share the input and are summed, with chain-select zones, chain volume and pan, and 16 macros.

wiki.intro: Audio Effect Rack is a mixer slot effect built on Patcher in rack mode. Every chain gets the same input and the outputs of the chains are summed, with delay compensation between them. Add it from the mixer slot's plugin picker as Audio Effect Rack, or group existing slots into one. Audio Effect Racks in Ableton Live sets (.als) open as racks, and racks are written back when you export a Live set.
controls: One row per chain with its name, volume, pan, an on switch and S for solo. The chain menu has Add chain, Rename, Duplicate, Delete, Move up and Move down.
The effects of the selected chain. The add menu offers Effects, Plugin effects and Racks, so racks can be nested.
Show or hide the chain-select zone editor. An Audio Effect Rack has no key or velocity zones.
Drag a bar or its ends to set the chain's zone, 0 to 127. The upper strip sets the fades, which scale the chain's output.
The value the zones are compared with. A macro can drive it.
Up to 16 knobs, each with a name plate and a value. + and - show more or fewer: 1, 2, 4 and so on up to 16.

Map mode. Each macro gets a Map button that opens a menu of the chains, their devices and parameters, Chain Volume, Chain Pan and Chain Selector. The mapping list shows Macro, Path, Name, Min and Max, with Invert Range and Delete.
Gives every mapped macro a random value. A macro's menu has Exclude Macro from Randomization.
New stores the macro values. A variation has Launch, Overwrite, Rename, Duplicate and Delete.

In the mixer slot menu: moves the effect into a new rack with one chain. Group all into Audio Effect Rack moves the whole chain of slots. The sound stays the same and automation of the moved parameters drives the rack's macros.
In the mixer slot menu of a rack with one chain: puts its devices back into the slots.
tips: Outside a zone that ends without a fade the chain's input closes, so its tails ring out.

From a Live set a rack keeps its chains, zones, chain volume and pan, macros, variations and nested racks. Third-party plugins in the chains are kept. Live's own devices are dropped and listed in the import report.
A macro mapping on a VST3 plugin parameter in a Live set is not kept. On export, LYNX SHARE built-in effects in a chain are not written; only VST2 and VST3 plugins and nested racks are.
Ungroup is not available for a rack with more than one chain.

name: Auto-pan
desc: Moves a sound between left and right from a tempo-synced LFO or a step pattern. It can also output only a control signal.

wiki.intro: Auto-pan moves a track between left and right. The movement comes from one of three sources: FL LFO, a triangle wave locked to the song position, LFO, a free rate in Hz, or Rhythm steps, a number of steps on the beat grid. A strip in the Pan section shows the current position.
controls: Centre position of the pan movement.
How far the sound swings to each side. The knob is bipolar, and negative values reverse the direction.
FL LFO source. Bends the triangle wave. In the centre it has no effect.
LFO and Rhythm steps sources. From a hard jump between positions to a soft glide.
Chooses the source of the movement. The Rate section shows the controls of the chosen source.
FL LFO source. Length of one cycle in beats, up to 64.
FL LFO source. Shifts the start of the cycle.
LFO source. Free rate from 0.01 Hz to 10 Hz.
Rhythm steps source. 2 to 8 pan positions, each lasting a note value from 1/1 to 1/32.
LFO and Rhythm steps sources. Back and forth, left to right, or right to left.
FL LFO source. Pans with FL Studio's pan law, which folds the far side into the near side, instead of only turning the far side down.
Leaves the audio untouched and provides the movement as a live automation source.
Gain before and after the panner, -24 dB to +24 dB each.
Analog adds an asymmetric soft saturation stage.
Switches to a second panner model with its own panel: Offset, Width, Smoothing, a Rate in Hz or Beats, pattern keys, Phase, Amount and a Tweak page.
tips: Use Control only when the pan movement should drive another parameter instead of panning the audio.
With the FL LFO source the movement follows the song position, so it lands on the same place of the bar on every playback.

name: Chorus
desc: Simple chorus with rate, depth, feedback and mix, and a display of the two modulation waves for the left and right channels.

wiki.intro: Chorus thickens a sound by mixing it with a slightly delayed, modulated copy. It is added to an insert slot and used on guitars, synths, pads and vocals.
controls: Speed of the modulation in hertz.
Amount of delay modulation in milliseconds.
Amount of the output fed back into the chorus.
tips: The display shows the left and right modulation waves moving against each other.
Keep Feedback at zero for a plain chorus and raise it for a flanger-like colour.

name: Compressor
desc: Compressor with threshold, ratio, attack, release, make-up gain and mix. It has a Classic voicing with a clean or FET law, a Vintage voicing and a switchable limiter.

wiki.intro: Compressor reduces the level of loud parts of a track. It is added to an insert slot and used to even out vocals, drums and basses. It has a Classic and a Vintage voicing. Classic runs clean or with a FET law that has a soft knee and a release that depends on the programme. The LYNX and RComp switch selects the ranges of the controls.
controls: How strongly signals above the threshold are reduced.
Dry and wet balance for parallel compression.
Shown with Classic. Clean is the compressor as it was. FET adds a 5 dB knee and a programme-dependent release. Clean is the default.
ARC / Manual, Electro / Opto, Warm / Smooth
Shown with Vintage: the release mode, the release curve and the character.
Shown with Vintage: the static curve. Projects saved with the old curve keep it until you switch.
Selects the ranges of the ratio, gain, attack and release controls.
tips: Use Mix below 100 percent to blend in the uncompressed signal.
The In and Out meters show the level before and after, the centre meter shows the gain change.
FET is off in existing projects, so they sound as before.

name: Control Surface
desc: A panel you build from knobs, sliders, buttons, check boxes and XY pads. Each control is an output that other parameters can be linked to.

wiki.intro: Control Surface makes no sound. It is a panel of controls that you place on an insert slot, and each control becomes a control output. You link any parameter to such an output with the link to internal controller command, and the outputs can be automated like effect parameters.
controls: Adds a knob, slider, button, check box or XY pad to the panel.
Edit mode: drag a control to move it, right-click it to rename it, resize it or delete it.
Gives a control a new name.
Sets the size of a control.
Removes a control and keeps the outputs of the others in place.
Menu item that keeps a control as a control output only, without sending MIDI.
tips: An XY pad counts as two outputs.
A new panel starts with two knobs.

name: Crest Compressor
desc: Style compressor with eleven styles, knee, range, look-ahead, a three-band side-chain EQ, character, oversampling and a live gain-reduction graph.

wiki.intro: Crest Compressor is a compressor for insert slots, fitted to black-box measurements of a widely used style compressor. The display shows the input level, the gain reduction and the threshold line, and you pick one of eleven styles.
controls: Clean, Allround, Punch, Upward, Two-way, Vari-mu, Classic, Opto, Vocal, Bus or Pumping.
Level above which compression starts. Drag the dashed line in the display.
Softness of the transition at the threshold.
Limits how much gain change is allowed.
Release time, with an auto option.
Off, or a character with Post or Pre placement.
Opens the side-chain section with a three-band EQ, level and listen.
tips: Look-ahead adds latency, so the plugin reports it to the host.
Use the side-chain EQ to keep low frequencies from triggering the compressor.

name: Crossover
desc: A high-pass and a low-pass filter in one effect, each with its own cutoff and slope in decibels per octave, and a response display.

wiki.intro: Crossover combines a high-pass and a low-pass section in one insert effect. It is used to cut unwanted low or high frequencies, or to limit a signal to a band before further processing.
controls: Switches the high-pass section on and off.
Switches the low-pass section on and off.
tips: The graph shows the combined response from minus 12 to plus 12 dB.
Set both sections to isolate a band.

name: Delay
desc: Simple echo with time, feedback, damping, mix and a ping-pong switch. Time can follow the song tempo, and the display shows the repeats.

wiki.intro: Delay repeats the signal after a set time. Add it to an insert slot for slapback, echoes or ping-pong effects. The display plots the repeats as they fade.
controls: Delay time, as a note value such as 1/8 dotted or in milliseconds.
How much of the delayed signal returns to the input.
Alternates the repeats between the left and right channels.
tips: Pick a note value for Time to keep the echoes in time with the song.
Raise Damping so the repeats sit behind the dry sound.

name: Distortion
desc: Drive-based distortion with tone, mix and output level, and a graph of the input to output curve.

wiki.intro: Distortion adds harmonics by pushing the signal into a saturating curve. It is added to an insert slot for guitars, drums, synths or to add edge to a bus. The graph on the left shows the curve in use.
controls: Amount of gain into the curve, shown in decibels.
Tone filter, shown as a frequency in hertz.
tips: Lower Mix to keep the original transients with the distortion underneath.
Lower Output after raising Drive, as the level rises with the drive.

name: Distructor
desc: Chain of up to four modules, distortion, filter, chorus or amp and cabinet, each with in, mix and out controls, followed by a soft clipper.

wiki.intro: Distructor is a chain of four module slots for an insert. The modules are not built in the editor: they come from an imported FL Studio Distructor preset or project. The amp and cabinet impulses are read from your own FL Studio installation, so those modules need it.
controls: Each module is a distortion, filter, chorus or amp and cabinet.
Dry and wet balance of the module.
Switches on the final soft clipper.
tips: An empty module slot reads 'Modules come from an FL Studio Distructor preset or project'.
The four knob sets are automatable like other effect parameters.

name: Echoform
desc: Multi-mode echo with tape, bucket brigade, analog, digital, shifter, pitch and reverse characters, tempo sync, wow and flutter, and feedback past 100 percent.

wiki.intro: Echoform is an echo with twelve styles and five echo layouts. The Main page has three sections: Echo for time, feedback and filters, Tap tempo for groove and the echo mode, and Style for saturation, levels and the style menus. The Tweak page holds the remaining controls.
controls: Balance between the dry signal and the echoes.
Delay time. The Time, Note, Dot and Trip keys set it in milliseconds or as a straight, dotted or triplet note value. In Dual and Ping-pong modes it is the left time.
How much of the output is fed back. The range goes to 200 percent, and the loop is soft limited so it stays bounded.
Remove the echoes' lows below 10 Hz to 2 kHz and their highs above 200 Hz to 20 kHz.
Single mode. Offsets the two sides in time for width. In the other modes the same place holds Ratio, Spacing or Delay R.
Snaps the delay times to a prime number of samples.
Tap the key to set the left echo time. The read-out shows the tempo.
Moves the odd repeats early or late by up to 25 percent of the echo time. The scale runs from Shuffle to Swing.
Moves the whole echo train early (Rushin) or late (Draggin) by up to 25 percent of the echo time.
Echo layout: Single, Ratio, Quad (four taps), Dual or Ping-pong.
Level into the echoes only, -24 dB to +24 dB. The dry signal is not touched.
Level of the echoes, -18 dB to +18 dB.
Wear of the machine the style imitates: noise and darkening.
The machine the echo imitates: Tape, Lo-Fi, Hi-Fi tape, Bucket brigade, Analog, Digital, Clean, Phaser, Shifter, Pitch, Reverse or Detune.
Selects a measured tape loop voicing: Off, Ping-pong tape, Studio tape or Studio tape hot.

Tweak page. Measured runs the measured tape stage in the Tape style when the Tape menu is Off: the tone of the output and of the loop, the tape's hiss and the lag of the wow. It costs a little more CPU. New instances start on Measured. Projects and presets saved before 0.1.27 load on Classic and sound as before.
Tweak page. The modulation swings the echo time by a fraction of itself, up to 50 percent at full depth, on both sides together, like a clocked delay line. Off by default.
tips: The status line under the editor describes the chosen style.

The Tweak page adds Width, Diffusion, the style's modulation (Wow and Flutter for tape), Ducking, Accent, X-feed and Balance, plus Freeze, a Rhythm mode with its own tap editor and a choice between the project tempo and the echo's own BPM.
Feedback above 100 percent keeps building, so raise it slowly.

name: Edison
desc: Audio editor in a mixer slot, as in FL Studio: it records the slot's input, passes it on and can play its audio back in time with the song. Its window is the LYNX SHARE audio editor.

wiki.intro: Edison is an audio editor that sits in a mixer slot. It passes the slot's input through unchanged, records that input while Record is on, and adds its own playback to the output. Several Edison slots can be on one track. Add it from the slot's plugin list, or use the mixer track menu: Open audio editor (Ctrl+E) puts it in the first empty slot, and Open audio editor and record (Shift+E) also arms it with Record mode On play, 5 min, Append off and Slave on. Its window is the LYNX SHARE audio editor, with the slot's recording controls added. Recording goes on while the window is closed. Edison slots in .flp projects open as Edison, with their settings and audio.
controls: Records the slot's input, depending on the mode. Key R.
Now, On input, Input, On play

The record mode. Now starts at once. On input starts when the input goes above the noise threshold and keeps 0.1 s from before. Input records only while the input is heard and pauses after 1 s of silence. On play records while the song plays and adds a Song jump marker each time the song position jumps, so a looped song gives one take with a marker per pass. New slots start on On input.
Forever, 1, 3, 5, 10, 30 or 60 min. New slots start at 30 min.
On: a new take goes after the audio already there. Off: it replaces it. On by default.
Slave playback to host: while the song plays, the audio plays at the song time. Key H. The Record menu also has Ignore own selection.
The slot's input is not passed on, only Edison's playback. Key I.
Snap to the grid, to regions, to samples or to zero crossings, keys 1 to 4.
Drag the sample or the selection as a WAV onto the Playlist or the Channel Rack. Right-click copies it to the editor's clipboard.
Send to the Playlist as an audio clip, to the selected channel or to a new Sampler channel.
In a region's menu: the note linked to the region. Regions › Assign trigger notes to all... and Assign all to set them for every region.
tips: The audio is kept as a WAV file in the project's recordings folder, not inside the project file.
Tools › Acquire noise threshold, on a selection of background noise only, sets the level that On input and Input listen for.
Tools › Macros › Remove all Edison instances removes every Edison slot of the project.
A slot made in LYNX SHARE is not written into a .flp on export. An Edison slot that came from a .flp and was not edited keeps FL Studio's data.
Trigger notes are stored with the regions and read by audio scripts. Playing a region from its note is not done yet.

name: Effector
desc: Twelve effect types on one XY pad, each with two parameters, an LFO that follows the song tempo, and input and output gain.

wiki.intro: Effector has twelve effect types behind one XY pad. One type is active at a time. X and Y set its two parameters, and an LFO synced to the project tempo can move them. It loads the settings of the FL Studio Effector from an imported .flp project.
controls: Distort, Lo-fi, Flanger, Phaser, Filter, Delay, Reverb, Stereo, Trans, Grain, Vox or Ring.
The two parameters of the chosen type. Their meaning changes with the type.
Sets X and Y together by dragging.
Amount of the effect in the output.
Length of one LFO cycle in beats, from eight beats to an eighth of a beat. The Delay type takes its echo time from this setting and Grain its repeat length.
How far the LFO moves X and Y. Both are bipolar.
Shortens the LFO cycle set by the rate buttons.
tips: Distort: X is the amount, Y the tone. Lo-fi: X holds samples longer, Y reduces the bit depth. Flanger and Phaser: X is the sweep position, Y the feedback.

Filter: X is a low-pass left of centre and a high-pass right of centre, Y the resonance. Delay: X is the feedback, Y darkens the echoes below centre and cuts their lows above it. Reverb: X is the decay, Y the high damping.

Stereo: X is the pan position, Y how much of it becomes a level difference. Trans: X is the release time and Y the drop level of a gate that repeats every LFO cycle. Vox: X picks the vowel, Y scales the formant frequencies. Ring: X is the carrier frequency, from 32 Hz to about 13.3 kHz.
Grain repeats a slice of the audio every LFO cycle and does not use X or Y.

name: Ember Saturator
desc: Saturator with tube, tape, transistor and fuzz styles, tone tilt, auto gain and oversampling, which can split the signal into up to four bands with their own style and drive.

wiki.intro: Ember Saturator is an effect slot plugin for adding harmonics and grit. Use it on single tracks, buses or the master. It runs as one band or as up to four Linkwitz-Riley bands, each with its own style and drive.
controls: Amount of saturation applied to the band.
Saturation curve: tube (asymmetric, even harmonics), tape (odd harmonics), transistor or fuzz, plus the other entries of the style menu.
Number of bands, up to four.
Slope of the band splits: 12, 24 or 48 dB per octave.
Blend of the band's processed signal.
Blend of the whole plugin with the unprocessed signal.
Tilts the balance between low and high frequencies.
High-pass filter on the processed signal.
Low-pass filter on the processed signal.
Compensates the level change caused by the drive.
tips: Start with one band and the tube style, then switch to more bands when the low end distorts more than you want.
Keep Auto gain on while setting Drive, so you compare processed and dry at a similar level.

name: Emphasis
desc: Limiter-style dynamics effect with an emphasis amount, ceiling, envelope and hardness controls, true peak and mid/side modes, oversampling and a level-matching option.

wiki.intro: Emphasis is a mastering limiter. The signal passes an input gain, the limiter with its mode, envelope and hardness settings, and a final limiter that holds the output to the ceiling. It loads the settings of the FL Studio Emphasis from an imported .flp project and reports its latency for delay compensation.
controls: Gain before the limiter, 0 dB to +24 dB.
Amount, 0 to 100 percent. It sets the attack shape, release shape and knee amount of the limiter.
Highest output level, up to 0 dB. A new instance is at -0.2 dB.
Order of the envelope, 1 to 4: the number of attack and release stages in series.
0 to 9. Each step up halves the limiter's time constant.
0 to 100 percent. At 100 percent both channels are controlled by the louder one.
Processes left and right (L/R) or mid and side (M/S).
The final limiter detects peaks on a 4 times oversampled signal instead of the sample values.
Scales the output to the level of the input, by a factor of 2 at most.
Outputs the delayed dry signal minus the processed signal.
Fixes the release time at 5 ms.
A 5 Hz high-pass on the input.
Changes the meter only, not the audio.
Crossfades to the dry signal, which keeps the plugin's latency.
tips: Delta plays what the limiter removes.
Turn on Level matching to compare the processed and bypassed signal at a similar level.

name: Emphasizer
desc: Effect with input gain, an emphasis amount, output level, soft clipping and level matching, and a 2 ms look-ahead that is reported for delay compensation.

wiki.intro: Emphasizer is a look-ahead limiter with one main knob. The input gain feeds a peak detector, the gain reduction is applied to the signal delayed by 2 ms, and the result is clipped and sent to the output gain. It loads the settings of the FL Studio Emphasizer from an imported .flp project and reports the 2 ms look-ahead for delay compensation.
controls: Gain before the limiter, 0 dB to +24 dB.
Amount, 0 to 100 percent. It scales the level that the peak detector sees.
Replaces the hard clip at full scale after the limiter with a soft clip that starts below it.
Divides the output by the input gain, so raising Input gain does not raise the level.
Crossfades to the delayed dry signal instead of switching hard.
tips: With Level matching on, Input gain can be raised to drive the limiter harder without the output getting louder by the same amount.
The meter strip on the right shows the levels.

name: Epoch Verb
desc: Reverb with 22 algorithms covering halls, plates, rooms, chorused and random spaces and gated tails, in three colours of converter character.

wiki.intro: Epoch Verb is a reverb effect slot plugin. It has 22 algorithms and three colours (1970s, 1980s and Now). Use it for halls, plates and rooms on sends or inserts.
controls: Length of the tail, 0.2 to 70 seconds.
High frequency and bass frequency crossover points, the high shelf gain and the bass multiplier.

Measured is the reverb engine of 0.1.27: the decay is set per octave band, a tone corrector follows the reverb network and a diffusion network shapes the onset. It uses less CPU than Classic. New instances start on Measured. Projects and presets saved before 0.1.27 load on Classic and sound as before.
tips: Low cut is useful to keep the reverb out of the low end of a mix.
The hint line under the editor describes the selected mode.

name: EQ
desc: Simple three-band equaliser with low and high bands, a mid band with adjustable frequency, an output level and a live curve display.

wiki.intro: EQ is a basic effect slot plugin for quick tone corrections. It has a low band, a mid band with a movable centre frequency and a high band, with the resulting curve drawn above the knobs.
controls: Centre frequency of the mid band.
tips: For more bands, a spectrum and dynamic bands, use Facet EQ.

name: EQUO
desc: Graphic equaliser with 31 third-octave bands and eight banks, with band shift, mix and morph, per-band volume, pan and send.

wiki.intro: EQUO is an effect slot plugin built around 31 third-octave band passes. It opens the settings of an FL Studio EQUO plugin when a .flp project is imported. It holds eight banks plus a master bank, and each band has its own volume, pan and send.
controls: Selects the master bank or one of the eight banks.
Selects which value the band sliders edit.
Sends the bands only to the chosen insert.
Adds the band signals instead of replacing the input.
Insert that receives the band sends.
tips: Band sends go to the insert chosen in the Send box.

name: Facet EQ
desc: Eight-band equaliser with bells, shelves, notches and cuts up to 96 dB per octave, a spectrum display, dynamic bands and tone matching against another track.

wiki.intro: Facet EQ is a precision equaliser for effect slots. It has eight bands with a live spectrum drawn behind the curve. Use it for surgical cuts, broad tone shaping and mastering corrections.
controls: Bell, shelves, cuts of 6 to 96 dB per octave, notch, band pass and tilt.
Zero latency, natural phase or linear phase. The latency is compensated.
Shows the spectrum before, after or before and after the EQ.
Input or sidechain track, for the dynamic bands.
Matches the tone of the source to a target.
tips: Each band can work dynamically, with threshold, range, attack and release.
Band solo helps to find a problem frequency.

name: Filter
desc: State-variable filter with low-pass, high-pass and band-pass modes at 12 dB per octave, with cutoff, resonance, mix and a live response curve.

wiki.intro: Filter is a simple effect slot plugin. It is a 12 dB per octave state-variable filter with a response curve drawn above the controls.
controls: Blend of filtered and dry signal.
tips: Automate Cutoff for sweeps.

name: Foil Plate
desc: Bright plate reverb that speaks at once, with a frequency-dependent decay, twelve plate types, low and high EQ shelves and modulation.

wiki.intro: Foil Plate is a plate reverb effect slot plugin. It has twelve plate types and a decay that depends on frequency. Use it on snares, vocals and busses.
controls: Length of the tail, 0.5 to 30 seconds.
The plate type, each with its own brightness, density and decay.

Measured is the reverb engine of 0.1.27: the decay is set per octave band, a tone corrector follows the reverb network and a diffusion network shapes the onset. It uses less CPU than Classic. New instances start on Measured. Projects and presets saved before 0.1.27 load on Classic and sound as before.
tips: The Full and Plate buttons switch between the full panel and a panel with one knob.

name: Formula Controller
desc: Controller that outputs a value from 0 to 1 calculated by a formula of three knobs and the song position, to link to any parameter.

wiki.intro: Formula Controller makes no sound. It outputs a value between 0 and 1 that is the result of a formula, and you link that output to any parameter. It opens the settings of an FL Studio Fruity Formula Controller when a .flp project is imported.
controls: Three knobs you can use in the formula.
The formula. SongTime is the song position in quarter notes.
Compiles the formula. Pressing Enter does the same.
A menu of ready formulas such as sine, triangle, saw and square LFOs, sample and hold, random and steps.
tips: The default formula a+b+c outputs the sum of the three knobs.
Right-click a parameter knob and choose Link to internal controller to use the output.

name: Frequency Shifter
desc: Moves every frequency of the signal by a fixed amount of hertz in shifter, high quality shifter or ring modulator mode, with feedback and stereo phase controls.

wiki.intro: Frequency Shifter is an effect slot plugin that moves all frequencies up or down by the same number of hertz, which makes harmonic sounds inharmonic. It opens the settings of an FL Studio Frequency Shifter plugin when a .flp project is imported. Its latency is compensated.
controls: Shifter HQ, Shifter or Ring modulator.
Shape control for the left channel.
Shape control for the right channel.
Start phase of the left channel.
Phase offset between left and right.
Feeds the output back to the input.
tips: The side chain input of the ring modulator is not routed.

name: Frequency shifter
desc: Simple frequency shifter that moves all frequencies up or down by a number of hertz, with mix and stereo controls and a spectrum display.

wiki.intro: Frequency shifter is a small effect slot plugin that shifts all frequencies of the signal by the same number of hertz, up or down. It has a spectrum display above its three knobs.
tips: Small shifts of a few hertz give a slow beating, large ones make the sound inharmonic.

name: Frequency Splitter
desc: Splits the signal into two or three frequency bands with crossover slopes from 6 to 96 dB per octave and sends each band to its own insert.

wiki.intro: Frequency Splitter divides the signal into low, mid and high bands. It opens the settings of an FL Studio Frequency Splitter when a .flp project is imported. The main output is the sum of the bands, and each band can also be sent to another insert.
controls: Slope of each crossover, 6 to 96 dB per octave.
Crossover frequency, low to mid and mid to high.
Switches between two and three bands.
Level, mute and solo of each band in the main output.
Level, mute and solo of each band sent to its insert, and an Out selector.
FFT mode, which adds latency that is compensated.
Fade setting of the FFT mode.
tips: In a Patcher, the bands go to the buses connected to them.

name: Fret Channel
desc: Channel strip for guitar and bass with phase correction, a three-band equaliser with filters, a compressor and a drive section with guitar and bass amp models.

wiki.intro: Fret Channel is a channel strip for guitar and bass for effect slots. From the left, it has input, phase correction, equaliser, compressor, drive and output sections. It has a latency of 20 ms plus the amp's oversampler, which is compensated.
controls: Gain of plus or minus 24 dB.
Align to side chain, left or right, with a delay of plus or minus 20 ms, polarity and an all-pass of first or second order with frequency and Q.
Low and high shelves, mid bell with frequency from 0.5 to 7 kHz, gains of plus or minus 12 dB, and a low-pass from 3 to 20 kHz.
Places the equaliser before or after the compressor.
Threshold from minus 36 to 0 dB, mode from fastest to slowest, mix and auto gain.
Guitar amp or bass amp model with pre-amp, drive from 0 to 11 and mix.
Listens to the signal in mono.
tips: Auto listen solos the equaliser band while you turn its knob.

name: Fruity 7 Band EQ
desc: Seven fixed-frequency bands with one gain fader each: a low shelf, five peaking bands and a high shelf, for quick tone shaping on a mixer insert.

wiki.intro: A graphic-style equaliser with seven faders at fixed centre frequencies. Add it to a mixer insert for broad tone shaping. It opens the settings of the matching effect from an imported FL Studio project.
tips: Each fader covers plus or minus 18 dB; the middle position is 0 dB.
The filters are always designed for 44.1 kHz, whatever the project rate.

name: Fruity Balance
desc: A simple stereo balance control with a volume knob and level meters, for shifting a signal between left and right or trimming its level.

wiki.intro: A minimal utility for the mixer. It moves the stereo balance toward the left or right channel and sets the output volume. It reads the settings of the matching effect from an imported FL Studio project.
controls: Moves the signal between the left and right channels; the centre position leaves it as is.
Show the level of the left and right channels.
tips: Use it to correct a lopsided recording or to trim the level at the end of an insert chain.

name: Fruity Bass Boost
desc: Adds low frequencies with a resonant low-pass whose output is mixed back into the dry signal. Two controls: frequency and amount.

wiki.intro: A one-purpose bass enhancer for mixer inserts. A resonant two-pole low-pass is added to the dry signal, so the low end gets heavier without a full equaliser. It opens the settings of the matching effect from an imported FL Studio project.
controls: Frequency of the boost, 20 to 100 Hz.
How much of the low-passed signal is added.
Graph of the resulting frequency response.
tips: The frequency range stays in the sub-bass region, so it suits kicks and bass lines.
A graph under the knobs shows the resulting curve.

name: Fruity Big Clock
desc: A silent display that shows the song position in large digits. It does not process audio and offers three time formats.

wiki.intro: A display plugin that makes no sound. It shows the song position in big digits, handy when recording or working from a distance. It opens the settings of the matching effect from an imported FL Studio project.
controls: Chooses the time format; right-click the clock to change it.
Position as bars, beats and ticks.
Position as bars, steps and ticks.
tips: The digits use the biggest size that fits the window, so resize it to taste.

name: Fruity Blood Overdrive
desc: An overdrive with a pre filter, a colour control, a large pre-amp knob with an x100 switch, and a post filter and gain.

wiki.intro: An overdrive effect for mixer inserts. The signal passes a pre band filter, is driven by the pre-amp, then shaped by a post filter and gain. It opens the settings of the matching effect from an imported FL Studio project.
controls: Multiplies the range of the pre-amp.
tips: Lower Post gain as Pre amp goes up to keep the level steady.

name: Fruity Center
desc: Removes DC offset with a two-pole high-pass filter. A single On and Off switch, for cleaning a signal before further processing.

wiki.intro: A tiny utility for mixer inserts. It runs a DC-removing high-pass filter that re-centres a waveform around zero. It opens the settings of the matching effect from an imported FL Studio project.
tips: Place it early in a chain when a source has a constant offset, before compressors or limiters.

name: Fruity Chorus
desc: A chorus with three LFOs, each with its own frequency and waveform, plus stereo spread and a crossover that decides which part is chorused.

wiki.intro: A modulated-delay chorus for mixer inserts. Three LFOs move the delay time, which thickens the sound and widens it in stereo. It opens the settings of the matching effect from an imported FL Studio project.
controls: How far the LFOs move the delay.
Selects which part of the spectrum is chorused.
tips: Turn on Wet only when the effect is on a send.

name: Fruity Compressor
desc: A compressor with threshold, ratio, gain, attack, release and a hard or soft type, and support for a sidechain input.

wiki.intro: A straightforward compressor for mixer inserts. It reduces the level of signals above the threshold and can follow a sidechain. It opens the settings of the matching effect from an imported FL Studio project.
controls: Level above which compression starts, shown in dB.
Amount of reduction above the threshold.
Time the compressor takes to react, in ms.
Time it takes to recover, in ms.
Compression type; Hard is shown as the default.
tips: Right-click a compressor slot in the mixer to pick a sidechain source.

name: Fruity Convolver
desc: A convolution effect that applies an impulse response to the signal, with dry and wet levels, stereo separation, delay, stretch and an EQ curve.

wiki.intro: Fruity Convolver convolves the signal with an impulse response. The impulse response comes from an imported FL Studio project: it is either embedded in the plugin's state or a file of your own FL Studio installation, which is read at import and then kept in the project. A new instance has no impulse response, shows No impulse response and passes the dry signal only.
controls: Stereo separation of the input before the convolution, from separated to merged.
Stereo separation of the convolved signal.
Blends the impulse response with its own self-convolution.
Resamples the impulse response, from half speed to double speed.
Amount of the EQ applied to the impulse response.
Scales the impulse response by the level of its loudest 300 ms.
The Impulse page shows the waveform with its rate, format and length. The Equalizer page draws and edits the EQ curve.
tips: Dry, Wet and the two separation knobs are the plugin's four automatable controls. The other knobs are part of the plugin state.
FL Studio's sample editor tools for the impulse response are not reproduced.

name: Fruity Delay 2
desc: A feedback delay with input pan and volume, dry level, time and stereo offset, plus a feedback section with three modes and a cutoff.

wiki.intro: A compact stereo delay for mixer inserts. The Feedback section offers normal, inverted and ping-pong modes. It opens the settings of the matching effect from an imported FL Studio project.
controls: Pans the input into the delay.
tips: Ping-pong mode bounces the repeats between left and right.

name: Fruity Delay 3
desc: A stereo delay with tempo sync, modulation, diffusion, a filtered feedback path and feedback distortion with sample rate and bit reduction.

wiki.intro: A full-featured delay for mixer inserts, with sections for delay time, model, feedback, modulation, diffusion and feedback distortion. It opens the settings of the matching effect from an imported FL Studio project.
controls: Delay time; follows the song tempo when Tempo sync is on.
Locks the delay time to the tempo.
Keeps the pitch while the time changes.
Mono, Stereo, Ping pong or Off.
Limit or Sat for the feedback distortion.
tips: The feedback filter can be low-pass, high-pass or band-pass.
Sample rate and bit reduction act inside the feedback loop.

name: Fruity Delay Bank
desc: A bank of up to eight delay lines with per-line input, filter, feedback, grain and output sections, plus global dry, wet, input and feedback levels.

wiki.intro: Fruity Delay Bank has eight delay banks. Each bank has an input stage, a filter, a delay line with a feedback path and its own feedback filter, a stepped gain pattern and an output stage, and can send into the next bank. It loads the settings of the FL Studio plugin from an imported .flp project.
controls: The switches on top turn each bank on. The tabs choose the bank shown.
Global levels: the dry signal, the output of the banks, the input into the banks and the feedback of all banks.
Pan and level of the signal entering the bank.
Type (off, low pass, band pass, notch, high pass, low shelf, peaking or high shelf), 1 to 3 sections, Gain, Cut and Res. Post places it after the delay instead of before.
Off for no delay, Norm, Inv for swapped outputs, or P.pong for ping-pong feedback.
Delay time. T syncs it to the tempo.
Time offset between the left and right delay.
Stereo matrix, pan and level of the feedback path.
A second filter with the same types, inside the feedback path.
A stepped gain pattern on the delay. Div is the number of steps per delay time (0 is off) and Sh the shape of the steps.
Amount of this bank sent into the next bank. Bank 8 has no Next.
Pan and level of the bank in the output.
tips: Select a bank with the numbered tabs to edit it. The switches above the tabs show which banks are on.

name: Fruity Delay
desc: The original simple delay: a sixteenth-note delay line with input, feedback and cutoff, a tempo setting, a step count and three stereo modes.

wiki.intro: A basic delay for mixer inserts. The delay line is set in sixteenth notes and has a low-pass in the feedback loop. The dry signal always passes at unity. It opens the settings of the matching effect from an imported FL Studio project.
controls: Low-pass cutoff in the feedback loop.
Host follows the song tempo; otherwise a fixed tempo of 60 to 280 BPM.
tips: Leave Tempo on Host to keep the echoes in time with the song.

name: Fruity Fast Dist
desc: A quick distortion with pre-amp, threshold, mix and post gain, two types (A and B) and a transfer curve display.

wiki.intro: A simple distortion for mixer inserts. The signal is boosted, clipped at the threshold and mixed with the dry signal. A graph shows the transfer curve. It opens the settings of the matching effect from an imported FL Studio project.
controls: Level at which the signal is clipped.
Switches between types A and B.
Balance of dry and distorted signal.
tips: Lower Post as Pre goes up to keep the level steady.

name: Fruity Fast LP
desc: A resonant low-pass filter with just two controls, cutoff and resonance. Cheap to run and handy for darkening a track or sweeping a filter.

name: Fruity Filter
desc: A state-variable filter with separate low-pass, band-pass and high-pass levels that you can mix freely, plus resonance and an optional second pass.

wiki.intro: Fruity Filter is a state-variable filter for mixer insert slots. Instead of choosing one filter type, you set the level of the low-pass, band-pass and high-pass outputs and they are mixed together. It suits sweeps and simple tone shaping.
controls: Centre of the filter. Fully open by default.
Level of the band-pass output. Off by default.
Runs the filter twice in series for a steeper slope.
Removes DC offset from the output.
tips: Raise Low pass and High pass together with Band pass at zero for a notch-like response.
The filter coefficient does not depend on the project sample rate.

name: Fruity Flanger
desc: A tape-style flanger with an LFO-swept delay line, damped feedback, phase offset between the sides and separate dry and wet levels.

wiki.intro: Fruity Flanger is a delay-line flanger for mixer insert slots. A short delay is swept by an LFO and mixed with the dry signal, with feedback for the classic jet sound. Use it on guitars, synths, drums or whole mixes.
controls: Base delay time of the line.
How far the LFO sweeps the delay.
Phase offset of the LFO between the two sides.
Inverts the polarity of the feedback.
Inverts the polarity of the effect signal.
Crossfeed between the left and right sides.
tips: Invert feed changes the character of the comb filtering a lot, try both settings.
Raising Damp makes the repeats darker.

name: Fruity Flangus
desc: A multi-voice flanger and chorus hybrid with adjustable voice order, depth, speed and delay, plus spread and cross controls for the stereo image.

wiki.intro: Fruity Flangus is a multi-voice modulated delay. Each side gets as many delay voices as the Order setting, each swept by its own LFO, and the voices are mixed with the dry signal. It loads the settings of the FL Studio plugin from an imported .flp project.
controls: Order, 1 to 9. The number of voices per side.
How far the LFOs sweep the delay of the voices.
Spread. How far the start phases of the voices' LFOs are offset from one another.
Bipolar. How much of each voice is sent to the opposite channel.
Bipolar. Level of the unprocessed signal.
tips: Changing Order, Depth, Speed, Delay, Spread or Cross sets the voices up again. New voices start with their LFO at phase zero.

name: Fruity Free Filter
desc: A single filter with seven types: low pass, band pass, high pass, notch, low shelf, peaking and high shelf. Frequency, Q and gain are adjustable.

wiki.intro: Fruity Free Filter is a one-band filter for mixer insert slots. You pick the type, set the frequency, then adjust the Q and the gain where the type uses it. It works as a simple filter or a single EQ band.
controls: Low pass, band pass, high pass, notch, low shelf, peaking or high shelf.
Centre or corner frequency, 10 Hz to 16 kHz.
Width or steepness of the filter.
Boost or cut of up to 18 dB, used by the shelf and peaking types.
Removes DC offset from the output.
tips: The filter is always designed for 44.1 kHz, whatever the project rate, so its response can differ slightly at other rates.
Gain only matters for the shelf and peaking types.

name: Fruity HTML NoteBook
desc: A notepad for the project that shows a page from a local HTML file or a web address. The sound passes through unchanged.

wiki.intro: Fruity HTML NoteBook does not process audio. It holds the address of a page, either a local .html file or a web address, so you can keep notes, lyrics or references next to the project. It is added like an insert effect.
controls: The local .html file or web address of the page.
Opens the address in your default browser.
tips: Local pages are shown inside the editor as formatted text, links open in your browser.
LYNX SHARE never fetches web pages itself, web addresses always open in your browser.

name: Fruity Limiter
desc: A limiter, compressor and noise gate in one effect, with gain, saturation, ceiling, envelope curves and a sidechain-capable compression section.

wiki.intro: Fruity Limiter chains a gain, a compressor with an RMS detector, a look-ahead limiter, a noise gate and a soft saturation or clip stage at the ceiling. The Limit and Comp tabs switch the middle of the panel between the limiter and the compressor controls. It loads the settings of the FL Studio plugin from an imported .flp project and reports its look-ahead for delay compensation.
controls: Loudness section. Gain at the input of the chain.
Threshold of the soft saturation at the output. At its top the saturation is off and the output is clipped at the ceiling.
Chooses which page of controls is shown. Both sections keep working.
Limit page. The level the limiter holds the output to.
Limit page. Attack and release time of the limiter.
Limit page. Length of the limiter's peak window.
The steppers under Att and Rel set the number of smoothing stages of that envelope.
Comp page. Level above which the compressor works.
Comp page. How gradually the compression starts around the threshold.
Comp page. Attack and release time of the compressor, with their own Curve stepper.
Comp page. Length of the compressor's RMS detector window.
Level below which the gate acts.
Gain the signal is turned down to while it is below the gate threshold.
How fast the gain moves to the gate gain.
tips: With a sidechain route into the insert, only the compressor's detector listens to it. The limiter and the gate always use the insert's own signal.
The limiter acts at 0.975 times the ceiling unless the option that makes it act exactly at the ceiling is on.

name: Fruity Love Philter
desc: A multi-unit filter and shaper with eight chainable units, envelopes, LFOs and an envelope follower for animated filtering.

wiki.intro: Fruity Love Philter has eight units. Each unit has an input level, a filter, a waveshaper and an output with pan and volume, and can feed the next unit. Per unit, articulators modulate pan, volume, cutoff, resonance, the low, band and high levels and the waveshaper mix from a pattern envelope, an LFO, the Mod X and Mod Y controls and an envelope follower. It loads the settings of the FL Studio plugin from an imported .flp project.
controls: The switches on top enable each unit. The tabs choose the unit shown.
Level of the plugin input into this unit. Negative values invert the phase.
The type selector picks the filter. The mode sets the number of stages in series: Off, Single, Dual, Triple, Alt dual or Alt triple. Off leaves only gain, pan and waveshaper.
Cutoff and resonance (or width) of the unit's filter.
Levels of the low-pass, band-pass and high-pass outputs of the SVF type.
Alternative resonance or width response of the filter.
Waveshaper: gain into the shaper, its mix with the unshaped signal, and a unipolar or bipolar curve.
Pan and level of the unit in the plugin output.
How much of this unit's output feeds the next unit. At zero the units run in parallel.
The tabs PAN, VOL, CUT, RES, LOW, BAND, HIGH, WS and WMIX choose the target, and PAT, LFO, MOD X, MOD Y and IEF choose the source whose curve is drawn below.
Sets Mod X and Mod Y. SMOOTH glides their changes.
Master level, master LFO level and the level into the envelope follower.
Attack and release of the envelope follower. USE1 makes it follow the output of unit 1 instead of the plugin input.
Removes DC offset from the output.
Oversampling order of the engine. It is doubled while rendering.
tips: Only the first unit is enabled in a new instance.
The output of every enabled unit is summed, so with NEXT at zero several units work as parallel filters.

name: Fruity Multiband Compressor
desc: A three-band compressor with adjustable crossovers, separate threshold, ratio, attack, release, knee and gain per band, and an optional linear-phase mode.

wiki.intro: Fruity Multiband Compressor splits the input into a low, a mid and a high band, each with its own filters, runs a peak compressor with make-up gain on each band, and sums them through an output gain and an optional soft limiter. It loads the settings of the FL Studio plugin from an imported .flp project.
controls: Type of the band filters. IIR uses 4th-order filters. FIR uses linear-phase filters with 52 samples of latency, which is reported for delay compensation.
Switches the soft limiter on the output.
Output gain after the three bands are summed.
Four knobs under the band graph: the top of the low band, the bottom and the top of the mid band, and the bottom of the high band.
Per band. A compresses the band, M mutes it and B passes it uncompressed.
Per band. Level above which the band is compressed.
Per band. How gradually the compression starts around the threshold.
Per band. Attack and release time of the band's compressor.
Per band. Make-up gain after the compressor.
tips: Each band is filtered from the input on its own, so the four crossover knobs are independent of each other.
Switching between IIR and FIR clears the filters.

name: Fruity Mute 2
desc: A mute switch for a mixer insert slot that silences the left side, the right side or both. Useful as an automatable on and off for a signal.

name: Fruity PanOMatic
desc: A pan and volume control with a built-in LFO that can modulate either one, for auto-panning and tremolo-style movement.

wiki.intro: Fruity PanOMatic sets pan and volume on a mixer insert slot and adds an LFO that can move one of them. Use it for auto-pan or tremolo, or just as a simple pan and level control.
controls: Whether the LFO moves the pan or the volume.
tips: A fresh instance starts at its settled values instead of fading in.

name: Fruity Phase Inverter
desc: Flips the polarity of the signal. In its default state only the right side is inverted.

name: Fruity Phaser
desc: A phaser with a variable number of stages, sweep range and speed, stereo phase offset, feedback and a dry and wet mix.

wiki.intro: Fruity Phaser runs the signal through a chain of 3 to 23 all-pass stages whose coefficient an LFO sweeps between a minimum and a maximum depth, with feedback from the last stage to the input. It loads the settings of the FL Studio plugin from an imported .flp project.
controls: All-pass coefficient at the bottom of the LFO.
All-pass coefficient at the top of the LFO.
Switches the LFO between a small and a large rate range. Sweep freq. then covers that range.
Phase offset of the right channel's LFO, up to half a cycle.
Amount of the last stage's output fed back to the input.
Share of the dry signal in the output. Lower values give more of the phased signal.
tips: With Stereo at zero both channels sweep together.
The value shown for Sweep freq. is the real rate in Hz and the value for Stereo is the offset in degrees.

name: Fruity Scratcher
desc: A turntable that plays a loaded sample on a platter you can spin, hold and scratch. Its sound is added to the signal passing through.

wiki.intro: Fruity Scratcher is a turntable over one sample, added to the signal in a mixer insert slot. The sample is one turn of the platter and loops. With Hold off a motor turns the platter, with Hold on the platter follows the wave position, so you can scratch by dragging it.
controls: Position of the platter within the sample.
How quickly the platter reaches its speed.
Position of the turntable in the stereo field.
Makes the platter follow Wave position instead of the motor.
How far a drag on the platter moves it.
Smoothing of the platter in hold mode. Smooth 2 to 4 follow.
Number of whole turns added to the wave position.
tips: Drop an audio file on the editor or use Load sample to change the sample.
A still platter in hold mode is silent, only its movement makes sound.

name: Fruity Send
desc: Sends the signal at its place in an effect chain to another mixer insert, with its own volume, pan and dry level.

wiki.intro: Fruity Send is an effect slot plugin that sends the signal at its position in the chain to another mixer insert. You use it when you need a send from the middle of a chain, for example after one effect but before the next. It is read from FL Studio projects when they are imported.
controls: Level of the signal that continues down the current chain.
The mixer insert that receives the sent signal.
tips: The target insert is chosen in the Send to box; the docs note that in FL Studio the insert is not an automatable parameter.
Pan, Volume and Dry are editable and can be automated.

name: Fruity Soft Clipper
desc: Soft clipper with a threshold and a post gain, showing its transfer curve. Rounds off peaks that pass the threshold.

wiki.intro: Fruity Soft Clipper is a mixer effect that bends the signal softly once it passes a threshold, instead of cutting it flat. You add it to an insert to round off peaks or add light distortion. The editor shows the transfer curve and input and output level meters.
controls: Threshold where the soft knee starts.
Button on the panel next to the curve display.
tips: The engine follows FL Studio's exponential knee, so imported projects keep their settings.
Raise Post to make up the level you lose when you lower the threshold.

name: Fruity WaveShaper
desc: Draws a transfer curve that reshapes every sample, with pre amp, mix and post gain. Used for distortion, folding and custom saturation.

wiki.intro: Fruity WaveShaper maps each incoming sample through a curve you draw on a grid, which changes the harmonics of the sound. You add it to an insert for distortion, wave folding or custom saturation. Curves from FL Studio projects are imported.
controls: Chooses whether the curve is applied to both signal polarities or to one.
Pre amp: level into the curve.
Balance of dry and shaped signal.
tips: The editor toggle stored by newer FL Studio project layouts is not identified, so it is not imported.
Exports are treated as FL Studio's rendering mode.

name: Gemini Doubler
desc: Two-voice vocal doubler. Each voice has its own delay, detune, pitch drift, pan, gain and feedback, plus an octave-down switch and voice shelves.

wiki.intro: Gemini Doubler is a native LYNX SHARE effect that thickens a vocal or other mono source with two delayed, slightly detuned copies. Add it to the insert of the track you want to double. Each voice is a pitch-shifting delay.
controls: Switches the unprocessed signal on or off.
Level of the direct signal or of a voice.
Position of the direct signal or of a voice.
Aligns the direct signal with the voices.
Low cut in the feedback path, 80 Hz or 20 Hz.
Pitch offset of a voice in cents.
Source for voice 1: left, sum or difference.

The voices' read head when Align is off. Measured reads each voice with one head that drifts and jumps back, as measured, and uses less than half the CPU. Classic uses two crossfaded taps. New instances start on Measured. Projects and presets saved before 0.1.27 load on Classic and sound as before.
tips: The docs describe the LFO on the pitch as a triangle wave.
The Direct section has low and high shelves; the display shows the combined curve.

name: Glow Leveler
desc: Optical leveler built on an electro-optical cell model, with peak reduction, gain, compress or limit mode, a VU meter and mix control.

wiki.intro: Glow Leveler is an optical leveler: a model of an electro-optical cell with a program-dependent attack and a two-stage release. It has two voicings, Modern and Opto classic, and a new instance starts on Opto classic. A VU meter sits between the Gain and Peak reduction knobs.
controls: How much the leveler turns peaks down. This is the main control.
Limit uses a harder ratio than Compress.
Sets the meter to show the input level, the gain reduction (GR) or the output level.
Turns the gain up as the peak reduction rises.
Adds mains hum and noise after the gain: 50Hz, 60Hz or Off.
Makes the detector more sensitive to highs, which gives less reduction on bass.
Balance between the dry signal and the leveled signal.
Output trim after the mix, -18 dB to +18 dB.
Chooses the voicing: Glow's own engine or the measured classic opto leveler.
Opto classic only. Two small switches keep the limit and make-up law and the attack and release timing of projects saved with earlier versions, or use the measured ones.
Opto classic only, Compress mode. On, the release slows down after long or hard gain reduction, so the leveler recovers fast after a short peak and slowly after a long one. Off by default.
Opto classic only. The peak reduction value at which Auto makeup was switched on. The make-up follows the dial from there.
tips: Turn Mix down to blend the leveled signal with the dry one for parallel leveling.
Switching Auto makeup off leaves the make-up it had applied in the Gain knob.

name: Gross Beat
desc: Time and volume slicing effect with 36 time and 36 volume slots for stutters, gates, tape stops and reverses.

wiki.intro: Gross Beat is a mixer effect that rearranges time and volume of the incoming audio. You trigger slots that stutter, reverse, stop like a tape or gate the signal, usually on a drum bus or a full mix. It is built from the state saved in FL Studio projects, which the project keeps.
controls: Master amount of the time effect.
Master amount of the volume effect.
Edit the envelope of the selected slot.
36 time slots and 36 volume slots, such as Stutter 1/8, Tape stop and Gate 1/4 beat.
tips: The dry path has a latency of 15 samples.
MIDI control of the slots and spline curve type 10 are not supported.

name: Halo
desc: Shimmer reverb with a pitch shifter of plus or minus 12 semitones inside the decay, one or two voices, and tone and modulation controls.

wiki.intro: Halo is a native LYNX SHARE shimmer reverb. A pitch shifter inside the feedback path raises or lowers each repeat, so the tail climbs or falls as it decays. You add it to an insert or a send for pads, vocals and ambient textures.
controls: Pitch shift in the feedback path, -12 to +12 semitones.
Size of the space, which sets the decay.
Tone of the reverb, for example bright.

Measured is the reverb engine of 0.1.27: the decay is set per octave band, a tone corrector follows the reverb network and a diffusion network shapes the onset. It uses less CPU than Classic. New instances start on Measured. Projects and presets saved before 0.1.27 load on Classic and sound as before.
tips: Some mode lists are not fully confirmed against the original, according to the docs.
Use a dual pitch mode for a thicker tail.

name: Hardcore
desc: Guitar pedalboard of five boxes holding 11 pedal types, plus cabinet convolution and an 8-band EQ. Needs files from your own FL Studio installation.

wiki.intro: Hardcore is a guitar multi-effect. The signal passes an input level with a 30 Hz high-pass, five pedal boxes in series, a cabinet convolution, an 8-band EQ and an output level. The cabinet impulses are files of your own FL Studio installation: they are read when an FL Studio project is imported and stored in the project, and without the installation the effect runs with no cabinet.
controls: Eight bipolar faders at 125, 250, 500, 1k, 2k, 4k, 8k and 16k Hz.
Chooses the cabinet impulse, or none.
Switches one of the five boxes on or off.
Under each box. Picks its pedal: Distortion, Chorus, Flanger, Phaser, Reverb, Delay, Noise gate, Equalizer, Compressor, Modulator, Tube drive, or empty.
Distortion: Dist, Comb, Inferno, Glass. Tube drive: Low, High, Gain.
Chorus and Flanger: Width, Speed, Intensity. Phaser: Speed, Tune, Width, Intensity.
Reverb: Decay, Hi-damp, Mix. Delay: Time, Decay, Mix.
Noise gate: Attack, Release, Threshold. Compressor: Threshold, Ratio, Attack, Release.
Equalizer: Low, Middle, Treble, High. Modulator: Pitch, Amp, Pan, Rate.
tips: Each box shows only the knobs its pedal uses.
Because the cabinet impulse is stored in the project, a saved LYNX SHARE project keeps its cabinet without FL Studio.
FL Studio's own preset browser for this plugin is not reproduced.

name: Hardware Insert
desc: Sends audio out of an output on your audio device to outboard gear and brings the return back in, with level, invert and dry/wet controls.

wiki.intro: Hardware Insert routes a track out through a physical output of your audio interface and back in through an input, so you can use outboard gear as an effect. It can also sit in a Patcher. Its round trip is measured and the project delay compensation is built on it.
controls: Audio device output that receives the send.
Sends the sum of both channels to a single output.
Audio device input for the return.
Uses two inputs as a stereo return.
Inverts the polarity of the return.
Measures the round trip through the device.
Balance of dry and returned signal.
tips: With no device open, the round trip shows a note and the plugin has nothing to send to.
Run Ping with your gear connected to set the delay.

name: Horizon
desc: Echo into or after a reverb. Tape, analog, digital, reverse and octave echoes feed eight reverb modes, with modulation and EQ.

wiki.intro: Horizon is a native LYNX SHARE effect that combines an echo and a reverb in one plugin. You choose whether the echo feeds the reverb or follows it. It suits vocals, guitars and synths where you want repeats that melt into a space.
controls: Echo time in ms, or a note value when synced.
Echo level, or reverb level in its own section.
Balance of early and late reflections.
Menus for the echo type, the reverb type and the tone.

Measured is the reverb engine of 0.1.27: the decay is set per octave band, a tone corrector follows the reverb network and a diffusion network shapes the onset. It uses less CPU than Classic. New instances start on Measured. Projects and presets saved before 0.1.27 load on Classic and sound as before.
tips: The ECHO > REV and REV > ECHO switch sets the order of the two stages.
The echo modes are LYNX SHARE's own interpretation, according to the docs.

name: Hush De-esser
desc: Split-band or wideband de-esser with band or high-pass detection, a listen mode and 2 ms lookahead, shown over a live waveform.

wiki.intro: Hush De-esser is a native LYNX SHARE effect that reduces harsh sibilance in vocals. It can work on the sibilant band only or on the whole signal. The large display shows the signal with the threshold line, which you can drag.
controls: The two markers set the detected band.
Lets you listen to the detected band.
A high shelf at about 8 kHz on the processed signal, from off to +12 dB. Off by default.
Balance between the dry signal and the processed one. The dry signal is delayed to match the lookahead. 100 % by default.
tips: Use Audition to find the sibilant range before you set the threshold.
Detection can be set to band or high-pass in the status bar.

name: Hyper Chorus
desc: Dense chorus with two four-voice cores, movement panning, filters and a high-pass cross-fade, built from FL Studio's saved controls.

wiki.intro: Hyper Chorus is a mixer effect that thickens and widens a sound with many modulated delay voices. You add it to pads, synths and vocals. It reads the saved controls of FL Studio's plugin of the same name.
tips: LYNX SHARE starts the LFOs at phase 0, while the original picks random start phases.
All controls are editable and automatable.

name: Kiln Channel
desc: Single console channel strip with six console models, drive, input and output trims, noise reduction and a group bypass shared across channels.

wiki.intro: Kiln Channel is a native LYNX SHARE effect that models one channel of a mixing console. You pick one of six console models and push it with the drive control. It is meant for adding console character to individual tracks.
controls: Level into the console model, -18 to +18.
Selector: American A, British N, Y, Tube, British E and British G.
Group number from 1 to 8, or None.
Switches the console noise floor reduction.
Bypasses all channels in the same group.
Keys that link input and output settings.
Main input and output gain columns with meters.
tips: With noise reduction off each console adds its own noise floor, according to the docs.
Channels that share a group number are bypassed together.

name: Lattice Mod
desc: Multitap modulated delay with 1 to 16 taps, detune and vibrato, rotating stereo feedback, diffusion and drive, in six tabbed pages.

wiki.intro: Lattice Mod is a native LYNX SHARE modulated delay. It spreads one to sixteen taps over the delay time and modulates each with slow detune and vibrato. You use it for chorus, flanging, ensemble and delay textures.
controls: Speed and depth of the slow detune.
Speed and depth of the vibrato.
WARP tab. Measured makes the slow detune swing 3.5 times as far as Classic, as measured. New instances start on Measured. Projects and presets saved before 0.1.27 load on Classic and sound as before.
tips: The tabs MOD, TAPS, DIFF, EQ, DRIVE and WARP hold the remaining controls.
The tap layout and gains are LYNX SHARE's own, according to the docs.

name: Limiter
desc: Simple output limiter with a gain knob, a ceiling and a release time. A transfer display shows how the level is being shaped.

wiki.intro: A small limiter you put on a mixer insert, usually last in the chain, to stop the signal going above a set ceiling. It has three controls and a curve display. Fruity Limiter settings in imported FL Studio projects can load into it.
controls: The level the output is held under, shown in dB.
How quickly the limiter lets go after a peak, shown in ms.
Shows the input to output curve, so you can see where the limiting starts.
tips: Raise Gain while watching the display to see how hard the signal is being limited.
For a mastering limiter with more options, see Apex Limiter.

name: Lo-fi
desc: Sample rate and bit depth reducer with a dry and wet mix. Use it for crunchy, grainy or retro digital sounds.

wiki.intro: A bit crusher for any mixer insert. It lowers the sample rate and the bit depth of the signal and blends the result with the original. A transfer display shows what the reduction does to the signal.
controls: The sample rate the signal is reduced to, shown in Hz. The default is 44100 Hz.
The bit depth the signal is reduced to. The default is 16 bits.
Balance between the dry and the reduced signal, shown in percent.
Plots the input against the output level.
tips: Lower Bits for stepped distortion and lower Rate for aliasing.
Turn Mix down to keep some of the clean signal underneath.

name: Low Lifter
desc: Generates harmonics of the low end of a sound and shows them in a display. It has a look-ahead limiter, a diffuser and a low cut.

wiki.intro: Low Lifter is a bass enhancer. A crossover splits off the low band, which goes through a pre gain, a look-ahead peak limiter and a harmonic enhancer, and is then added back to the delayed high band. It loads the settings of the FL Studio Low Lifter from an imported .flp project.
controls: Pre gain into the limiter and enhancer, 0 dB to 18 dB.
Amount of generated harmonics, -60 dB to 0 dB.
Splits the low band again into four bands around the crossover and processes each on its own.
Lets the limiter see peaks 10 ms ahead. The delay is reported for delay compensation.
Inverts the polarity of the processed low band.
Runs the processed low band through four all-pass stages. Depth sets their coefficient and Mix their amount.
Gain of the processed low band (-120 dB to +12 dB) and of the high band (-120 dB to 0 dB).
Turn the low band and the high band on or off.
Crossover frequency between the bands, 20 Hz to 120 Hz.
High-pass on the output, 20 Hz to 120 Hz.
Balance between the dry signal and the processed signal. The dry signal is delayed to match.
Switches the effect on or off.
tips: After the effect starts, the processed band fades in over the first second.
After a second of silence the engine is skipped and the input passes through.

name: LuxeVerb
desc: Large reverb with decay, size, diffusion, a feedback or feedforward pitch shifter, an output peak filter and a side-chain controlled envelope.

wiki.intro: LuxeVerb is a reverb built on a 16-line feedback delay network with a pitch shifter in its feedback path, or two feed-forward shifters. The page has Input, Reverb, Pitch, Output and Envelope sections. A second page, Space, switches to a separate reverb engine with its own controls. It loads the settings of the FL Studio LuxeVerb from an imported .flp project.
controls: Input: Wet gain, High cut, Low cut
Level and filters of the signal sent into the reverb.
Reverb time. The switch in the section title turns the reverb network on or off.
How long the highs last compared with the rest of the tail.
Sets the lengths of the 16 delay lines.
Amount of the two-stage all-pass diffuser before the network.
Rotation angle of the network's feedback matrix, which changes how the lines feed each other.
Predelay before the reverb. T sets it as a tempo-synced value.
Amount and speed of the LFO that modulates the line lengths.
Freeze stops new input and removes the damping, so the current tail is held. Sustain removes the damping but keeps taking input.
Reads the delay lines with cubic instead of linear interpolation.
A pitch shifter in the reverb's feedback path, with Pitch shift, Gain, Delay, Reverb mix and its own High cut and Low cut. The switch in the section title turns it on.
Two shifters ahead of the reverb, each with Pitch, Amp and Delay, plus Direct amp for the unshifted signal.
Dry and wet levels. L switches the soft limiter.
Peak freq / Peak gain / Peak Q
A peak filter on the output.
Off, Wet or Decay. An envelope follower with Threshold, Scale, Offset, Low cut, Attack, Decay and Smooth raises or lowers the wet level or the decay time. Sidechain picks the input it follows.
tips: Freeze holds the current tail while you play over it.
In Envelope mode Decay the decay time stays between 0.25 and 20 seconds.
The LuxeVerb and Space tabs also switch the engine, so the page shown is the engine heard.

name: LYNX Tune
desc: Real-time vocal pitch corrector with key and scale selection, adjustable retune speed, formant control, a breathiness knob and MIDI target notes.

wiki.intro: LYNX Tune corrects the pitch of a voice or a single-note instrument while you play, on any mixer insert. It is a LYNX SHARE design and is not an import of another plugin. It uses YIN pitch detection and TD-PSOLA shifting.
controls: The voice range of the source.
The notes the pitch is moved to. Auto Key finds them for you.
How fast the pitch moves to the note. 0 ms gives the hard robot effect, up to 400 ms.
Lets held notes keep their natural vibrato.
Switches formant preservation. Shift moves the formants.
Breathiness, 0 to 100 percent. Adds breath noise shaped by the formants of the corrected voice, on voiced sounds.
Shorter delay, about 16 ms instead of about 25 ms for alto and tenor.
Uses the notes held on a Channel Rack channel as targets.
Balance of corrected and original signal.
tips: Set the key and scale first, then lower the retune speed until the correction sounds natural.
The pitch graph shows the input and the corrected pitch over the last 8 seconds.

name: Maximus
desc: Three-band compressor, limiter and saturator for mastering, with a master section, adjustable crossovers and a low cut.

wiki.intro: Maximus splits the signal into low, mid and high bands and processes each with its own dynamics, plus a master stage. It is meant for the end of a mixer chain. The docs mark it with a dagger, which means it reads data from your own FL Studio installation, and some imported states, such as the linear-phase split and Master Mid mode, are only approximated.
controls: Low, Mid, High and Master, each with its own settings.
The state of the selected band.
Level before and after the processing.
Threshold and ceiling of the selected stage.
Delay and mix between the low, mid and high bands.
Crossover frequencies, each with 12 dB or 24 dB slopes.
tips: Use the display to see which band is working while you set each tab.
Four of the 100 FL Studio demo states used the linear-phase split or Master Mid mode, which LYNX SHARE only approximates.

name: Multiband Delay
desc: Splits the sound into 16 bands, each with its own delay, volume and pan, with eight switchable banks and a morph control.

wiki.intro: Multiband Delay splits the signal into 16 bands, sends each band through its own delay line with feedback, volume and pan, and sums the bands again. Eight banks each hold a delay time, a volume and a pan per band. It loads the settings of the FL Studio Multiband Delay from an imported .flp project.
controls: Sixteen bars with their frequencies. Drag across them to draw the value of each band for the chosen target and bank.
Selects which of the three values per band the bars show and edit.
Selects the bank the bars show and edit.
Type of the band crossover. Linear phase adds 1536 samples of latency, which is reported for delay compensation.
Scales the delay times of all bands. The knob is bipolar.
Shortens the delay times to a tenth.
Harmonic scale. The delay times follow a pitch scale, and Scale moves it in semitone steps.
Weighting. Derives each band's feedback from a decay time set by Feedback, so short and long delays die away over the same time.
Amount of each band's delayed signal fed back into its delay line, up to 95 percent.
How slowly the delay times glide to new values.
Crossfades to a new delay time over 100 ms instead of gliding, so the pitch does not bend.
Interpolates the band values between neighbouring banks, from bank 1 at the left to bank 8 at the right.
Stage on the summed bands: a compressor, a saturator or a hard clip.
High-pass filter on the summed bands, 10 Hz to 1 kHz.
Balance between the dry signal and the delayed bands. The dry signal is delayed to match the plugin's latency.
tips: Automate Morph to move through the eight banks.
The selected target and bank are saved with the plugin state.

name: Nebula
desc: Delay and reverb networks with free or tempo-synced delay time, feedback, density, warp and 22 network shapes to choose from.

wiki.intro: Nebula builds large echo and reverb spaces from a delay network. You pick one of 22 network shapes with the Mode control and set the delay time, feedback and density. Add it to a mixer insert, or to a send for ambient effects.
controls: Delay time, from 0 to 2000 ms in free mode.
Free time or a tempo-synced note value.
Amount fed back into the network.
Speed and amount of the modulation.
Upper and lower cut of the wet signal.

Classic or Measured. Measured runs six of the shapes (Ripple, Fold, Drift, Abyss, Glint and Mirage) on a different network model, ported from an MIT-licensed model. The other shapes sound the same on both. New instances start on Measured. Projects and presets saved before 0.1.27 load on Classic and sound as before.
tips: Press Clear to silence a tail that has built up after a feedback change.
The line at the bottom explains the selected mode.

name: Newtime
desc: Time editor for a sample using warp markers. In a song it passes audio through, and plays the warped sample when set to follow the host.

wiki.intro: Newtime edits the timing of a sample by moving warp markers. In LYNX SHARE it passes the insert audio through unchanged, as the FL Studio plugin does. In slave mode it plays the warped sample from the start of the song.
controls: Chooses the audio file to edit: WAV, AIFF, FLAC, OGG or MP3.
Slave to host playback: the edited sample plays from the start of the song.
Makes markers land on the beat grid.
Sends the result to the Playlist as an audio clip.
Writes the edited audio to a file.
tips: Markers from an imported FL Studio project are kept and used when the sample plays.
The docs say the time stretching is LYNX SHARE's own, so results differ from FL Studio's.

name: Newtone
desc: Pitch editor for a sung or played sample. It finds the notes so you can move, cut and reshape them, and plays the edit with the song.

wiki.intro: Newtone analyses a sample into notes and lets you edit pitch, formants, volume and timing for each one. As in FL Studio, it passes live audio through unchanged. In slave mode it plays the edited sample from the song start.
controls: Chooses the audio file to edit.
