Finds the notes again and discards the note edits.
Click a note to slice it there. Ctrl+click glues a note to the one before.
Moves every note to the nearest semitone.
Pulls the notes toward their semitone.
The notes' vibrato and drift. 100 percent is as sung.
How long the pitch takes to move between notes.
Per note pitch change, from -24 to 24 semitones.
Moves the voice's formants, from -12 to 12 semitones.
Per note level, from -24 to 12 dB.
Glide at the start or end of a note.
Adds a vibrato to a note.
tips: Score sends the notes to a piano roll or saves them as a MIDI file.
Pitch edits are rendered by LYNX SHARE's own engine, so they are close to FL Studio but not identical.

name: Orbit
desc: Modulation machine with barber-pole and through-zero flangers, choruses, a doubler, an ensemble and a symphonic mode, controlled by five knobs.

wiki.intro: Orbit covers flanging, chorus and doubling in one effect for mixer inserts. You pick the character with Mode, such as the rising barber-pole flange, and shape it with five knobs. The hint line under the Mode control describes the current mode.
controls: Dry and wet balance, equal power.
Modulation rate, within plus or minus 10 Hz.
Manual delay offset of the sweep.
Barber-pole, through-zero flange, tri and octo chorus, doubler, ensemble, symphonic and more.

Measured changes the sweep of Rise and Rise / fall, the base delay under Manual and the feedback curve to measured ones. In Rise / fall the left side rises while the right side falls. New instances start on Measured. Projects and presets saved before 0.1.27 load on Classic and sound as before.
tips: Feedback is signed, so it can be set below zero as well as above.
The Rise mode is a flanger whose sweep rises and falls like a barber-pole.

name: Parametric EQ
desc: Seven-band parametric equaliser with a draggable frequency response and a linear-phase mode, used for tone shaping on any insert.

wiki.intro: A seven-band parametric EQ for mixer inserts. You shape it on the response graph with drag handles, and the faders and knobs on the right show the same values. It loads Fruity Parametric EQ 2 and Fruity Parametric EQ settings from FL Studio projects, including their band widths.
controls: Moves a band in frequency and gain.
Changes the Q of the band under the cursor.
Sets the band gain to 0 dB.
One fader per band, with a range of 18 dB up and down.
tips: The graph shows the frequency range in note names and in ranges from sub to treble.
Linear phase is part of the engine; see the docs for its latency.

name: Patcher
desc: Node graph that holds plugins and cables inside one insert, with side-chain, extra outputs and a control surface you can build.

wiki.intro: Patcher lets you connect effects, instruments and VST3 or CLAP plugins with cables inside a single mixer slot. The graph has an input and an output node. FL Studio projects with a Patcher open as the same graph.
controls: The graph view, where plugins are nodes and wires carry audio, notes and control values.
A page of your own knobs, sliders, buttons, check boxes and XY pads.
Lets you move, rename or delete Surface controls.
Adds a control to the Surface.
Right-click in the Map to add a plugin.
Scales the view to show the whole graph.
tips: Drag from an output pin to an input pin to connect two nodes.
Double-click a node to open its editor.

name: Peak Controller
desc: Follows the level of the audio and an LFO and turns them into control values that can move other plugin parameters.

wiki.intro: The Peak Controller passes audio through unchanged and measures its peak level. That level, mixed with an LFO, becomes a control value you can link to other parameters, for example to duck a pad from a kick. FL Studio's Fruity Peak Controller loads into it.
controls: Base value of the peak output.
Shapes the curve of the peak response.
How slowly the detector falls after a peak.
Shapes the curve of the LFO.
Limits how fast each output can change.
Silences the audio that passes through.
tips: The graph shows the combined Peak and LFO output.
The LFO follows the song position while the song plays.

name: Pitch correction
desc: Real-time pitch corrector for a single voice or line. Notes you leave lit on the keyboard strip pull the sung pitch towards them, with a speed control.

wiki.intro: Pitch correction detects the pitch of a monophonic input and shifts it to the nearest allowed note. It loads the settings of an FL Studio Pitcher from an imported .flp project. The plain shifter has 9 samples of latency and the Formant path 257 samples, both reported for delay compensation.
controls: The twelve notes. Lit notes are the ones the voice is pulled to.
One per note. A note switched here passes uncorrected.
Bypasses the correction for every note.
How fast the pitch moves to the target note. Fully up, the correction is immediate.
Offset of the output pitch, from -1 to +1 semitone.
Reference frequency of A that the notes are measured against, adjustable by up to a semitone either way.
Lowest note the detector looks for: 220, 170, 110, 80, 55 or 25 Hz.
Switches to the formant path, which shifts with pitch-synchronous grains so the Gender knob can set the formants.
Formant path only. Resamples the grains by a factor from 0.5 to 2, which moves the formants down or up.
Which channel the pitch is read from: Left, Independent (each channel on its own) or Right.
Takes the allowed notes from held MIDI notes instead of the note keys.
In MIDI mode, allows only the octave of each held note instead of that note in every octave.
Builds up to four harmony voices from held MIDI notes. The panel then shows Voice panning, Stereo spread, Replace or Mix, and Vel.
tips: Effects in LYNX SHARE receive no MIDI notes, so MIDI mode applies no correction and Harmonize outputs the dry voice.

name: Pitch shift
desc: Simple pitch shifter with semitone and cent controls, a grain size and a dry and wet mix. Used to transpose a track or add a detuned copy.

wiki.intro: Pitch shift is LYNX SHARE's own, simple pitch shifter for a mixer insert. It transposes the signal by semitones and cents and blends the result with the original. When a .flp project with an FL Studio Pitch Shifter has no exact engine to open it, its settings are converted to this effect.
controls: Size of the grains the signal is cut into, shown in milliseconds (the parameter is called Window).
Balance between the dry and the shifted signal.
tips: Keep Mix below 100 % and Cents small to get a detune thickening instead of a plain transposition.

name: Pitch Shifter
desc: Pitch and formant shifter with voice and music modes, a delay with feedback and pitch analysis settings. It runs the engines of the FL Studio original.

wiki.intro: Pitch Shifter is an effect for a mixer insert that moves pitch and formants separately, and can add a delay to the shifted signal. It is built on the engines of FL Studio's Pitch Shifter, and opens its settings when a .flp project is imported. The Voice and Music tabs on the left pick the kind of material.
controls: Amount of formant correction, shown as a percentage.
Three selectors (Relative, Fast, Left in the picture) for how the pitch is measured.
Delay time of the delay section.
Switch next to Delay, used for tempo sync.
Amount fed back into the delay.
Off, Post, Pre or No shift: where the delay sits relative to the shifter.
Balance between the dry and the processed signal.
Drag in the large pad to move the pitch and formant values together.
tips: The engines match FL's bit for bit on the states tested, and the latency is reported so the mixer can compensate.
FL's granular engine shares one random sequence across all instances. LYNX gives each instance its own.

name: Pocket Autoduck
desc: Ducks the volume on every beat of the song, with depth, attack, hold, length, shift and six recovery shapes. No sidechain input is needed. Rebuilt from FL Studio Mobile's Autoduck.

wiki.intro: Pocket Autoduck lowers the level at each beat and lets it rise again, which gives a pumping sound like sidechain compression against a kick. It follows the beat of the song, not an audio input. It is the engine that FL Studio Mobile projects (.flm) load their Autoduck module on, and it can also be added to any mixer slot.
controls: Depth of the level drop, 0 to 100%. At 100% the signal is silent at the lowest point.
Time the level takes to fall, from a very short time up to about half a beat. It is shown in ms at the song tempo.
Bends the fall and the recovery. The value reads Linear at the top of its range.
Length of the whole duck as a part of the beat, 0 to 100%.
Moves the duck earlier or later, -50 to +50% of a beat.
How long the level stays down before it recovers, as a part of Time.
Shape of the recovery: Accel, Accel 2, Decel, Decel 2, S-Curve or S-Curve 2.
tips: The duck always repeats once per beat. Other note lengths are not available.
While the song is stopped, the duck keeps running at the song tempo.

name: Pocket Chorus
desc: Chorus with two modulated voices, rate, depth, stereo spread and mix. Rebuilt from FL Studio Mobile's Chorus.

wiki.intro: Pocket Chorus adds two modulated copies of the signal to the dry sound for a wider, thicker tone. The copies are made from the sum of the left and right sides and the delay is at most 10 ms. It is the engine that FL Studio Mobile projects (.flm) load their Chorus module on, and it can also be added to any mixer slot.
controls: Speed of the modulation, 0.20 to 4.20 Hz. The second voice runs 0.1 Hz faster.
How far the modulation moves, 0 to 100%.
At 100% one voice goes to the left side and the other to the right. Lower values put both voices on both sides.
Level of the two voices, 0 to 100%. They are added to the dry signal, which stays at full level. The control follows a square law.
tips: Because the voices are added on top of the dry signal, high Mix values raise the level.
The second voice fades between the current signal and a copy about 10 ms old. Its delay time does not sweep. This matches FL Studio Mobile.

name: Pocket Comb Filter
desc: Comb filter with feedback that is tuned by hand, to the lowest held key, or to the pitch it detects in the input. Rebuilt from FL Studio Mobile's Comb Filter.

wiki.intro: Pocket Comb Filter adds a short delay with feedback to the dry signal, so the sound rings at the tuned pitch. The pitch can be set by hand, follow the lowest key held on the Channel rack, or follow the pitch detected in the input. It is the engine that FL Studio Mobile projects (.flm) load their Comb Filter module on, with every value copied as it is, and it can also be added to any mixer slot.
controls: Manual, Lowest Note or Detect Pitch. Manual uses Pitch, or Pitch oct and Pitch note when Snap is on. Lowest Note follows the lowest key held on the Channel rack and keeps the last one after release. Detect Pitch follows the pitch of the input.
Frequency in Manual mode when Snap is off, 1 Hz to 2.50 kHz on a fourth-power law.
How much of the delayed signal is fed back, 0 to 100 %. Higher values ring longer.
Level of the comb signal added to the dry signal, 0 to 100 %. The dry signal stays at full level.
Moves the pitch by -2 to +2 octaves in Lowest Note and Detect Pitch modes.
How slowly the pitch glides to a new value, 0 to 100 %.
On: Manual mode plays the note set by Pitch oct and Pitch note. Off: it uses the Pitch frequency.
Sign of the feedback per side: Both +, Left -, Right - or Both -.
-5.0 to +5.0 %. Lowers the left side's frequency and raises the right side's by this amount (negative values do the opposite).
Note name, C to B. With no key held yet, Lowest Note also starts on this note (E3 by default).
tips: Lowest Note reads the keys held on all channels of the Channel rack. In FL Studio Mobile it reads only the rack the effect sits on.
Detect Pitch works best on pitched sounds. On drums or noise it can lock to wrong pitches, and FL Studio Mobile's own detector is not consistent there either.
The tuning follows FL Studio Mobile's delay loop, which is about 19 cents off an ideal comb at the same note.
The effect has a plain knob page, not FL Studio Mobile's panel.

name: Pocket Compressor
desc: Peak compressor with threshold, ratio up to infinity, attack, hold, release, auto gain, an output level and a detector input gain. Rebuilt from FL Studio Mobile's Compressor.

wiki.intro: Pocket Compressor reduces the level of the loud parts of a track. A peak detector with hold reads the louder of the two channels and one gain is applied to both. It is the engine that FL Studio Mobile projects (.flm) load their Compressor module on, with every value copied as it is, and it can also be added to any mixer slot.
controls: Level above which compression starts, -40 dB to 0 dB.
1:1 to 20:1 on a square law. The top of the range reads +inf and holds the level at the threshold.
How fast the detector follows a rising level, 0 to 50 ms on a square law.
How fast the held peak falls after the hold time, 10 ms to 500 ms on a square law.
Output gain. With Auto gain on it reads -20 dB to +20 dB, with Auto gain off 0 dB to +40 dB for the same knob travel.
Time the detector keeps a peak before the release starts, 0 to 50 ms on a square law.
Adds make-up gain worked out from Thresh and Ratio, so that a full-scale input comes out at full scale.
Gain of the signal that feeds the detector only, -20 dB to +20 dB. It does not change the level of the audio itself.
Stored for compatibility. FL Studio Mobile never turns it on, so it always reads Off and has no effect.
tips: Switching Auto gain moves the Level read-out by 20 dB and the output level with it. Check Level after changing it.
There is no look-ahead and no latency.

name: Pocket Distortion
desc: Distortion with four curves, drive, bias, a left and right drive balance, a sample-and-hold crusher and an output gain. Rebuilt from FL Studio Mobile's Distortion.

wiki.intro: Pocket Distortion shapes the signal with one of four curves, then holds samples for a crushed sound and scales the output. Use it to add grit to drums, basses and synths. It is the engine that FL Studio Mobile projects (.flm) load their Distortion module on, and it can also be added to any mixer slot.
controls: Selects the curve. Hard is a knee curve that flattens as the level rises, Tube is a tanh curve, Soft is an exponential curve and Clip cuts the signal off at full scale.

Bipolar, -100 to 100. Adds an offset before the curve so the two halves of the wave distort differently. The slider follows a fifth-power law, so it acts mostly near the ends. A high-pass filter removes the offset after the curve.
Amount of distortion, shown as 0 to 100.
Shares the drive between the sides, shown as -100 to 100. At 0 both sides get the full drive. Below 0 the left side gets less drive, above 0 the right side gets less.
Holds each output sample for 1 to 257 samples. The slider follows a fourth-power law, so the first half changes little.
tips: BitCrush lowers the sample rate by holding samples. It does not reduce the bit depth.
Gain only lowers the level. Use it to compensate for the level that Drive adds.

name: Pocket EQ
desc: Four-band equalizer with a low shelf, peak or high shelf per band, a bandwidth in octaves and a choice of channel per band. Rebuilt from FL Studio Mobile's Equalizer.

wiki.intro: Pocket EQ has four bands. Each band is a low shelf, a peak or a high shelf with its own gain, frequency and bandwidth, and it can work on both sides, on one side only, or on the two sides in opposite directions. It is the engine that FL Studio Mobile projects (.flm) load their Equalizer module on, with every value copied as it is, and it can also be added to any mixer slot.
controls: Gain of the band, shown as -12 to +12 dB. As in FL Studio Mobile, the band boosts or cuts twice the amount shown, so the full range is -24 to +24 dB.
Frequency of the band, 32 Hz to about 19.5 kHz.
Width of the band, 0.25 to 7.25 octaves.
Low shelf, Peak or High shelf. Low shelf is the lower half of the range, Peak the upper half, and High shelf only the very top.
Which side the band works on: Both, Left, Right, Left + / right - (the right side gets the opposite gain) or Left - / right + (the left side gets the opposite gain).
tips: The bands run at twice the sample rate, as in FL Studio Mobile.
The four bands are chained in FL Studio Mobile's way, which delays the sound by 1.5 samples. Like FL Studio Mobile, the effect does not report this to the delay compensation.
The effect has a plain knob page, not FL Studio Mobile's EQ panel.

name: Pocket Filter
desc: Low-pass, band-pass or high-pass filter with a frequency, a Q and a slope of 24, 48 or 96 dB per octave. Rebuilt from FL Studio Mobile's Filter.

wiki.intro: Pocket Filter is a resonant filter made of one, two or four pairs of identical filter stages. It is the engine that FL Studio Mobile projects (.flm) load their Filter module on, with every value copied as it is, and it can also be added to any mixer slot.
controls: Cutoff or centre frequency, 16 Hz to about 20 kHz.
Resonance, shown as 0.80 to 2.80, on a square law.
LP (low-pass), BP (band-pass) or HP (high-pass). LP is the lower half of the range, BP the upper half, and HP only the very top.
24 dB/O, 48 dB/O or 96 dB/O. 24 dB/O is the lower half of the range, 48 dB/O the upper half, and 96 dB/O only the very top.
tips: As in FL Studio Mobile, the low-pass lowers the level by about 2 dB per pair of stages: about 2, 4 and 8 dB at 24, 48 and 96 dB/O. The band-pass raises the centre by the Q value, up to about 9 dB.
A change of Slope switches at once, and the low-pass level follows only at the next change of Frequency, Q or Type. FL Studio Mobile does the same.
Each pair of stages delays the sound by one sample, which is not reported to the delay compensation, as in FL Studio Mobile.

name: Pocket Flanger
desc: Flanger built on a short tape loop of up to 5 ms, with an LFO, feedback, a stereo phase offset and polarity switches for feedback and wet. Rebuilt from FL Studio Mobile's Flanger.

wiki.intro: Pocket Flanger adds a very short, LFO-swept delay to the dry signal. The delay is a tape-style loop whose speed glides, which smooths the sweep. It is the engine that FL Studio Mobile projects (.flm) load their Flanger module on, with every value copied as it is, and it can also be added to any mixer slot.
controls: Length of the LFO cycle when Sync is on, in 13 steps: 1/4, 3/8, 1/2, 3/4, 1/1, 2/1, 4/1, 8/1, 1 bar, 2 bars, 4 bars, 8 bars, 16 bars.
On uses LFO rate and follows the song position. Off uses LFO speed.
Speed of the LFO when Sync is off, 0.1 Hz to 10 Hz on a cubic law.
How far the LFO sweeps the delay around its centre, 0 to 100 %.
Centre delay, 0 to 2.5 ms on a square law.
Amount of the delayed signal fed back into the loop, 0 to 100 %.
Inverts the polarity of the feedback. On by default.
Moves the right channel's LFO ahead in phase, up to half a cycle at 100 %.
Level of the delayed signal added to the dry signal, 0 to 100 % on a square law.
Inverts the polarity of the delayed signal. On by default.
tips: The rate labels are FL Studio Mobile's own: 1/1 is one beat and 1 bar is sixteen beats.
The two invert switches change which frequencies the comb filter cancels, try both settings.
After a reset the delayed signal stays silent until one loop has been recorded.

name: Pocket Gate
desc: Noise gate with threshold, asymmetry, attack, hold and release with curve controls, and a mix control that can invert the gate. Rebuilt from FL Studio Mobile's Gate.

wiki.intro: Pocket Gate lowers the signal while it is below a threshold. Use it to cut noise between notes or to tighten drums. The controls are on two pages, LEVEL and ENVELOPE. It is the engine that FL Studio Mobile projects (.flm) load their Gate module on, and it can also be added to any mixer slot.
controls: Switches between the level page and the timing page.
Level that opens the gate, -60 to +6 dB. The gate opens when either side is above it.
How far below the threshold the level must fall before the gate closes, 0 to 66 dB.
Show the input level with a mark at the threshold. The threshold in dB is printed below.
Depth of the gate, -100 to 100%. At 100% a closed gate lowers the signal by 60 dB. At 0% the gate does nothing. Negative values invert the gate, so it lowers the signal while it is open.
Time the gate takes to open and to close, each 0 to 1000 ms.
Bipolar, -1 to 1. Bend the opening and the closing ramp. At 0 the ramp is linear, one direction gives a logarithmic shape and the other an exponential shape.
Shortest time the gate stays open after it opens, 0 to 1000 ms.
tips: The gate measures the level in blocks of 256 samples and looks ahead by 255 samples. It reports this as latency.
Set Asymmetry above 0 to stop the gate from chattering on a signal that hovers around the threshold.

name: Pocket Graphic EQ
desc: Eight-band graphic equalizer from 80 Hz to 12 kHz, one octave per band. Rebuilt from FL Studio Mobile's Graphic EQ.

wiki.intro: Pocket Graphic EQ has eight fixed bands, one octave wide: a low shelf at 80 Hz, peaks at 160 Hz, 375 Hz, 750 Hz, 1.5 kHz, 3 kHz and 6 kHz, and a high shelf at 12 kHz. It is the engine that FL Studio Mobile projects (.flm) load their Graphic EQ module on, with every value copied as it is, and it can also be added to any mixer slot.
controls: Low shelf. Gain shown as -12 to +12 dB.
160 Hz, 375 Hz, 750 Hz, 1.5 kHz, 3 kHz, 6 kHz
Peak bands. Gain shown as -12 to +12 dB.
High shelf. Gain shown as -12 to +12 dB.
tips: As in FL Studio Mobile, each band boosts or cuts twice the amount shown, so the full range is -24 to +24 dB.
The bands are chained in FL Studio Mobile's way, which delays the sound by 8 samples. Like FL Studio Mobile, the effect does not report this to the delay compensation.
The effect has a plain knob page, not FL Studio Mobile's sliders.

name: Pocket Leveller
desc: Gain and pan trim with a level meter and a dB scale. Rebuilt from FL Studio Mobile's Leveller.

wiki.intro: Pocket Leveller sets the level and the left and right balance of a track. It is a trim and does not compress. It is the engine that FL Studio Mobile projects (.flm) load their Leveller module on, and it can also be added to any mixer slot.
controls: Long bar under the dB scale. Sets the level from -60 to +12 dB. The value is shown above the bar.
Balance between the sides, from 100% L through mid to 100% R. It lowers the opposite side and leaves the other side at full level.
Thin bar under the scale that shows the output level on the same dB scale as Gain.
tips: The left end of the scale is labelled -inf., but the lowest gain is -60 dB, so the signal is not fully muted.
Gain and Pan changes glide over a few milliseconds, so moving them does not click.

name: Pocket Limiter Classic
desc: Peak limiter with threshold, release time and output gain and no look-ahead. Rebuilt from FL Studio Mobile's Limiter (legacy).

wiki.intro: Pocket Limiter Classic is a simple peak limiter. When the louder side goes over the threshold, the gain drops at once and then recovers along a smooth curve. It is the engine that FL Studio Mobile projects (.flm) load their Limiter (legacy) module on, and it can also be added to any mixer slot.
controls: Level above which the gain is reduced, -24 to 0 dB.
How long the gain takes to recover, shown as 0 to 100%. It runs from about 200 ms at 0% to 1 second at 100%.
tips: The output is scaled up by the amount the threshold is lowered, so limited peaks come out at the Output Gain level. Lowering Threshold makes the signal louder.
There is no look-ahead and it adds no latency. The gain drops within one sample when a peak crosses the threshold.

name: Pocket Limiter
desc: Look-ahead peak limiter with input gain, threshold, release and output gain, and a trace of the gain reduction. Rebuilt from FL Studio Mobile's Limiter.

wiki.intro: Pocket Limiter is a peak limiter with a 2 ms look-ahead. Push the level with In Gain and it holds the peaks at the threshold. It is the engine that FL Studio Mobile projects (.flm) load their Limiter module on, and it can also be added to any mixer slot.
controls: Gain before the limiter, -24 to +24 dB.
Threshold. Level above which the gain is reduced, -24 to 0 dB.
Time the gain takes to return to full level after a peak, 0.10 to 2.00 seconds.
Gain after the limiter, -24 to +24 dB.
Draws the recent gain reduction, from 0 dB on the top line down to 24 dB, with the newest value on the right.
tips: The look-ahead adds 2 ms of latency, which the effect reports to the host.
There is no automatic make-up gain. Use Out Gain to set the final level.

name: Pocket Multiband Compressor
desc: Three-band compressor with two crossovers, and per band an input gain, threshold, ratio, attack, release, output gain, On, Bypass or Mute, and a stereo width. Rebuilt from FL Studio Mobile's Multiband Compressor.

wiki.intro: Pocket Multiband Compressor splits the sound into low, mid and high bands with two 24 dB crossovers and compresses each band on its own. Its ratio works on the signal's amplitude, not on decibels, so it is gentler than a usual compressor at the same numbers. It is the engine that FL Studio Mobile projects (.flm) load their Multiband Compressor module on, with every value copied as it is, and it can also be added to any mixer slot. Its editor is a page of plain knobs, one row of names per band (Low, Mid, High).
controls: Output level of the whole effect, -24 dB to +24 dB.
Split between the low and mid bands, 20 Hz to 10.2 kHz.
Split between the mid and high bands, 20 Hz to 10.2 kHz.
Off, Low, Mid or High: plays only that band. This control is LYNX SHARE's own; FL Studio Mobile keeps an editor setting in its place, which a .flm import resets to Off.
Adds the uncompressed band to the compressed one, 0 to 100%, for parallel compression.
Gain into the band, -24 dB to +24 dB. It feeds both the detector and the audio.
Level above which the band is compressed, -48 dB to 0 dB.
How fast the band's compressor reacts, 0 to 50 ms on a square law.
How fast it lets go, 10 ms to 1 s.
Output gain of the band, -24 dB to +24 dB.
On compresses the band, Bypass passes it as split, Mute silences it.
Stereo width of the band, 0 to 200%. 100% leaves it as it is, 0% is mono.
Mode 1: above 100% the width moves towards the side signal alone. Mode 2: above 100% part of the other channel is subtracted from each side.
tips: A bypassed band skips its input gain, output gain and width as well.
Attack and release are worked out for 44.1 kHz at every sample rate, as FL Studio Mobile does. At 48 kHz or 96 kHz they are shorter than their read-outs.
For new mixes the Fruity Multiband Compressor or Prism Multiband are the fuller tools. This one is here so that FL Studio Mobile songs sound as they did on the phone.

name: Pocket MultiFX
desc: Eight effects on one X/Y pad: delay, reverb, low-pass and high-pass filter, flanger, phaser, panner and a vowel filter, with a tempo-locked LFO. Rebuilt from FL Studio Mobile's MultiFX.

wiki.intro: Pocket MultiFX runs one of eight effects and puts its two main settings on an X/Y pad. An LFO locked to the song position can move the X setting. It suits live sweeps and automation. It is the engine that FL Studio Mobile projects (.flm) load their MultiFX module on, and it can also be added to any mixer slot.
controls: Delay, Reverb, LP Filter, HP Filter, Flanger, Phaser, Panner, Vox
Selects the effect. The old effect fades out and the new one fades in.

Sets the two settings of the selected effect. The lines on the pad carry the names of the axes. Delay: Feedback and Filter. Reverb: Decay and Filter. LP Filter and HP Filter: Frequency and Resonance. Flanger and Phaser: Frequency and Feedback. Panner: Panning and Distance. Vox: Vowel and Size.
Length of one LFO cycle, in ten steps: 1/8, 1/4, 3/8, 1/2 and 3/4 of a beat, 1 beat, 2 beats, 1 bar, 2 bars and 4 bars. In Delay it also sets the delay time.
How far the LFO moves the X setting. In Delay the LFO pans the echoes instead. The slider follows a square law.
tips: The LP and HP filters are 48 dB per octave. LP Filter covers about 64 Hz to 20 kHz and HP Filter about 32 Hz to 5.5 kHz.
The LFO has no effect on Reverb.
In Delay, a delay time above 1.5 seconds is halved until it fits.

name: Pocket Phaser
desc: Six-stage phaser with feedback, a centre frequency, a tempo-synced or free LFO with three shapes, and a stereo phase offset. Rebuilt from FL Studio Mobile's Phaser.

wiki.intro: Pocket Phaser runs the sound through six first-order all-pass stages that an LFO sweeps, and adds the result on top of the dry signal. It is the engine that FL Studio Mobile projects (.flm) load their Phaser module on, with every value copied as it is, and it can also be added to any mixer slot.
controls: Length of the LFO cycle when Sync is on, in 13 steps: 1/4, 3/8, 1/2, 3/4, 1/1, 2/1, 4/1, 8/1, 1 bar, 2 bars, 4 bars, 8 bars, 16 bars.
How far the LFO moves the stages, 0 to 100 % on a cubic law.
Feeds the last stage back into the first, 0 to 100 % (up to 0.95).
Centre of the sweep, 50 Hz to 16 kHz on a square law.
Level of the phased signal added to the dry signal, 0 to 100 % on a square law. The dry signal stays at full level.
On uses LFO rate and follows the song position. Off uses LFO speed.
Speed of the LFO when Sync is off, 0.1 Hz to 10 Hz on a cubic law.
Moves the right channel's LFO ahead in phase, up to half a cycle at 100 %.
tips: The rate labels are FL Studio Mobile's own: 1/1 is one beat and 1 bar is sixteen beats, so 16 bars is 256 beats.
The sweep is limited to the range 50 Hz to 16 kHz.

name: Pocket Reverb
desc: Plate reverb with one Mix knob that blends dry and wet, decay, damping, room size, predelay, width, low and high cuts, early reflections, modulation and a pan for the reverb. Rebuilt from FL Studio Mobile's Reverb.

wiki.intro: Pocket Reverb is FL Studio Mobile's current reverb module on FL Studio Mobile's own plate. It uses the controls of the older module, with the plate's early reflections and tail at fixed levels, and mixes them with the dry signal itself. It is the engine that FL Studio Mobile projects (.flm) load their Reverb module on, with every value copied as it is, and it can also be added to any mixer slot. Its editor is a page of plain knobs.
controls: Length of the tail, 0.1 s to 20 s. The knob follows a cube law, so most of its travel covers the short times.
Frequency above which the tail loses its highs faster, 0.5 kHz to 22.1 kHz. The top of the range reads Off.
Blend of dry and reverb. Below the middle the dry stays at full level and the reverb rises; above it the reverb stays at full level and the dry falls. In the middle both are at full level.
Pans the reverb, not the dry signal.
Level of the early reflections, 0 to 100% on a square law.
Time before the reverb starts, 0 to 250 ms.
How quickly the echoes blur into a smooth tail, 0 to 100%.
Stereo width of the reverb, 0 to 200%.
Cuts the lows of the signal that enters the reverb, 19 Hz to 3000 Hz. The bottom of the range reads Off.
Cuts the highs of the signal that enters the reverb, 0.5 kHz to 22.1 kHz. The top of the range reads Off.
Speed of the modulation in the tail, 0.1 Hz to 10 Hz.
Amount of modulation in the tail, 0 to 100%.
Overall level of the reverb, 0 to 100%.
Overall level of the dry signal, 0 to 100%.
tips: Level changes glide over a few milliseconds, so moving Mix, Pan, ER or the two levels does not click.
This plate is not Fruity Reeverb 2: at the same settings its low end rings longer.
Modulation has not been compared with FL Studio Mobile by ear yet: none of the projects it was measured on uses it.

name: Pocket Reverb 2
desc: Plate reverb with size, decay, damping, low and high cuts, dry, early reflection and wet levels, a predelay of up to 1000 ms that can follow the tempo, a side input, separation and a wet pan. Rebuilt from FL Studio Mobile's Reverb 2.

wiki.intro: Pocket Reverb 2 runs FL Studio Mobile's plate at full level and mixes the dry signal, the early reflections and the tail itself, then sets the stereo separation and pans the reverb. It is the engine that FL Studio Mobile projects (.flm) load their Reverb 2 module on, with every value copied as it is, and it can also be added to any mixer slot. Its editor is a page of plain knobs.
controls: Cuts the highs of the signal that enters the reverb, 0.5 kHz to 22.1 kHz. The top of the range reads Off.
Cuts the lows of the signal that enters the reverb, 19 Hz to 3000 Hz. The bottom of the range reads Off.
Length of the tail, 0.1 s to 20 s, on a straight scale.
How quickly the echoes blur into a smooth tail, 0 to 100%.
Frequency above which the tail loses its highs faster, 0.5 kHz to 22.1 kHz. The top of the range reads Off.
Level of the original signal, 0 to 125%.
Level of the early reflections, 0 to 125%.
On feeds the reverb with the difference of left and right instead of their sum, so only the stereo part of the sound is reverberated.
Time before the reverb starts, 0 to 1000 ms.
On makes Delay a number of sixteenths of a beat at the song tempo, up to one beat. A delay longer than 1000 ms is shortened by a sixteenth at a time until it fits.
Amount of modulation in the tail, 0 to 100%.
Decay of the lows against the rest of the tail, x0.2 to x3.0.
Stereo width of the reverb, 0 to 200%. 100% leaves it as the plate makes it.
Speed of the modulation, 0.1 Hz to 10 Hz on a cube law.
Frequency below which Bass acts, 25 Hz to 2000 Hz.
Pans the reverb, not the dry signal.
tips: Unlike the other two Pocket reverbs, the dry signal has its own level here, so Dry at 0% gives the reverb alone.
Delay always reads in ms, also when Tempo is on.
Modulation has not been compared with FL Studio Mobile by ear yet: none of the projects it was measured on uses it.

name: Pocket Reverb Classic
desc: Plate reverb with decay, room size, predelay, damping, low and high cuts, a bass multiplier, modulation, and input, early reflection, dry and wet levels in dB with a mute switch each. Rebuilt from FL Studio Mobile's Reverb (legacy).

wiki.intro: Pocket Reverb Classic is FL Studio Mobile's older reverb module on FL Studio Mobile's own plate, a network close to Fruity Reeverb 2 but not the same. The original signal always passes at full level and the reverb is added to it. It is the engine that FL Studio Mobile projects (.flm) load their Reverb (legacy) module on, with every value copied as it is, and it can also be added to any mixer slot. Its editor is a page of plain knobs.
controls: Length of the tail, 0.1 s to 20 s. The knob follows a cube law, so most of its travel covers the short times.
Frequency above which the tail loses its highs faster, 0.5 kHz to 22.1 kHz. The top of the range reads Off.
Level of the reverb, shown in dB from -inf up to +6.0 dB.
Time before the reverb starts, 0 to 250 ms.
How quickly the echoes blur into a smooth tail, 0 to 100%.
Stereo width of the reverb, 0 to 200%.
Cuts the lows of the signal that enters the reverb, 19 Hz to 3000 Hz. The bottom of the range reads Off.
Cuts the highs of the signal that enters the reverb, 0.5 kHz to 22.1 kHz. The top of the range reads Off.
Level of the signal sent into the reverb, -inf to +6.0 dB.
Level of the early reflections, -inf to +6.0 dB.
Extra dry signal added by the reverb, -inf to +6.0 dB. It is -inf on a new instance.
Mutes the signal sent into the reverb. Reads On or Muted.
Mutes the extra dry signal of Dry level. Reads On or Muted.
Mutes the early reflections. Reads On or Muted.
Mutes the reverb tail. Reads On or Muted.
Decay of the lows against the rest of the tail, x0.2 to x3.0.
Frequency below which Bass mult acts, 25 Hz to 2000 Hz.
Speed of the modulation in the tail, 0.1 Hz to 10 Hz.
Amount of modulation in the tail, 0 to 100%.
tips: The original signal is never lowered: Dry off and Dry level only change the extra dry copy, not the signal that passes through.
Of the three Pocket reverbs this is the only one with mute switches and levels in dB. Pocket Reverb 2 sets its levels in percent and Pocket Reverb has one Mix knob.
Modulation has not been compared with FL Studio Mobile by ear yet: none of the projects it was measured on uses it.

name: Pocket Spacer
desc: Stereo tool with a left/right delay, pan, separation, a mid/side delay, polarity switches for each pair and three stereo modes. Rebuilt from FL Studio Mobile's Spacer.

wiki.intro: Pocket Spacer moves a sound around the stereo field with short delays, polarity inversion and a width control. Use it to offset one side, narrow or widen a track, or work on mid and side separately. It is the engine that FL Studio Mobile projects (.flm) load their Spacer module on, with every value copied as it is, and it can also be added to any mixer slot.
controls: Delays one side by up to 300 ms on a cubic law. Right of centre delays the left channel, left of centre delays the right channel. Reads off in the centre.
Lowers the level of the opposite side. Reads Center in the middle, then 0 to 100 %.
Bipolar, -100 % to +100 %, off in the centre. Positive values narrow the image down to mono. Negative values subtract part of each channel from the other to widen it.
Inverts the polarity of the channels: none, left, right or both.
Delays one signal of the mid/side pair by up to 100 ms on a fifth-power law, so the range near the centre is very fine (microseconds). Right of centre delays mid, left of centre delays side.
Inverts the polarity of the mid/side pair: none, mid, side or both.

Standard encodes to mid/side, applies the M/S stage and decodes back to left/right. Output M/S leaves the result as mid on the left and side on the right. Input M/S treats the incoming left and right as mid and side and decodes them to left/right.
tips: The four continuous controls glide to a new value, so a delay change bends the pitch for a moment.
The delays are part of the sound and are not reported as latency.

name: Pocket Spreader
desc: Stereo widener that delays a side signal and adds it back, with width, separation, a low frequency bypass and a mono bass amount. Rebuilt from FL Studio Mobile's Spreader.

wiki.intro: Pocket Spreader widens the stereo image by delaying a side signal and adding it back, and leaves the part below the Low bypass frequency out of the widening. It runs the same engine as Spreader behind FL Studio Mobile's control ranges. It is the engine that FL Studio Mobile projects (.flm) load their Spreader module on, with every value copied as it is, and it can also be added to any mixer slot.
controls: Reads 0.0 to 2.0. Up to 1.0 it lengthens the delay of the widening signal, up to about 6.35 ms. Above 1.0 the delay stays at its maximum and only the level of the widening signal rises.
Frequency below which the signal is split off from the widening, 10 Hz to 10 kHz.
How much of the part below the Low bypass frequency is output in mono. Continuous, reads 0 to 100.
Level of the side signal, -100 % to +100 %. Reads Original in the centre. At -100 % the side signal is removed, at +100 % it is doubled.
tips: The effect reports a latency of about 6.35 ms (280 samples at 44.1 kHz) to the delay compensation.
The controls are smoothed, so the effect fades in over a few milliseconds after a reset.

name: Pocket Stereoizer
desc: Makes a stereo image from the mono sum with a filtered short delay, plus a left/right delay and a pan. Rebuilt from FL Studio Mobile's Stereoizer.

wiki.intro: Pocket Stereoizer widens a sound by delaying and filtering its mono sum, then adding the result to the left channel and subtracting it from the right. Use it on mono or narrow sources. It is the engine that FL Studio Mobile projects (.flm) load their Stereoizer module on, with every value copied as it is, and it can also be added to any mixer slot.
controls: Level of the added signal, on a square law. Reads 0 to 100. Near 0 the widening is switched off.
Delay of the mono sum, from 0.5 ms to 50 ms on a cubic law. Reads 0 to 100.
One-pole filter on the delayed signal. Reads -100 % to +100 %. Below the centre it is a low-pass, above the centre a high-pass.
Delays one side by up to 25 ms on a cubic law. Reads -100 % to +100 %. Left of centre delays the left channel, right of centre delays the right channel.
Linear balance, -100 % to +100 %. Lowers the opposite side and glides to a new value.
tips: The added signal has opposite sign on the two sides, so with L/R delay and Pan in the centre it cancels when the output is summed to mono.

name: Pocket Tape Delay
desc: Tape-style delay with time, feedback, a left and right time offset and mix. Changing the time bends the pitch of the echoes. Rebuilt from FL Studio Mobile's Tape Delay.

wiki.intro: Pocket Tape Delay models one tape loop per side. The tape speed glides to a new delay time, so the echoes change pitch while Time moves. It is the engine that FL Studio Mobile projects (.flm) load their Tape Delay module on, and it can also be added to any mixer slot.
controls: Delay time, 0 to 1000 ms. It is not synced to the tempo.
Feedback, 0 to 100%. How much of the echo goes back onto the tape.
Bipolar, -100 to 100%. Shortens the delay of one side by up to half. Negative values shorten the left side, positive values the right side.
Level of the echoes, 0 to 100%. The echoes are added to the dry signal.
tips: The echo level is Mix times Fdbk, so with Fdbk at 0 no echo is heard at any Mix setting.
Move Time while sound is playing for a tape speed effect.

name: Pocket Tape Stop
desc: Slows the sound down to a stop like a tape machine and speeds it up again, with free or tempo-synced stop and start times, a Play switch and a curve for the speed. Rebuilt from FL Studio Mobile's Tape Stop.

wiki.intro: Pocket Tape Stop records its input all the time. Turning Play off plays the recording back at a falling speed until it stops, and turning Play on again speeds it up and fades back to the live input over the last 0.1 s. Automate Play to place the stops in a song. It is the engine that FL Studio Mobile projects (.flm) load their Tape Stop module on, with every value copied as it is, and it can also be added to any mixer slot. Its editor is a page of plain knobs.
controls: Length of the slowdown when Sync is off, up to 5 s. Shown in ms below one second. The bottom of the range reads Off: the tape stops within 5 ms.
Length of the speed-up when Sync is off, up to 5 s.
Length of the slowdown when Sync is on: Off, 1/4 beat, 3/8 beat, 1/2 beat, 3/4 beat, 1 beat, 2, 4, 8 or 16 beats.
Length of the speed-up when Sync is on, with the same steps.
On plays the input. Off stops the tape. Each change starts a slowdown or a speed-up.
Shape of the speed curve, -100% to +100%.
On uses the synced times at the song tempo, Off the times in seconds.
tips: It only works while the song plays. With the song stopped the audio passes through and nothing is recorded.
When the tape has stopped, the output fades to silence until Play is turned on again.
Turning Play back on during a slowdown speeds up from the speed it had reached.

name: Pocket Trance Delay
desc: Tempo-synced delay with five beat lengths, Stereo, Ping-Pong and Mirror modes, feedback, a low-pass or high-pass filter in the loop and a mix control. Rebuilt from FL Studio Mobile's Trance Delay.

wiki.intro: Pocket Trance Delay is a delay locked to the song tempo. The echoes are added to the dry signal, which always stays at full level. It is the engine that FL Studio Mobile projects (.flm) load their Trance Delay module on, and it can also be added to any mixer slot.
controls: Delay time as a part of a beat. The longest delay is 2 seconds.

Selects the mode. Stereo runs one delay line per side. Ping-Pong crosses the lines so the echoes alternate between the sides. Mirror uses lines of twice the length and delays the left input by the delay time.
Shown in Ping-Pong mode only, 0 to 100. Balance of the input that feeds the delay lines.
How much of each echo is fed back. The first echo is already scaled by this amount, so at 0 there are no echoes.
Bipolar filter in the feedback loop. Open at the centre, a low-pass below it and a gentle high-pass above it.
Level of the echoes. The slider follows a square law.
tips: Changing the time or the mode clears the delay lines, so the echoes stop and start again.
A stored Dry pan setting makes Input Pan also pan the dry signal in Ping-Pong mode. It is read from the .flm project and has no control in the editor.

name: Pocket Tremolo
desc: Tremolo and auto-pan with a free or tempo-synced rate, minimum and maximum gain, a stereo offset and four controls for the wave shape. Rebuilt from FL Studio Mobile's Tremolo.

wiki.intro: Pocket Tremolo moves the level of a sound between a minimum and a maximum gain with an LFO. A phase offset between left and right turns it into an auto-pan. It is the engine that FL Studio Mobile projects (.flm) load their Tremolo module on, with every value copied as it is, and it can also be added to any mixer slot.
controls: Speed of the LFO when Sync is off, 0.1 Hz to 20 Hz.
Length of the LFO cycle when Sync is on: 1/8, 1/4, 3/8, 1/2, 3/4, beat, 2 beats, 4 beats, 8 beats or 16 beats.
Highest gain of the cycle, 0 to 100 %. Setting it below Amount min pulls the minimum down with it.
Lowest gain of the cycle, 0 to 100 %. Setting it above Amount max pushes the maximum up with it.
Start phase of the LFO for both channels, 0 to 360.
Extra phase for the right channel, 0 to 360. At 180 the two sides move in opposite directions.
On uses Rate sync and follows the song position. Off uses Rate.
Bends the wave with an exponent. Reads 0 to 100, 50 leaves it unbent.
Blend between the straight-line wave (0) and its rounded, sine-like version (100).
Position of the peak inside the cycle. Reads -100 to +100, 0 is a symmetric rise and fall.
Share of the cycle spent near the maximum against the minimum. Reads 0 to 100, 50 is even.
tips: The gain swing reaches 99 % of the range between Amount min and Amount max.
The gain is smoothed by a filter at about 333 Hz, so hard-edged shapes do not click.

name: Pocket Waveshaper
desc: Waveshaping distortion with seven curves, X and Y shape controls, an LFO, input filters, a three-band tone section, auto-gain and mix. Rebuilt from FL Studio Mobile's Waveshaper.

wiki.intro: Pocket Waveshaper distorts a sound by passing it through one of seven curves. Two filters come before the curve and a three-band tone section after it, and an LFO can move the two shape controls. It is the engine that FL Studio Mobile projects (.flm) load their Waveshaper module on, with every value copied as it is, and it can also be added to any mixer slot.
controls: The curve: Soft, Tanh, Crossover, Fold, Octaver, Rectify or CrossFold.
On matches the level of the shaped signal to the input level, with a slow follower.
Two parameters of the selected curve. What they change depends on the shape. Read 0 to 100.
Gain into the curve, 0 dB to 40 dB. Reads 0 to 100.
Gain of the shaped signal, -18 dB to +18 dB.
Adds an offset of opposite sign to the left and right signal before the curve, so the two sides distort differently. Fourth-power law, reads 0 to 100.
Equal-power blend of dry and shaped signal. Reads 0 to 100.
Two-pole filters before the curve, each 20 Hz to 20 kHz.
Bell band at 100 Hz after the curve. Reads -18 dB to +18 dB.
Bell band after the curve, 500 Hz to 2 kHz. Gain reads -18 dB to +18 dB.
High shelf at 3.3 kHz after the curve. Reads -18 dB to +18 dB.
On uses LFO rate and follows the song position. Off uses LFO rate free.
Length of the LFO cycle when LFO sync is on: 1/8, 1/4, 3/8, 1/2, 3/4, beat, 2 beats, bar, 2 bars or 4 bars.
Speed of the LFO when LFO sync is off, 0.02 Hz to 9.92 Hz on a cubic law.
LFO to X / LFO to Y
How far the LFO moves X and Y, 0 to 100 %. At 100 % it moves a control by half of its range each way.
tips: The LFO and the X and Y values are updated once per song tick (1/96 of a beat), not per sample.
A DC filter after the curve removes the offset that asymmetric shapes and Stereo spread create.

name: Pocket Wow & Flutter
desc: Tape-style pitch wobble from a modulated delay: a slow wow, a fast flutter and a random change of the wow rate, free or tempo synced. Rebuilt from FL Studio Mobile's Wow & Flutter.

wiki.intro: Pocket Wow & Flutter passes the sound through a delay whose length is moved by two sine LFOs, which bends the pitch like an unsteady tape. The output is fully wet, there is no mix control. It is the engine that FL Studio Mobile projects (.flm) load their Wow & Flutter module on, with every value copied as it is, and it can also be added to any mixer slot.
controls: Speed of the slow LFO when Sync is off, 0.1 Hz to 5 Hz.
Length of the wow cycle when Sync is on: 1/8, 1/4, 3/8, 1/2, 3/4, beat, 2 beats, 4 beats, 8 beats or 16 beats.
Depth of the wow, 0 to 100 % on an exponential law. At 100 % the delay swings over up to 142 ms.
Speed of the fast LFO when Sync is off, 5 Hz to 20 Hz.
Length of the flutter cycle when Sync is on, same list as Wow sync.
Depth of the flutter, 0 to 100 %. It adds up to 3 ms on top of the wow delay.
On locks both LFOs to the tempo and uses the two sync lengths. Off uses the two rates in Hz.
How often a new wow speed is picked, 0.1 Hz to 10 Hz.
Sets the time between picks as a tempo length, same list as Wow sync.
Size of the window the random pick is taken from, 0 to 100 %. With Sync off the window is around Wow rate, with Sync on it is around the Wow sync step. At 0 % the wow speed does not change.
tips: Random rate and Random sync set the same timer. The one moved last wins, whatever Sync is set to.
The delay grows with Wow amount and is not reported as latency, so high amounts make the track late as well as wobbly.
With Sync on and Random amount at 0 % the wow follows the song position.

name: Prism Multiband
desc: Four-band dynamics processor. Each band can compress or expand, downward or upward, with its own attack, release, knee and level, drawn over a spectrum.

wiki.intro: Prism Multiband is a native LYNX SHARE effect for a mixer insert. It splits the signal into four bands and applies compression or expansion to each. A band that is not changing the gain leaves the signal untouched, so the effect is transparent at rest.
controls: Drag a handle up or down to set its level, and left or right to move the band.
Three crossovers between the four bands, with 12, 24 or 48 dB per octave slopes.
Solo and mute for each band.
Switch at the top right of the display.
Menu in the bottom bar (Dynamic in the picture).
Button that picks what the spectrum shows, such as Pre + Post.
tips: Whether a band compresses or expands, and downward or upward, follows the sign of its range.
The documented per-band settings are threshold, ratio, knee, attack and release as a percentage, level, solo and on.

name: Quell Denoiser
desc: One-knob noise suppressor with six bands, each with a downward expander that follows the Amount control. Listen plays back what is being removed.

wiki.intro: Quell Denoiser is a native LYNX SHARE effect for a mixer insert. It reduces steady broadband noise such as hiss with a single Amount control. Internally the signal is split into six phase-coherent bands, each with a soft-knee downward expander.
controls: Fader from 0 to 100. Sets the threshold, depth and trim of every band together.
Plays what is taken away instead of the result.
Level meter on the left with a held reduction read-out below it.
Switches from the six-band expander to the matched engine: cuts on seven octave bands, with no latency. Off by default.

Matched engine only. Measured lets each band follow the noise floor it measures over about a second, so steady noise is taken down further. It costs some CPU. The switch is shown only for an instance from a project or preset saved before 0.1.27, which loads on Classic and sounds as before. Once you switch to Measured it is hidden. New instances use Measured.
tips: Use Listen while raising Amount: if you start to hear the wanted signal in it, back off.
The expanders open fast and close more slowly, and both channels are linked.

name: Reeverb 2
desc: Algorithmic reverb with room size, diffusion, decay, damping, early reflections and modulation. It runs the engine of the FL Studio original.

wiki.intro: Reeverb 2 is an algorithmic reverb for a mixer insert, covering small rooms to large halls. It runs FL Studio's engine and opens the settings of a Fruity Reeverb 2 when a .flp project is imported. The animated frames on the left show the room.
controls: Low cut and high cut on the reverb input.
Selects mid or side as the input to the reverb.
Depth and speed of the modulation.
Bass multiplier and the crossover below which it applies.
Levels of the dry signal, the early reflections and the reverb tail.
tips: The engine matches FL's on all 293 states tested, from 22.05 to 96 kHz.

name: Reeverb
desc: Compact reverb with low and high cut, pre-delay, room size, diffusion, colour, decay and damping. It runs the engine of the FL Studio original.

wiki.intro: Reeverb is a simple reverb for a mixer insert, using the engine of FL Studio's first Fruity Reeverb. It opens the settings of that plugin when a .flp project is imported. Every control is a knob with a read-out beside it.
controls: Delay before the reverb starts, in milliseconds.
Tonal balance of the reverb (Flat in the picture).
Length of the tail, in seconds.
Frequency above which the tail is damped.
tips: The documentation lists its 7 demo states as matching FL's exactly.

name: Reverb
desc: LYNX SHARE's own reverb with room size, damping, width, pre-delay, low and high cut, and separate dry and wet levels, plus a decay curve display.

wiki.intro: Reverb is LYNX SHARE's own reverb, available on every mixer insert. The display at the top draws the decay curve and shows the decay time. The controls are grouped as Space, Tone and Mix.
controls: Delay before the reverb starts, in milliseconds.
Room size, shown as a percentage.
How quickly the tail loses its highs, shown as a percentage.
tips: The decay time is shown in the top right corner of the display, and it follows Size and Damping.

name: Rhythmic envelope
desc: Gain envelope drawn as up to twelve points over a looped length in beats and locked to the song. It gives rhythmic pumping or gating.

wiki.intro: Rhythmic envelope multiplies the level of an insert by a curve of up to twelve points. The curve spans a period in beats, loops and follows the song position. The top of the editor draws the curve.
controls: Length of the looped curve in beats, up to 64.
Number of points in use, 0 to 12. With 0 points the gain stays at unity.
Where each point sits in the period, from its start to its end.
Gain at each point, from silence to unity.
Bipolar. Bends the segment that leads to the point. In the centre the segment is a straight line.
Switch between the two pages of six points.
Leaves the audio untouched and provides the curve value as a live automation source.
tips: Before the first point the level is that of the first point, and after the last point the level of the last point is held until the period ends.
Use Control only when the curve should drive another parameter instead of the level.

name: Ridge Strip
desc: Console-style channel strip with high and low pass filters, a four-band equaliser with two curve families, a compressor and a gate or expander.

wiki.intro: Ridge Strip is a native LYNX SHARE channel strip for a mixer insert. It combines filters, equaliser and dynamics in one window, with a curve and gain meters in the middle.
controls: Filters with 18 dB per octave and 12 dB per octave slopes.
Four equaliser bands with gain and frequency. The two mid bands also have Q.
Switch on HF and LF that turns the shelf into a bell.
Curve families. Brown has constant Q and plain shelves, Black has proportional Q and shelves with the overshoot dip.
Threshold, ratio, release and mix, with Fast attack and Auto make-up switches.
Range, threshold and release, with a Fast switch and a Gate or Expand choice.
Switch the dynamics section and the equaliser on or off.
Order of the equaliser and the dynamics.
Sends the filters to the side chain.
Input trim, output fader and a phase switch.
Section with a mode menu, drive, input, trim and mix.
tips: Gain reduction meters for the compressor and the expander sit at the bottom right.

name: Sentry Gate
desc: Gate and expander with Classic, Clean, Vocal, Guitar and Upward styles, plus hold, knee, look-ahead and side-chain filters, drawn over a level display.

wiki.intro: Sentry Gate is a native LYNX SHARE gate and expander for a mixer insert. It cuts the signal below a threshold, from a gentle expansion to a full gate depending on ratio and range. The display shows the transfer curve over the live level.
controls: Classic, Clean, Vocal, Guitar or Upward. Changes how the gate opens and closes.
Level at which the gate opens, from -60 dB to 0 dB.
From 1:1 up to 100:1, expander to gate.
How far the signal is reduced, from 0 to 100 dB.
Opening time, from 0 ms to 1 s.
Closing time, from 0 ms to 5 s.
How long the gate stays open, from 0 to 250 ms.
Softness of the threshold, from 0 to 30 dB.
From 0 to 10 ms, with an On switch.
Internal or external, with a high pass and a low pass filter.
Menu in the bottom bar (Left/Right in the picture).
Oversampling menu and input and output gain.
Classic or Measured. Measured adds the Vocal style's noise reduction; the other styles ignore it. Projects saved before 0.1.26 load on Classic.

Level or Transient. Level is the gate as before. Transient is a drum gate: a hit above the threshold opens it fully, it stays open for Hold and closes over Release along the chosen shape, whatever the level does meanwhile. Ratio, Knee and the style's curve are not used in Transient. Level by default.
Transient only. The shape of the release: Smooth, Mid or Sharp.
Transient only. 1 to 10, default 5. Higher values open the gate on smaller hits.
tips: Turning Lookahead on adds 10 ms of latency.

name: Shell Channel
desc: Drum channel strip with a gate, a transient shaper, low and high frequency enhancers and a listen-mic compressor, in an order you can rearrange.

wiki.intro: Shell Channel is LYNX SHARE's own drum channel strip for a mixer insert. Five sections each have a power switch, and the chevrons at the bottom set the processing order by dragging them. It reports 4.1 ms of latency.
controls: Open, Close, Range, Hold, Attack and Release, with a meter beside it.
Gain, Speed and Amount, with Invert and Listen buttons.
Comp, Makeup gain and Mix, with a Narrow band button.
Gain at the left, with a level meter.
Dry and wet balance and output gain at the right, with a level meter.
tips: There are 120 possible process orders, set by dragging the chevrons at the bottom.

name: Spiral Echo
desc: Frequency-shifting echo. Every repeat moves by the shift amount, in opposite directions on the left and right in stereo, with filters in the feedback loop.

wiki.intro: Spiral Echo is a native LYNX SHARE delay for a mixer insert. Each repeat is shifted in frequency a little more than the last, which makes the echoes climb or fall instead of simply repeating. In stereo the right side hears each repeat with the opposite shift.
controls: Delay time, from 0.01 ms to 1000 ms.
Frequency shift added on every repeat, up to plus or minus 1 kHz.
How much of the output returns to the input.
Low cut in the feedback loop.
High cut in the feedback loop.
Free, or one of 23 tempo divisions.

Measured uses the measured feedback loop: its filters, an added all-pass, the limiter and the glide when the delay time changes. It uses a little less CPU. New instances start on Measured. Projects and presets saved before 0.1.27 load on Classic and sound as before.
tips: The feedback loop gain is 1.5 times the knob, and it is soft-limited, so high settings do not run away.

name: Spreader
desc: Stereo widener with spread and separation controls, a low frequency bypass and a mono switch, with a picture of the stereo image.

wiki.intro: Spreader widens the stereo image by delaying a side signal and adding it back. The part of the signal below the LF bypass frequency is left out of the widening. It loads the settings of the FL Studio Spreader from an imported .flp project. The display draws the stereo field.
controls: Delay of the side signal, up to about 6.35 ms.
Bipolar. How much of the delayed side signal is added, and with which sign.
Frequency below which the signal is split off from the widening. The first half of the knob covers up to 500 Hz and the second half 500 Hz to 10 kHz.
Mono bass. Outputs the part below the LF bypass frequency in mono.
tips: The controls are smoothed, so the effect fades in over about 2 ms after a reset.

name: Squeeze
desc: Coarsens the signal in steps, with an optional filter, a dry/wet mix and an output volume. Used for bit-crush style grit.

wiki.intro: Squeeze is an insert effect that quantises the signal to a reduced number of levels, can gate it periodically with its Puncher section and can filter it before or after. It loads the settings of Fruity Squeeze from an imported .flp project.
controls: Number of levels the signal is rounded to. Turning it up lowers the count from 32768 towards 1, so the steps get coarser.
Length, in samples, of the part of each Puncher cycle that passes unchanged.
Length, in samples, of the part of each cycle that is scaled by the Puncher Amount. At 0 the Puncher is off.
Ties Impact to Preserve: free, equal, double or half.
Gain applied during the Impact part of the cycle, from silence to unity.
Low-pass, high-pass, band-pass, notch or peak.
Filter cutoff, on a logarithmic scale starting at 50 Hz.
Places the filter before the quantiser and Puncher, or after them.
Balance between the dry and the processed signal.
Output level, applied to the dry and processed signal together.
tips: The Puncher is a periodic gate that does not follow the signal: it alternates Preserve samples at full level with Impact samples at the Amount gain.
A block of pure silence passes through unchanged.
The filter is designed for 44.1 kHz, so at other project sample rates its real cutoff scales with the rate.

name: Stereo Enhancer
desc: Pan, volume, stereo separation and phase offset in one small effect, with an option to invert. Used to widen or narrow a stereo signal.

wiki.intro: Stereo Enhancer changes the stereo image of the track it sits on. Add it to a mixer insert to widen a pad or to shift a mix slightly. The docs list it as an exact engine with import from FL Studio projects.
controls: Moves the signal left or right.
Amount of separation between the two channels.
Applies the effects after the enhancer stage.
tips: A phase offset delay set before a sample rate change keeps its old length in FL Studio; LYNX SHARE uses the current rate.

name: Stereo Shaper
desc: A stereo matrix that sets how much of each input side reaches left and right, with delay and phase between the channels.

wiki.intro: Stereo Shaper is a mixer matrix that sets how much of each input side reaches each output side, followed or preceded by a delay and a phase stage on one channel. It loads the settings of Fruity Stereo Shaper from an imported .flp project.
controls: How much of the right input goes to the left output. The fader is bipolar, so the signal can be added inverted.
Level of the left input in the left output. The default position is unity and the top of the range is 4 times (+12 dB).
Level of the right input in the right output, with the same range as Left.
How much of the left input goes to the right output.
Delays one channel by up to 500 ms: the right channel when turned right, the left channel when turned left.
Runs one channel through an all-pass filter, which shifts its phase: the right channel when turned right, the left when turned left.
Runs the delay and phase stages before the matrix or after it.
Outputs the input minus the output instead of the processed signal.
tips: With Left and Right at unity and both cross faders at zero the matrix passes the signal unchanged.
Changing Delay resizes the delay line and clears it.

name: Strike Shaper
desc: Level-independent transient designer. Attack and Sustain knobs shape hits and tails without a threshold, with output gain, parallel mix, a soft-clip guard and a detector high-pass.

wiki.intro: Strike Shaper is LYNX's own transient designer. It compares two envelopes of the same signal and sets the gain from their ratio, so it reacts the same way to quiet and loud hits and needs no threshold. Use Attack to make onsets harder or softer and Sustain to lengthen or shorten tails. It has no look-ahead and adds no latency.
controls: Raises or lowers the onset of each hit, -15 dB to +15 dB, on a printed scale that is finer near 0 dB.
Raises or lowers the decaying tail after each hit, -24 dB to +24 dB.
Output level, -20 dB to +6 dB, with 0 dB at the top of the knob.
Switches the effect on or off. The ON key and the Power lamp do the same thing.
On uses one detector and one gain for both channels, so the stereo image does not move. Off shapes left and right separately.
High-pass filter on the detector only, Off or 20 Hz to 1 kHz. It keeps low frequencies from triggering the shaping and does not filter the audio.
Soft clipper on the output. It leaves the signal alone below about -3 dBFS and never lets it pass 0 dBFS.
Blend between the dry and the shaped signal, 0 to 100 %, for parallel processing. Output gain and Guard come after it.
SIG lights when there is input signal. OVL lights when the output peak reaches full scale.
Two rows of lamps show how far each gain moves, live. Blue to the left is a cut, red to the right is a boost, with steps at 1, 3, 6, 10 and 15 dB.
tips: With Attack and Sustain at 0 dB, Mix at 100 % and Output gain at 0 dB the signal passes unchanged.
Large Attack boosts can add up to +15 dB on a hit. Switch Guard on or lower Output gain if the OVL lamp lights.
Hover a knob to read its value. Right-click a knob for its value menu.

name: Transient Processor
desc: Shapes the attack and release of a sound with separate shape controls, a gain, a drive and a frequency split.

wiki.intro: Transient Processor raises or lowers the attack and the release part of a sound. It splits the signal at a frequency, detects transients in the part above the split and applies the gain change there. It loads the settings of the FL Studio Transient Processor from an imported .flp project.
controls: Bipolar. Right of centre makes the onsets louder, left of centre softens them.
Slider under Attack with three positions, Sharp, Mid and Slow, that set how fast the attack detector follows the signal.
Bipolar. Right of centre lifts the tail after each hit, left of centre lowers it.
Slider under Release with three positions, Sharp, Mid and Slow, that set the timing of the release detector.
Drives the processed band into a soft saturation stage and divides the level back out afterwards.
Frequency of the split, 5 Hz to 1000 Hz. Only the part above it is processed.
Balance between the unprocessed low part and the processed high part. Both are at full level in the centre.
Output gain, from -9 dB to +9 dB.
Off passes the input through unchanged.
tips: The view under the controls shows the gain, and the meters at the sides show input and output.
About 1.5 seconds after the input goes silent the effect stops processing and passes the signal through until sound returns.

name: Transmitter
desc: Splits a sound into transient and sustain parts and treats each with its own level, tilt and saturation, diffusion, bounce or delay.

wiki.intro: Transmitter detects the transient and the sustain of the incoming signal and gives each part its own level, tilt and effect. Add it to an insert to rebalance the attack and tail of drums, plucks or loops. It imports the 42 controls of the FL Studio plugin of the same name.
controls: Detection mode: Smooth, Balanced or Dense.
Chooses the effect on the transient part, for example saturation.
Chooses the effect on the sustain part, for example diffusion.
Per effect controls for each of the two parts.
tips: Each part has an On switch, so you can process only the transient or only the sustain.
Each part also has a Send to button.

name: Transporter
desc: Detects transients and loops short slices of the input in two loops, with reverse and octave jumps, spread and auto-pan.

wiki.intro: Transporter is a transient looper: an eight-band detector triggers loops A and B that replay the input. Add it to an insert for stutters and glitch repeats.
controls: Chance that a loop plays backwards.
Spread and auto-pan of the loops.
Ratio between loop A and loop B.
Selects the loop mode, such as Auto, Bouncing, Adaptive or Tempo.
tips: Tempo mode follows the project tempo; the Tempo length and Tempo trigger controls set it.
Send to routes the loop to another insert.

name: Tuner
desc: Shows the note and the tuning of the incoming audio, in a basic view or as a dial, with an adjustable reference pitch.

wiki.intro: Tuner reads the pitch of the incoming audio and shows the note name and octave. Put it on an insert and play one note at a time to tune an instrument or a sample.
controls: How quickly the display follows the signal.
Off or On, for low notes.
tips: It does not change the sound.

name: Utility
desc: Gain, balance and a four-way channel matrix for the left and right inputs. Used for simple level and channel fixes.

wiki.intro: Utility is a small tool for levels and channel routing. Add it to an insert to change the gain, shift the balance or swap and mix the channels.
tips: Setting L -> R and R -> L high and the others low swaps the channels.

name: Vintage Chorus
desc: A two-delay chorus with an LFO, feedback, high-pass filter on the wet signal, hiss and a noise gate.

wiki.intro: Vintage Chorus thickens a sound with two modulated delays. Add it to an insert for chorus on guitars, keys or pads. It imports the settings of the FL Studio plugin of the same name, which the docs list as exact.
controls: Phase between the left and right LFO.
Delay time of the first chorus.
Delay time of the second chorus.
High-pass frequency of the wet signal.
tips: Mono input sums the input before the chorus.

name: Vintage Phaser
desc: A phaser with a frequency range, feedback, LFO and tempo sync, plus a built-in delay section and input colouring.

wiki.intro: Vintage Phaser sweeps a phaser between a minimum and a maximum frequency with an LFO, and adds a delay, a noise generator with a gate and a mono input switch. The Main page has the Phasing, Modulation, Delay and Levels sections, the Advanced page holds the remaining engine controls. It loads the settings of the FL Studio Vintage Phaser from an imported .flp project.
controls: The two ends of the sweep, each from 1.25 Hz to 20.48 kHz. The sweep between them is exponential.
Amount of phaser feedback. Invert feedback on the Advanced page flips its sign.
Switches the LFO off and holds the phaser at the Manual freq. set on the Advanced page.
LFO rate. With T on, the rate is a length in steps of the project tempo and the LFO follows the song position.
Where in its cycle the LFO starts. It is used only with tempo sync.
Offsets the LFO of the right channel against the left.
Bends the LFO waveform. At zero it has no effect.
Delay time, up to one second, or in steps of 1/192 beat with T on. The LED in the section title switches the delay on.
Mix is the level of the delayed signal, Stereo distributes the delayed and direct signals between left and right, and Feedback is the amount fed back.
Low-pass (320 Hz to 20.48 kHz) and high-pass (20 Hz to 20.48 kHz) filters in the delay's feedback path.
Crossfades between delay times over 100 ms when Time changes, instead of gliding the pitch.
Noise adds filtered noise after the phaser. Noise gate closes the output when the signal falls under a threshold tied to the noise level.
Sums left and right before the effect.
Balance between the dry and the phased signal.
tips: Advanced page: Drive sets the saturation of the V2 engine from -15 dB to +15 dB, Colour gain and Colour freq. set a low shelf before the phaser, Input HP and Feedback HP are high-pass filters from 5 Hz to 200 Hz.
Rate 1 and Rate 2 on the Advanced page set the two ends of the range that the Speed fader covers.
Min may be set above Max: the two values are sorted before use.

name: Visualizer
desc: Draws moving graphics from the audio in layers, with bars, rays, particles and images. It can export video and import FL visualiser presets.

wiki.intro: Visualizer renders layered graphics that react to the sound passing through it. Add it to the master or any insert, build a scene from layers and export it as video. An FL Studio ZGameEditor Visualizer preset can be imported; its effects are approximated by layers.
controls: How strongly the graphics react to the audio.
Level at which a beat is detected.
How many bars, rays, particles or rings.
tips: Some layers need the GPU and are drawn simplified without it.

name: Vocoder
desc: A band vocoder that imposes the spectrum of a modulator on a carrier, with band count, filter order, formant and envelope controls.

wiki.intro: Vocoder splits a modulator into 4 to 128 frequency bands, follows the level of each band and applies those levels to the same bands of a carrier. The left input is the modulator and the right input the carrier, and the output is mono on both sides. It loads the settings of Fruity Vocoder from an imported .flp project.
controls: Number of bands: 4, 8, 16, 32, 64 or 128. Changing it resets the per-band levels.
Number of equal band-pass filters in series per band: 1, 2 or 3.
Lowest and highest frequency covered by the bands.
How the band edges are spread between Min and Max.
Width of each band-pass filter, 5 to 200 percent.
Shifts the carrier bands against the modulator bands, from -1200 to +1200 cents.
Mirrors the band order of the carrier, so low modulator bands drive high carrier bands.
Attack and release time of the band envelope followers, 10 ms to 1000 ms each.
Stops the analysis and keeps the current band levels.
Levels of the unprocessed modulator, the unprocessed carrier and the vocoded signal in the output.
Listen switch: outputs the modulator alone, the carrier alone, or the mix set by the three faders.
Swaps which input side is the modulator and which is the carrier.
tips: The Side inputs switch in the plugin menu takes the modulator from side input 1 and the carrier from side input 2, each summed to mono, instead of the left and right sides of the insert.
The band display shows the levels of the analysis bands.

name: Vocodex
desc: A vocoder built from the saved state of the FL Studio plugin, with 13 per-band maps, followers, a gate and unison. Parts need an FL Studio installation.

name: Voice Shift
desc: Shifts pitch and formant of a voice or instrument, with a link between them, a drive stage, a mix and optional MIDI control.

wiki.intro: Voice Shift is a pitch and formant shifter for one voice or one monophonic line. It detects pitches between 70 Hz and 1000 Hz. It reports its latency for delay compensation and delays the dry signal to match.
controls: Makes the formants follow the pitch. Formant then works as an offset.
Transpose shifts by the Pitch amount. Quantize also moves the voice to the nearest semitone at once. Robot sings one fixed note, C4 at Pitch 0, which Pitch moves.
A tube-style saturation stage on the shifted voice, 0 to 10.
Balance between the dry and the shifted signal.
Off, or a Channel Rack channel whose held notes set the pitch. Transpose and Quantize shift by the distance of the highest held note from C4, and Robot sings that note.

Measured makes the sounds the detector does not find voiced, such as s and t sounds, follow the formant shift (with Link on, the pitch and the formant). The switch is shown only for an instance from a project or preset saved before 0.1.27, which loads on Classic and sounds as before. Once you switch to Measured it is hidden. New instances use Measured.
tips: With Link on, turning Pitch moves the formants with it, like a change of playback speed.

name: Volume gate
desc: Rhythmic gate with 32 drawable steps that cuts the signal on and off in time with the song, with attack, release and mix controls.

wiki.intro: Volume gate is an effect for a mixer insert slot. It opens and closes the volume in a pattern of 32 steps that you draw. You normally use it for chopped, stuttering or trance-gate style rhythms on pads, chords and whole mixes.
controls: 32 bars, each one sets how much of the sound passes in that step. A new gate starts with half a beat on and half a beat off.
How quickly the volume rises when a step opens. The default is about 2 ms.
How quickly the volume falls when a step closes. The default is about 43 ms.
Balance between the gated and the unprocessed sound.
tips: Draw the steps with the mouse and right-click the bars for ready-made patterns.
Raise Attack and Release for a softer pumping, lower them for hard cuts.

name: Wave Candy
desc: Audio display with oscilloscope, spectrum, spectrogram, peak meter and vectorscope modes. It shows the sound passing through and does not change it.

wiki.intro: Wave Candy is a display that you put on an insert slot to watch the signal. It does not change the sound. A new one starts in spectrum mode, and a Wave Candy from an imported FL Studio project opens in the display mode its saved state shows. The knobs under the display change with the mode.
controls: Auto, Oscilloscope, Spectrum, Spectrogram, Peak meter or Vectorscope. Auto shows the meter in a tall narrow window, the oscilloscope in a wide short one and the spectrum otherwise.
Freezes the display. Middle-clicking the display does the same.
Display gain, -24 dB to +24 dB. All modes.
Oscilloscope. Length of time shown, 2 ms to 500 ms.
Oscilloscope. Draws left and right apart.
Oscilloscope. Locks the trace to the period of the waveform, at a zero crossing.
Spectrum and spectrogram. How fast the spectrum falls or the spectrogram scrolls.
Spectrum and spectrogram. Level range shown, 30 dB to 120 dB.
Spectrum and spectrogram. Frequency scale, from near linear to logarithmic, which shows more low-frequency detail.
Spectrum and spectrogram. From flat to a tilt of +3 dB per octave.
Spectrum and spectrogram. Analysis size, 1024 to 16384 points.
Peak meter. Peak, PPM, RMS, VU or LUFS.
Peak meter. How long a peak is held, 0 to 5 seconds, and how fast the bar falls, 3 to 60 dB per second.
Peak meter. Lowest level shown, -24 dB to -96 dB.
Vectorscope. Length of the trail and size of the dots.
Hue of the trace. All modes.
tips: In Auto mode, make the window tall and narrow to get a meter, or wide and short to get a scope.

name: X-Y Controller
desc: Two-axis pad controller with level, range and tension per axis. Its outputs can be linked to any knob in the project.

wiki.intro: The X-Y Controller sits in an insert slot and makes no sound. It produces two control values, one per axis, that you move with an on-screen pad. Link its outputs to any knob with right-click, Link to internal controller.
controls: Where the target goes, per axis.
The output at the pad's low edge.
The output at the pad's high edge.
Bends the curve from the position to the output.
How fast the target follows the goal.
How quickly the target reaches its speed.
tips: Use the X and Y buttons to switch which axis the knobs edit.
Min and Max can limit a linked knob to a narrower range.

name: X-Y-Z Controller
desc: Three-axis pad controller with level, range, tension and output curve per axis. Its outputs can be linked to any knob in the project.

wiki.intro: The X-Y-Z Controller works like the X-Y Controller with a third axis. It sits in an insert slot, makes no sound and gives three control values that you can link to knobs with right-click, Link to internal controller.
