controls: Where the target goes, per axis.
The output at the pad's low edge.
The output at the pad's high edge.
Bends the curve from the position to the output.
The shape from the position to the output (single curve, stairs, wave and others), per axis.
How fast the target follows the goal.
How quickly the target reaches its speed.
tips: Use the X, Y and Z buttons to switch which axis the knobs edit.

name: 3x Osc
desc: Three-oscillator subtractive synth with several wave shapes per oscillator, detune and phase controls, and an optional high-quality oscillator mode.

wiki.intro: 3x Osc is a built-in generator that you add to the channel rack. It has three oscillators that you mix and tune against each other. It is a plain starting point for basses, leads and simple pads, and it opens the settings of the matching FL Studio plugin when an .flp project is imported.
controls: Choose the wave shape of each oscillator, with an invert button next to them.
Switch for the amplitude modulation option labelled on the panel.
Randomises the start phase of the oscillators.
tips: Random start phases are per instrument in LYNX SHARE, while FL Studio draws them per session.

name: BassDrum
desc: Bass drum generator with pitch, duration, drive, sub bass and click controls, plus a noise layer that uses a wave file. Needs FL Studio data.

wiki.intro: BassDrum is a kick drum generator built on the engine of the FL plugin of the same name: two table oscillators with a falling pitch sweep, a click, an optional noise sample layer, a drive stage and a 42 Hz high-pass. The oscillator table and the noise samples are read at run time from the BassDrum folder of your own FL Studio installation and are not included. A new instance starts from the plugin's preset in your own FL Studio installation, so adding one needs FL Studio installed; otherwise the Add menu lists it as requiring FL Studio. On .flp import without that folder the channel uses a simpler sine and sweep conversion.
controls: Output level. It is multiplied by the note velocity.
Resampling ratio of the whole voice, from a quarter to four times, which shifts pitch and length together. The played key transposes the drum the same way.
Length of the drum's level ramp. At 0 the drum is silent.
The pitch sweep. Base is the frequency it settles on (16 to 256 Hz), Peak is the depth of the sweep above it and Slide is how long the sweep takes.
Var base, Var peak, Var slide
Offsets of the second oscillator's base, peak and slide against the first, from half to double.
Delays the start of the second oscillator, by up to 350 samples of the internal 44.1 kHz rate.
Amount of the saturator after the voice.
Resonance of the 42 Hz high-pass at the output.
Smooths the start of the hit. Higher values give a slower rise.
A click that modulates the oscillator phase at the start. Click is its level, Freq its speed and Cut its start phase.
Shows the noise sample in use, or Needs FL Studio's files when it cannot be read.
Attack, decay and sustain of the noise layer's envelope.
Delays the noise against the oscillators or the oscillators against the noise, by up to 100 ms either way. At the centre both start together.
Playback speed of the noise sample (two octaves down to two octaves up), its low-pass filter and its level.
tips: Note length does not shorten a hit: the note-off is ignored and a voice ends after about 23 ms of silence.
The voice runs at an internal 44.1 kHz and is resampled to the project rate.

name: BeepMap
desc: Image-synthesis generator that turns the columns and rows of a bitmap into sound. Load a picture or paste one and play it with the keyboard.

wiki.intro: BeepMap is a generator for the channel rack that builds its sound from a bitmap. LYNX SHARE runs it on an image-synthesis engine that reuses the 3x Osc voice processor, and it opens the matching FL Studio plugin's settings on .flp import. Only uncompressed 24 and 32-bit BMP files are read.
controls: Option to use the blue channel of the image.
Number of rows of the image, shown next to its size in pixels.
Loads a bitmap from a file.
Pastes a bitmap from the clipboard.
tips: Bitmaps taller than the Max height setting are not fully used.

name: BooBass
desc: Bass instrument with a three-band EQ, built on a bass multisample. Needs FL Studio data, otherwise it falls back to a plain saw tone.

wiki.intro: BooBass is a bass generator for the channel rack, with Bass, Mid and Treble knobs. Needs the multisample of your own FL Studio installation, and the exact engine DLL build; without them it plays a saw approximation. It opens the settings of the matching FL Studio plugin on .flp import.
controls: Low band of the built-in EQ.
Middle band of the built-in EQ.
High band of the built-in EQ.
tips: The panel text says whether the sound was read from your FL Studio installation.

name: Clap
desc: Built-in synthesised clap drum: a band-passed noise burst with three short snaps and a tail. Part of the default drum rack.

name: Dashboard
desc: Control panel that you build from knobs, sliders, buttons, check boxes and XY pads. Each control is an output you can link to any knob.

wiki.intro: Dashboard is a channel with no sound of its own. You lay out your own panel of controls and link each one to a knob elsewhere in the project. It can also send MIDI. FL Studio Dashboards in .flp projects open as the same kind of panel.
controls: Edit mode: drag a control to move it, right-click to rename, resize or delete it.
Adds a knob, slider, button, check box or XY pad.
Sets the port, channel, program and bank the Dashboard sends on.
Per control: sends control change, RPN, NRPN, channel pressure or note messages.
Gives a control its own name.
Changes the size of a control.
tips: A new Dashboard starts with two knobs, Knob 1 and Knob 2.
Each control is an output: right-click a knob, Link to internal controller.

name: Drum Rack
desc: Ableton Live-style drum rack for the Channel Rack: 16 pads in view out of 128, each pad a chain with its own instrument and effects, with choke groups, return chains and sends. Drum Racks in Live sets (.als) open as one Drum Rack.

wiki.intro: Drum Rack is an Instrument Rack whose chains are pads. Each pad receives one note and plays the instrument and effects of its chain. Add it from the plugin picker as Drum Rack. A new Drum Rack shows only the pads and the devices pane, with C1 selected. Drop samples on the pads, or right-click an empty pad to load a sample or an instrument. A Drum Rack in an Ableton Live set (.als) opens as one Drum Rack with its pads, sends and return chains, and Drum Racks are written when you export a Live set.
controls: A 4 x 4 view of the pads, with an overview strip of all 128 above it: click, drag or scroll it to move the view. A filled pad shows its name with M (mute), a play button and S (solo). Drag a pad onto another to swap them. Dropping several samples fills consecutive pads.

Rename (Ctrl+R), Delete, Save as Default Pad, Next Similar (Ctrl+Right), Previous Similar (Ctrl+Left), Save as Similarity Reference (Ctrl+Up), Return to Reference (Ctrl+Down), and the LYNX SHARE items Duplicate and Choke.
M, V, P, C, I-O, S, R, D
The strip on the left shows or hides the macros, the macro variations, the pads, the chain list, the I-O, send and return columns, and the devices pane.
Per pad: the incoming note it answers to (or All), the note it hands its instrument, and its choke group (None or 1 to 16). A pad in a choke group cuts the other pads of that group.
The level each pad sends to each return chain.
Chains of audio effects fed by the sends, shown as a, b and so on, for example "a Mix Bus".
Where a pad's chain goes: Rack Output, or straight into a return chain.
A LYNX SHARE addition under the chain list: velocity and chain-select zones. Pads take the place of key zones.
Up to 16 macro knobs, with Map, Rand and Macro Variations, as in an Instrument Rack.
tips: Slice to Drum Rack in a Sampler channel's menu puts each slice of its sample on a pad. Slice to New MIDI Track... on an audio clip in the Playlist slices it per transient, bar, note value or warp marker into a new Drum Rack channel with a pattern that plays the slices.
In the Clip-launch layout the Piano roll of a Drum Rack channel shows one named row per filled pad. In the Pattern layout it keeps the piano keys, with the pad names on them.
Next Similar and Previous Similar swap the pad's sample using the Browser's Find similar samples index.
On .als export, LYNX SHARE's built-in effects in a chain are not written; Samplers on pads are written as Live's Simpler. No Live has opened an exported Drum Rack yet.

name: Drumaxx
desc: Physical-model drum engine with sixteen pads, each with mallet, membrane, EQ band and velocity sections, plus a master EQ and limiter.

wiki.intro: Drumaxx is a drum generator for the channel rack. It models the mallet and the membrane of each of its 16 pads, shown on two pages (1-8 and 9-16). It opens the settings of the matching FL Studio plugin on .flp import.
controls: Amp, Decay, Noise and Noise RP knobs and a Retrig switch.
Decay, Cutoff, Tension, Phase, Material and Size knobs.
Frequency bands with Freq, Res, Level and further knobs.
Four assignable slots, each with its own knob.
Eight bands from 63 Hz to 8 kHz.
EQ and Limiter switches, Gain and Release knobs.
tips: Drumaxx's own pattern sequencer and separate outputs are not played.
M and S on each pad mute and solo it.

name: Drumpad
desc: Physical-model drum with mallet, membrane, low, mid and high resonator sections and velocity routing, for kicks, toms, snares and hand percussion.

wiki.intro: Drumpad is a single drum voice built from a physical model of a mallet and a membrane, rebuilt from the engine. It opens the settings of the matching FL Studio plugin on .flp import. It has no key tracking and no controller sources.
controls: Amp, Decay, Noise and Noise RP knobs and a Retrig switch.
Decay, Cutoff, Tension, Phase, Material and Size knobs.
Frequency bands with Freq, Res, Level and further knobs.
Four assignable slots, each with its own knob.
tips: Presets include kicks, toms, snares, hand drums, hats, percussion and effects sounds.

name: Envelope Controller
desc: Note-triggered controller with envelope, LFO and key, velocity and modulation maps per output. It makes no sound and drives linked knobs.

wiki.intro: Envelope Controller is a channel with no sound of its own. Each note played on it starts its envelopes, and output k drives the knobs linked to output k. It is imported from FL Studio's Fruity Envelope Controller.
controls: Chooses what to edit: Envelope, LFO, Keyboard mapping, Velocity mapping, Modulation X or Y mapping, or Random.
Envelope attack, decay, sustain and release.
Inputs of the Modulation X and Y maps.
The range of keys the output follows.
Adds the envelope, LFO and maps around the base instead of multiplying them.
Follows the song instead of each note.
Keeps following the base and the Mod maps with no note playing.
tips: Right-click a knob, Link to internal controller, then pick the output.
Alt+click deletes an envelope point, right-click or double-click adds one.

name: FL Keys
desc: Sampled piano, electric piano and keys instrument with decay, release, overdrive, velocity and tuning controls. Needs FL Studio data.

wiki.intro: FL Keys is a sampled keyboard generator built on the engine of the FL plugin of the same name. It plays a wavetable set such as Grand Piano through an exponential envelope, a soft overdrive, a muffle low-pass, a treble shelf, a tremolo or auto-pan LFO and a short stereo delay. The wavetable files are read from your own FL Studio installation and are not included. A new instance starts from the plugin's preset in your own FL Studio installation, so adding one needs FL Studio installed; otherwise the Add menu lists it as requiring FL Studio. On .flp import, when the engine cannot load the set, the channel falls back to a zoned sampler.
controls: Shows the wavetable set in use, at the top right.
How fast a note decays while the key is held. At minimum, notes do not decay.
How fast a note fades after the key is released.
Depth of the LFO. Above the centre both sides move together (tremolo); below it they move in opposite directions (auto-pan).
Width of the stereo delay and the left to right spread of notes across the keyboard.
Amount of the soft overdrive on each note.
Rate of the tremolo or auto-pan LFO.
Gain of the treble shelf: a cut below the centre, a boost above it.
Stretches the tuning of notes above middle C, more the further they are from it.
Muffle sets the cutoff of the per-note low-pass. The Vel knob beside it sets how much velocity opens that filter.
Hardness shifts which sample group a key plays, by up to six keys either way. The Vel knob beside it adds a shift for velocities above 40.
Velocity sensitivity: the power applied to the note volume.
Detunes keys against each other in a fixed per-key pattern.
tips: Up to 32 voices play at once; beyond that the quietest sounding voice ends first.
Sets marked for resampling, such as Roto Organ, are not resampled when the project rate differs from 44.1 kHz.

name: FL Slayer
desc: Six-string guitar generator with play modes, an effects section, four amp types and four cabinets. Plays and imports FL Slayer channels.

wiki.intro: FL Slayer is a guitar generator built on the engine of the FL plugin of the same name: six strings played in six modes, an effects block, an amp with a three-band EQ and a cabinet. The recorded pick excitations and the chord and glide tables are read at run time from Slayer_Engine.dll in your own FL Studio installation and are not included. A new instance starts from the plugin's preset in your own FL Studio installation, so adding one needs FL Studio installed; otherwise the Add menu lists it as requiring FL Studio. On .flp import, if that file is missing or is a different build, the channel is left unsupported.
controls: Play mode: None, Auto chords, Power chords, Strumming, Solo fixed or Solo dynamic. Auto chords plays the chord of the pressed key across the strings, Power chords plays three notes, Strumming starts each held note one step later, and the Solo modes trigger on the first key and glide to later keys.
The knob sets the step between strings in the chord and strum modes (0 to 10 steps) and the glide time in the Solo modes. With Latch on, released strings keep sounding.
String excitation, 0 to 6. 0 uses noise, 1 to 6 use the recorded picks.
Pickup setting, 0 to 2. 0 switches both pickup taps off, 1 uses two taps with the second at twice the distance and opposite sign, 2 also scales the distance with the string length.
Distance of the pickup tap along the string.
Tone of the pick excitation and how fast the excitation decays.
Lowers the level at which the string signal clips and raises the output gain to match.
Amount of the excitation signal added to the string output as fret noise.
Frequency of the pickup's resonant filter, from 1000 Hz to 7000 Hz.
Damping of the string loop. Higher values also lower the loop gain, so notes ring for a shorter time.
How much note velocity changes the level, and how much it changes the damping.
Bend 2 is the mod wheel value. With Gliss off it sets the vibrato depth. With Gliss on it steps the pitch in semitones and the pitch bend becomes continuous.
Amp type: Clean, Overdrive, Distortion or Fuzz. The cabinet choice sets the amp's output filter, a short comb and the output gain.
Drive is the gain into the amp's shaper. Pres (presence) sets the filter stages around the shaper in Overdrive and Distortion. Fdbk is how much of the amp output is fed back into the strings.
Three-band EQ: low shelf at 500 Hz, peak at 1 kHz and high shelf at 2.5 kHz, each from -10 dB to +10 dB.

Effect menu with 16 entries: Dry, eight that run before the amp (such as Phaser, Tremolo, Wah-wah, Ring mod and Talk box) and seven that run after the cabinet (such as Chorus, Flanger and Dub delay). Par 1 and Par 2 are the two parameters of the chosen effect.
tips: Changing a setting restarts the sounding voices.
The channel's pan, volume and pitch are sent to the engine as FL sends them; the pitch becomes a pitch bend.
Notes can start up to 5 ms differently from an FL render, because the engine's 5 ms control grid starts with playback here.

name: FPC
desc: Pad drum sampler with 32 pads in two banks. Each pad has velocity layers, volume and pan envelopes, cut groups and its own trigger note.

wiki.intro: FPC is a drum sampler with 32 pads in two banks of 16, BANK A and BANK B. Each pad holds one or more sample layers, chosen by velocity. One channel holds the whole kit. It opens the FPC channels of a .flp, and FL's .fst kit presets load onto a channel. Without FL Studio a new FPC is FL's empty kit: 32 pads on FL's default notes with no samples.
controls: Click a pad to select and play it. Drop a sample on a pad to load it.
Switch between the two banks of 16 pads.
Double click to rename the pad.
Click to select the note that triggers the pad.
Level, pan and tuning of the whole pad.
The group this pad cuts and the group that cuts this pad.
Create a new layer or delete the current one. The arrows move a layer up or down.
Spread the velocity range across the layers.
Settings of the selected layer, with its active range: the velocities that play it.
Loads a sample into the selected layer.
How layers that cover the same velocity take turns: Cycle, Random or Random (avoid previous).
Show the pad's volume envelope or pan envelope in the envelope editor.
tips: Left click the waveform to preview the sample.
LYNX SHARE includes no kit samples. Kits come from FL Studio's and your own .fst files, or you load your own samples onto the pads.
An FPC kit preset loads as one channel with the whole kit.

name: Fruit Kick
desc: Small kick drum generator with pitch sweep, amplitude decay, click and distortion knobs. Plays and imports Fruit Kick channels.

wiki.intro: Fruit Kick is a kick drum generator built on the engine of the FL plugin of the same name: a sine wave whose pitch and amplitude fall over time, with an optional waveshaper. A new instance starts from the plugin's preset in your own FL Studio installation when there is one, and from LYNX SHARE's own preset bank otherwise.
controls: Frequency the pitch sweep starts at. The played note shifts it at half rate.
Floor frequency where the pitch sweep stops falling.
How fast the pitch falls from Max to Min.
How fast the amplitude falls. The voice ends when the amplitude drops below 0.0002.
Start phase of the sine wave, 0 to 64, where 64 is a quarter cycle. It sets the click at the onset.
Mix of the waveshaper: as it rises the dry signal falls and the shaped signal rises.
tips: Because the note tracks at half rate, one octave on the keyboard moves the start pitch by half an octave.
Channel envelopes and LFOs for pan, volume, cutoff and resonance are stepped once per sequencer tick.
A note released without a volume envelope ends with a 10 ms fade.

name: Fruity Dance
desc: Silent channel that shows an animated dancer on screen. Notes choose the dance move, and it can load sprite sheets made for Fruity Dance.

wiki.intro: Fruity Dance is LYNX SHARE's own dancer in the role of the FL plugin of the same name; its editor is titled LYNX Dance. It makes no sound; the notes of the channel pick the move. You can drag the dancer to place it and right-click it for its moves. It can also show a sprite sheet made for Fruity Dance in place of LYNX SHARE's dancer.
controls: The dance move used by the channel. With a sprite sheet the list shows the sheet's own moves.
On: a new move starts at the next cycle. Off: it starts at once.
On: the dancer takes mouse clicks. Off: clicks go through it.
Keep the dancer in front of the panels and docked plugins.
Kept for FL Studio projects. It does nothing here: the dancers stay inside the main window.
Scale of the dancer, as a multiplier.
Speed of the animation, as a multiplier.
Motion blending between the frames of a sprite sheet, 0 to 100 percent.
Opacity of the mirror image under the dancer.
Colour of the outfit of LYNX SHARE's dancer.
Reset the dancer to its default position and show it.
Pick a picture in Fruity Dance's format: 8 frames across and one row per move, with a text file of the same name that has one move name per line.
Go back to LYNX SHARE's own dancer.
tips: The editor lists which key plays which move; mirrored versions of the moves sit on a separate range of keys, and further keys hide or show the dancer.
The sprite sheet chooser accepts PNG and JPEG files. If the picture's size does not fit the names file, the editor says Bitmap size is incorrect and keeps the current dancer.

name: Fruity DX10
desc: Two-operator FM synthesizer with an amplitude envelope, two modulator sections and a low-frequency oscillator. Plays and imports Fruity DX10 channels.

wiki.intro: Fruity DX10 is a compact FM generator that runs the engine of the FL plugin of the same name. You add it as a channel and play it from the piano roll. It needs no files from an FL installation.
controls: Waveform selector in the Misc section.
Coarse tuning (Misc section and each modulator).
Attack, decay and release of the amplitude envelope.
Fine tuning and velocity sensitivity of a modulator.
Amount of the signal passed through the first modulator.
Envelope of each modulator: initial level, time, sustain and release.
tips: Each modulator has its own envelope display, so you can see the shape while turning the four envelope knobs.

name: Fruity Granulizer
desc: Granular sampler that plays a sample as a stream of short grains, with grain shape, spacing, pan, depth and speed controls.

wiki.intro: Fruity Granulizer cuts the sample of its channel into grains and plays them back. You add it as a channel, drop a sample on it and play it from the piano roll. It needs no files from an FL installation.
controls: Spacing between positions in the wave; has no effect while Tempo locked is on.
Off, Markers or Auto slice: where the slices come from.
Hold of the first grain of each slice (Transients section).
Match the song tempo; the sample plays once per its length in beats.
What the keys do: Pitch, Percent, Step or Transient.
tips: With Key to set to Pitch the keys transpose; Percent and Step turn them into start points instead.
Slice modes and tempo sync are not played yet in imported projects.

name: Fruity Slicer
desc: Beat slicer that cuts a loop into slices and plays each slice from its own key. Can dump the beat to the piano roll, and has an envelope page.

wiki.intro: Fruity Slicer loads a sample, cuts it into slices and plays one slice per key, starting from the first slice's note. You use it to rearrange drum loops. A note-off ends its slice. The channel window also has an Envelope / instrument page with the envelopes, LFOs and filter of the voices. It reads FL's saved state and needs no files from an FL installation.
controls: Open a sample to slice, or drop one on the window.
Menus for the sample, the slicing and dumping the beat to the piano roll.
Dump the beat to the piano roll right after loading.
Fit the beat to the project tempo right after loading.
Play from a slice to the end of the sample.
Slice fade in and fade out, 0 to 100 ms.
A page of the channel window with the tabs Panning, Volume, Mod X, Mod Y and Pitch.
On each tab: a switch, Delay, Attack, Hold, Decay, Sustain, Release and Amount knobs, three Tension knobs and a Tempo switch.
Sine, Triangle or Pulse shape, Delay, Attack, Amount and Speed knobs, and Tempo and Global switches. Global makes the phase follow the song position.
Mod X and Mod Y knobs and the filter type: Fast LP, LP, BP, HP, BS, LP x2, SVF LP or SVF LP x2.
tips: Double-click the selected slice's name to rename it; each slice can have its own trigger key.
A new Fruity Slicer starts as in FL: Animate and Declick on, Dec at 4 ms and the volume envelope on with a short release.
The envelope page edits FL's own values, so they are kept when the project is exported to a .flp.
Slices that FL stretches in time are not reproduced exactly in imported projects.

name: Fruity Video Player
desc: Plays a video file in step with the song position and can show it in its own window, with start, end and delay settings.

wiki.intro: Fruity Video Player shows a video file inside the project and follows the song position. You add it as a channel and load a file or drop one on the window. Some formats need ffmpeg; the plugin has a button to locate it.
controls: Menu: enable audio, dock the control panel, keep aspect ratio, time display, delay playback, send audio to playlist, locate ffmpeg.
Use the current position as the start or end time.
Play, pause and stop the video.
Mute the sound of the video.
The song position drives the video; when off, the player's own Play and Stop are used.
tips: Double-click the video to show it in its own window.
Use Delay playback to start the video when the song reaches a chosen time.

name: GMS
desc: Subtractive synthesizer with three oscillators, filter, two envelopes, two LFOs, ten effect slots and an output equaliser. Plays and imports GMS channels.

wiki.intro: GMS is a subtractive generator built on the engine of the FL plugin of the same name: three wavetable oscillators plus noise per unison voice, a ladder filter, two envelopes, two LFOs, ten effect slots and an output EQ. The oscillator waves are read at run time from the GMS Synth Waves folder of your own FL Studio installation and are not included; without them the wave screen shows Needs FL Studio's files. A new instance starts from the plugin's preset in your own FL Studio installation, so adding one needs FL Studio installed; otherwise the Add menu lists it as requiring FL Studio. On .flp import without the waves the channel uses a simpler three-oscillator conversion.
controls: Pitch and fine detune of each of the three oscillators.
Mix levels of oscillator 2, oscillator 3 and the noise.
Phase offset of oscillator 2, a switch that retriggers its phase on each note, and a switch that inverts it.
Unison phase with its own Retrig switch, the number of unison voices, their stereo spread and their detune.
Modulation between oscillators: Off, FM or Sync, with a slider for its amount.
Cut (cutoff), Res (resonance) and Kbd (key tracking) faders with LP, BP and HP types.
Atk, Dec and Amt faders, an Inv switch, and a destination: Flt (filter), Mod (modulation amount), Freq or LFO.
Rate and Amt faders, Sync (None, Beat or Bar), Retrig, Inv, Dest (Flt, Mod, Freq or Level) and Shape (Sine, Triangle, Saw or Square).
Amp level and the Att, Dec, Sus and Rel of the level envelope.
Out (master level), Pan, Pitch, and Slide time with its On switch.

Tabs for ten units: Dist, Crush, Flang, Phas, LP, HP, Delay, Verb, Pan and Tranc. Each has an On switch, two main knobs named for the unit (for example Feedback and Filter for Delay), and its own LFO with rate, amount, Shape and Sync.
On switch and five band faders.
tips: Noise, dither and random phases come from a generator owned by each instance, so they differ from any given FL render.

name: GMSynth (FLM)
desc: FL Studio Mobile's GMSynth module as its own voice engine. A channel gets it when you open an FL Studio Mobile project (.flm). It is not in the plugin picker.

wiki.intro: GMSynth (FLM) plays the GMSynth module of FL Studio Mobile projects: two oscillators plus noise, four voices, a filter, envelopes, one LFO and three effect slots. It is not listed in the plugin picker. A channel gets it only when you open a .flm project that uses GMSynth. The wave spectra and the filter table are read at run time from the FL Studio Mobile resources folder of your own FL Studio installation and are not included. If those files are not found when the project is opened, the channel stays on the built-in synth and the import report lists GMSynth as not converted.
controls: What the engine plays: two oscillators, each on one of the module's 29 waves, with pitch, detune, mix and phase for oscillator B, plus a noise level.
Four kinds between the oscillators, AM, FM, SNC and FLT, with an amount and an attack and decay envelope.
Level, pan and a linear attack, decay, sustain and release envelope.
Cutoff, resonance, filter kind and keyboard tracking, with its own attack and decay envelope.
A second envelope with attack, decay, sustain and release, an amount, a destination and velocity.
One tempo-synced LFO with rate, shape, amount and destination.
Up to four detuned copies per voice, with scale, detune and stereo spread.
Transpose, slide time, single voice and auto portamento.
Three slots. DIST, PHAS, F LP, DLY, RVRB and PAN are played. FLNG, F HP, RING and VOX pass the signal through, and the import report lists them when they are switched on.
tips: The settings come from the .flm. LYNX SHARE has no window that edits this module's parameters.
The channel's volume, pan and pitch are applied on top of the module's own.
Noise, dither and the start phases of new voices come from a generator owned by each instance, so they differ from any given FL Studio Mobile render.
The module's pitch bend and mod wheel are not converted.

name: Harmless
desc: Additive synthesizer with timbre sliders, harmonic mask, filter, unison, phaser, harmonizer, LFO and an effects rack. Plays and imports Harmless channels.

wiki.intro: Harmless is an additive generator built on the engine of the FL plugin of the same name: up to 528 sine partials per voice, shaped by colour, timbre EQ, harmonic mask, filter, resonance, phaser and pluck, followed by a rack of chorus, delay, reverb and compressor. It can be added without FL Studio and then starts from LYNX SHARE's own preset bank. The rack's compressor loads its presets from your own FL Studio installation; without them the compressor stays off.
controls: Prot is low harmonics protection. The three Sub faders set the levels of sub harmonics 1, 3 and 4.
Six band faders that raise or lower regions of the timbre.
Base spectrum of the timbre: Saw, Bright saw, Brighter saw, Dephased saw, Dephased saw 2, Squaretooth, Squaretooth 2, Mole, Double saw, Triple saw, Triple saw 2 or Custom.
Twelve faders that set the mask, Mix for how much of it is applied, and LFO for how much the LFO moves that mix.
Trem is stereo tremolo depth. Att, Dec and Rel are the volume envelope. The Vel buttons send velocity to the attack and release velocity to the release.
Decay sets the pluck decay, with a Vel button for velocity. Alt selects the alternate pluck mode, Mask makes the pluck use the harmonic mask, and Rel applies the pluck only on release.
Master volume fader, with a Vel button that sends velocity to volume.

Pitch is master pitch and Det is detuning. Grit is grittiness, Vib is vibrato depth and LFO is the pitch LFO amount. Porta and Mono switch portamento and monophonic play; Time is the portamento time, with a Vel button.

Type picks one of 17 filter shapes, Freq and Width set its frequency and width, and Oct or Hz sets the scale. Env is the filter envelope amount, with Att, Dec, a Slope knob for each and an Adapt switch. LFO and Key set the LFO and key tracking amounts.

Res is the resonance amount, Ofs its offset and Osc the self-oscillation level. Res type picks one of nine shapes with its own Oct or Hz scale. Motion tracks the motion of the filter frequency and Adapt adapts the resonance width.
Order sets the number of unison voices and Type is Classic, Uniform or Blurred. The faders set panning, pitch thickness, phase and variation; Vel sends velocity to the pitch thickness.

Type picks one of ten shapes with an Oct or Hz scale. Mix, Width and Offset set the phaser, the two LFO knobs under them move width and offset, Speed is the motion speed and Key tracks the offset with the key.

Mix, Width and Str (strength), an LFO amount and a Vel button for the width. Type is Oct up, Oct up +1, Oct up +2, Harm up or Harm up +1. Position places it before the filter, before the phaser, before the pluck or last.

Shape picks one of 14 sources, including wave shapes and Filter envelope, Filter frequency, Voice random, Velocity and Pitch. Att is the LFO attack, Speed its speed, and Global switches the global LFO.
Chorus type with Mix; Delay type with Vol (input level), Fb and Time; Reverb type with Wet; Comp type with Level. HQ switches high quality and Threaded switches threaded processing.
tips: Picking a Comp type loads that type's preset from the Harmless folder of the FL Studio installation.
The rack runs in the order chorus, delay, reverb, compressor.
Imported channels the engine cannot read fall back to a simple synth approximation.

name: Harmor
desc: Additive synthesizer with image synthesis, two filters, unison, blur, prism, harmonizer and an effects rack. Plays and imports Harmor channels.

wiki.intro: Harmor is an additive generator built on the engine of the FL plugin of the same name: parts A and B, each with up to 520 sine partials per unison voice, image synthesis and an effects rack. The Add menu marks it as beta. A new instance starts from the plugin's preset in your own FL Studio installation, so adding one needs FL Studio installed; otherwise the Add menu lists it as requiring FL Studio. The rack's compressor also needs its preset from that installation. The editor shows the controls of part A or B plus the Global and FX strips; FL's timbre and filter shape menus, EQ, envelopes and image pages are not editable here.
controls: A and B tabs, A / B slider
The tabs choose which part the panel shows. The slider sets the mix between part A and part B.
Start and Rand set the phase start and phase randomness, Mix is the timbre mix, the three Sub faders set the sub levels, Prot is low harmonics protection and Clip is the clip threshold.
FX is the part's effects send, Vol its volume, Env the amount of the volume envelope and Auto the auto gain.
Mix sets the blur mix, Att and Dec the attack and decay of the time blur, and Harm the harmonic blur.
Depth is the tremolo depth and Gap its stereo gap.
Amt is the prism amount; it works in both directions from the centre.
Amt, Width and Str set the harmonizer amount, width and strength.
Depth and Speed of the vibrato.
Order is 1 to 9, Type is Classic, Blurred, Uniform, Random or Hz, and Alt switches alternate phase. The faders set unison pitch, panning and phase.
Freq and Width set the filter, Env is the envelope amount, Key the key tracking, Oct or Hz the scale and Adapt the adaptive envelope.

Each filter has a resonance with Res (amount), Width, Ofs (offset), an Oct or Hz scale and an Adapt switch for adaptive width. Osc on Filter 1 is self-oscillation. Mix on Filter 2 is the mix between filter 1 and filter 2.
Mix, Width, Ofs (offset), Speed and Key (key tracking), with an Oct, Hz or Harm scale.

Legato and Porta switch legato and portamento, and Vel makes portamento follow velocity. Pre and Post are the volumes before and after the effects, Pitch is the global pitch and LFO the global LFO amount.
X, Y, Z and the pad
Modulation values X, Y and Z. The pad sets X and Y together.
Delay switch with Fdbk (feedback) and Vol; Reverb switch with Wet.
tips: Resynthesis images (a sample analysed when it loads) are ignored: the part plays its timbres instead.
Filter, resonance or phaser shapes the engine does not know switch that stage off.
Random draws use a fixed seed per instance, where FL seeds from the clock.

name: Hat
desc: Built-in hi-hat generator: a short burst of high-passed noise. Add it as a channel and trigger it from the step sequencer.

name: Instrument Rack
desc: Ableton Live-style rack for the Channel Rack. Parallel chains each hold MIDI effects, an instrument and audio effects, with key, velocity and chain-select zones and 16 macros.

wiki.intro: Instrument Rack is a Channel Rack generator built on Patcher in rack mode. Every chain gets the same notes and the outputs of the chains are summed. A chain keeps its devices in this order: MIDI effects, the instrument, audio effects. Add it from the plugin picker as Instrument Rack. Instrument Racks in Ableton Live sets (.als) open as racks, and racks are written back when you export a Live set.
controls: One row per chain with its name, volume, pan, an on switch and S for solo. The chain menu has Add chain, Rename, Duplicate, Delete, Move up and Move down.
The devices of the selected chain. The add menu offers Effects, Plugin effects, Racks, MIDI effects and Instruments. Instruments lists Synth, Instrument Rack and Plugin instruments.
Choose the zone editor: key zones, velocity zones, chain-select zones, or none. Zones run from 0 to 127.

Drag a bar or its ends to set the zone. The upper strip of a bar sets the fades. Key and velocity fades scale the velocity of the notes that enter the chain. The chain-select fade scales the chain's output.
The value the chain-select zones are compared with. A macro can drive it.
Up to 16 knobs, each with a name plate and a value. + and - show more or fewer: 1, 2, 4 and so on up to 16.

Map mode. Each macro gets a Map button that opens a menu of the chains, their devices and parameters, Chain Volume, Chain Pan and Chain Selector. The mapping list shows Macro, Path, Name, Min and Max, with Invert Range and Delete.
Gives every mapped macro a random value. A macro's menu has Exclude Macro from Randomization.
New stores the macro values. A variation has Launch, Overwrite, Rename, Duplicate and Delete. A macro's menu has Exclude Macro from Variations.
LYNX SHARE additions in the variations menu, both off by default: a Morph slider between two variations, and a glide time for a launched variation.
tips: A macro moves each mapped parameter linearly between Min and Max. A parameter belongs to one macro at a time.
The macros, the chain selector and the morph can be automated like the published parameters of a Patcher.

From a Live set a rack keeps its chains, zones, chain volume and pan, macros, variations and nested racks. Third-party plugins in the chains are kept. Live's own devices are dropped and listed in the import report.
A macro mapping on a VST3 plugin parameter in a Live set is not kept. On export, LYNX SHARE built-in devices in a chain are not written; only VST2 and VST3 plugins and nested racks are.

name: Kepler
desc: Analogue-style synthesizer with one oscillator, sub and noise, high-pass and low-pass filters, envelope, chorus and an arpeggiator. Plays and imports Kepler channels.

wiki.intro: Kepler is a polyphonic generator built on the engine of the FL plugin of the same name: eight voices, each with one oscillator (saw, pulse with pulse width modulation, sub square and noise) and a ladder low-pass filter, then a high-pass filter and a chorus, with an LFO, one envelope and an arpeggiator. The LFO shape and noise tables are read at run time from the engine DLL in your own FL Studio installation, which must be a supported build, and are not included. When that file is not found the editor shows a notice and the channel stays silent with its settings kept. A new instance starts from the plugin's preset in your own FL Studio installation, so adding one needs FL Studio installed; otherwise the Add menu lists it as requiring FL Studio. On .flp import without that file the channel uses a simpler synth conversion.
controls: Hold button, octave shift of -1, 0 or +1, and the main volume.
On button, Mode (Up, Up/dn or Down), Range (1, 2 or 3), Sync and Rate.
Rate with a Sync switch, Delay, Auto or Man trigger mode with a Trig button, and a Phase switch with its fader for the retrigger phase.
LFO is the amount of LFO on the oscillator. PWM sets the pulse width, driven by the LFO, set by hand (Man) or driven by the envelope.
Buttons that switch the pulse, saw and sub waves, a fader for the sub level and a fader for the noise level.
Freq (cutoff) and Res (resonance) of the low-pass filter, Env amount with a + or - polarity switch, LFO amount and Kybd (key follow).
The amplifier follows the envelope (Env) or the key gate (Gate).
A, D, S and R faders of the envelope.
tips: Cut groups do not cut this generator.
Self-oscillating presets can drift in phase against an FL render.

name: Kepler Exo
desc: Two-oscillator analogue-style synthesizer with cross modulation, two envelopes and LFOs, modulation matrix, arpeggiator and effects. Plays and imports Kepler Exo channels.

wiki.intro: Kepler Exo is the two-oscillator version of Kepler and runs on the same engine, with a second oscillator, cross modulation, a second envelope and LFO, a modulation matrix and effect pages for saturation, chorus, EQ, delay and reverb. Its tables are read at run time from the Kepler Exo engine DLL in your own FL Studio installation, which must be a supported build, and are not included. When that file is not found the editor shows a notice and the channel stays silent with its settings kept. A new instance starts from the plugin's preset in your own FL Studio installation, so adding one needs FL Studio installed; otherwise the Add menu lists it as requiring FL Studio. There is no fallback conversion for imported channels.
controls: Hold, Octave (-1, 0 or +1), the X and Y offsets of the modulation routes, master Detune, Vol and Pan.
DCO 1, DCO 2: LFO1, LFO2, Env2, PWM
Amounts of LFO 1, LFO 2 and envelope 2 on the oscillator, each LFO with a wide switch, and the pulse width with its source: LFO, Man or Env.
Buttons for the pulse, saw and sub waves, with faders for the sub level and the sub Phase.
Switches oscillator 2, tunes it in semitones and fine steps, and syncs it.
1>2 and 2>1 set how much each oscillator is modulated, each with a shape: Sine, Tri, Pulse, Saw, Noise or the other oscillator.
Levels of DCO1, DCO2 and Noise, and the AM amount.
Slope of 6, 12, 18 or 24 dB, Freq, Res, Env1 amount with a + or - polarity switch, LFO1, LFO2 and Kybd amounts, and FM with its own shape choice.
On switch and Freq of the high-pass filter.
The amplifier follows Env1, the key gate or Env2. Vel sets how much velocity changes the volume and Smooth switches smoothing.
A, D, S and R faders of each envelope.
Rate with Sync, Delay, Auto or Man trigger mode and a Phase switch with its fader. LFO 2 adds a shape: Tri, Ramp up, Ramp dn, Sine, S&H or Rnd glide.
LFO trig button, Exp or Lin portamento with the Glide knob, and the Mono, Legato, Retrig and Release switches.
On button, Range (1 to 3), a Mode menu with nine modes (up, down, random and as played variants), Sync, Rate and Gate.
Eight knobs, 1 to 8, that set the amounts of the eight modulation routes.
Off, I, II or I+II, with a Noise knob and a Gate switch.
Tabs for Saturation (Drive, Pre or Post, HQ), Chorus, EQ (Gain, Freq and Q for Low, Mid and High), Delay and Reverb. Each page has its own On switch.
tips: Imported Kepler Exo channels keep their settings, including the modulation matrix.
States that use the 4x oversampling flag are refused by the engine.

name: Keyboard Controller
desc: Control generator that turns the last key played into a value you draw per key. It makes no sound and can drive other controls.

wiki.intro: The Keyboard Controller sets its output to the value you drew for the last key played. It makes no sound; you link its output to another control. You draw the values with the mouse over the keyboard.
controls: Bars above the keyboard; the height of each bar is the output for that key.
Value the output goes to when no key is held.
When no key is held, the output goes to the note-off value.
Every key's value rising from 0 at the lowest key to 1 at C10.
tips: Imported FL projects keep Keyboard Controller values.

name: Kick
desc: Built-in kick drum: a sine tone that sweeps down from about 155 Hz to 45 Hz with a short decay. It has no editor window.

name: Layer
desc: Makes no sound itself. Every note it receives is passed on to its child channels, so one pattern can play several generators at once.

wiki.intro: A Layer is a channel without a sound of its own. Add it to the Channel Rack, choose which channels are its children, and every note sent to the Layer plays those children. Use it to stack instruments, split a keyboard between sounds or alternate between samples.
controls: The channels selected in the Channel Rack become this Layer's children.
Selects this Layer's children in the Channel Rack.
Menu to split, reset, group or delete the children.
Each note plays one child picked at random. Off, every child plays.
The children play in turn, one per note (round robin).
The Fade knob moves from the first child to the last, blending neighbours.
tips: Inside a Patcher the Layer has a Children pin: cable it to the generators it should play.
Layering > Split children gives each child one key, starting from the root key.

name: LYNX Soundfont
desc: Plays SoundFont 2 and 3 banks and SFZ instruments, with preset search across all your SoundFonts, envelope, filter and built-in reverb and chorus.

wiki.intro: LYNX Soundfont is the generator for SoundFont banks and SFZ instruments. Load a file, pick a preset and play it, or search the presets of every SoundFont in your folders and preview them with a click. It opens the settings of FL Studio's SoundFont player when a .flp project is imported.
controls: Searches every preset of every SoundFont in your folders. Click previews, double-click loads it into the channel.
The folders searched for SoundFonts, and a rescan.
Pitch LFO: Delay, Amount, Speed, Mod wheel
Vibrato of the voice and how far the mod wheel drives it.
Send amount of the player's own reverb and chorus.
Also sends the effect input to a mixer insert, for a reverb or chorus of your own.
How transposed samples are interpolated, from linear to 16-point sinc.
Plays the loops of the samples. Off, every sample plays once.
tips: Drag a preset from the list onto the Channel Rack to get a new channel with it.
The reverb and chorus are LYNX SHARE's own, not the sound of FL Studio's built-in ones.

name: MIDI Effect Rack
desc: Ableton Live-style rack of MIDI effect chains on a Channel Rack channel. It makes no sound itself: the notes from its chains play the channels set as its children.

wiki.intro: MIDI Effect Rack is a Channel Rack generator built on Patcher in rack mode. Its chains hold MIDI effects only. Every chain gets the same notes, and what the chains play goes to the rack's child channels, as with a Layer channel. Add it from the plugin picker as MIDI Effect Rack. The same chains of MIDI effects can also sit at the head of an Instrument Rack chain.
controls: In the chain menu: makes the channels selected in the Channel Rack the children this rack plays. Show children selects them again.
One row per chain. The chain menu has Add chain, Rename, Duplicate, Delete, Move up and Move down.
The MIDI effects of the selected chain, added from the MIDI effects menu.
Choose the zone editor: key zones, velocity zones, chain-select zones, or none. Zones run from 0 to 127.
Drag a bar or its ends to set the zone. The upper strip of a bar sets the fades. In a MIDI Effect Rack all three fades scale the velocity of the notes.
The value the chain-select zones are compared with. A macro can drive it.
A switch in the chain menu, stored with the rack.
Up to 16 knobs. + and - show more or fewer.
Map mode. Each macro gets a Map button that opens a menu of the chains' device parameters and Chain Selector. The mapping list shows Macro, Path, Name, Min and Max.
Gives every mapped macro a random value, except macros excluded from randomization.
Store and launch sets of macro values: New, Launch, Overwrite, Rename, Duplicate and Delete.
tips: Until children are set, the rack's title bar says there are none yet and the rack plays nothing.
The chains have no volume or pan: a MIDI Effect Rack only passes notes.

A LYNX SHARE MIDI Effect Rack is written to an exported Live set as a MIDI Effect Rack, without the built-in MIDI effects inside it. When a Live set is opened, Live's MIDI Effect Racks are not converted; they are listed in the import report.

name: MIDI Out
desc: A silent channel that sends its notes and controller values as MIDI to the plugins listening on its port, and carries 72 controller knobs.

wiki.intro: MIDI Out makes no sound. Its notes go out as MIDI on a port, and plugin channels whose MIDI input port matches that port play them. It also holds 72 controller knobs in 8 pages that can send CCs, aftertouch or pitch bend to those plugins.
controls: MIDI channel the notes go out on, 1 to 16. A new MIDI Out takes the next channel and skips channel 10.
The program change this channel selects.
Bank select CC 0, sent before the patch. A dash means not sent.
Bank select CC 32, sent before the patch. A dash means not sent.
MIDI output port. Plugins whose MIDI input port is this port play it.
Chooses one of the 8 pages of 9 knobs.
The channel's pan, volume and pitch go out as CC 10, CC 7 and pitch bend.
Map note color to MIDI channel
Each note goes out on the MIDI channel of its colour.
Sets a plugin channel's MIDI input port to this port.
Every control sends nothing until it gets a value.
Sends reset all controllers (CC 121) and resets the controls.
Load or save the settings as a preset.
tips: The editor shows which plugins currently listen on the port.
Right-click a knob and choose Configure... to assign its controller.

name: MiniSynth
desc: Synth engine with table oscillators and noise, a 4-pole filter, two envelopes, an LFO and distortion, delay, phaser and chorus effects, rebuilt from FL Studio's MiniSynth.

wiki.intro: MiniSynth is a generator built on the engine of the FL plugin of the same name: table oscillators with noise, a 4-pole filter, amplifier and filter envelopes, an LFO, and distortion, delay, phaser and chorus in that fixed order. The wave tables are built at run time from oscdata.dat in your own FL Studio installation, which is not included. A new instance starts from the plugin's preset in your own FL Studio installation, so adding one needs FL Studio installed; otherwise the Add menu lists it as requiring FL Studio. On .flp import without that file the channel uses a simpler internal synth conversion.
controls: Oscillator, Amplifier, Filter, Filter env, LFO and Effects. Each tab shows one group of controls.

Oscillator page. The menu picks one of ten oscillator kinds (Saw, Saw + saw, Pulse, Square + saw, Square + square, Supersaw, Bell, Deaf saw, Saw spread, Saw spread 2). Transpose shifts the pitch, Modifier changes the chosen waveform and Noise adds noise.
Poly, Mono or Lead, and the slide time between notes.
Sends the mod wheel to Filter or LFO, by the set amount.
Attack, Decay, Sustain and Release faders of the amplifier envelope, with a display of its shape.
A pad that sets Cutoff and Resonance together, the same two values as knobs, and Keyboard and Velocity tracking.
Attack, Decay, Sustain and Release faders, and an Amount knob that works in both directions.
Shape (Sine, Saw or Square), Rate, Destination (Filter, Frequency or Osc. modifier) and Amount.
On switch, Time, Feedback, Filter and Mix.
On switch, Rate, Mod (depth) and Mix.
On switch, Speed, Width, Feedback, Mix and Freq.
tips: Noise, dither, drift and random phases come from a generator owned by each instance, so they differ from any given FL render.

name: Morphine
desc: Additive synthesizer engine that morphs between waveforms, with a noise generator, equaliser and chorus, delay and reverb effects.

wiki.intro: Morphine is an additive generator built on the engine of the FL plugin of the same name: four generators combined through a morph line into up to 128 sine oscillators per voice, plus a noise sample player, then overdrive, chorus, delay, reverb and an eight-band equalizer. The noise sample is read at run time from your own FL Studio installation; when it is not found the noise stays silent. A new instance starts from the plugin's preset in your own FL Studio installation, so adding one needs FL Studio installed; otherwise the Add menu lists it as requiring FL Studio. The generator, morph line and modulation pages are not editable here.
controls: Transpose, fine tuning and pitch bend range.
Attack, Decay, Sustain and Release of the master amplitude envelope.
Level, pan and velocity response of the noise sample player.
On switch and eight band faders at 62, 125, 250 and 500 Hz and 1, 2, 4 and 8 kHz.
On switch, Depth, Rate and Mix.
On switch, Time, Stereo, Fdbk (feedback), Mod depth and Mix.
On switch, Decay, Hi-cut (damping) and Mix.
tips: Effects run in the order overdrive, chorus, delay, reverb, equalizer.
Release loops and unison of the original are not modelled.
Changing a setting restarts the sounding voices.

name: Ogun
desc: Additive synthesizer engine with spectral timbre controls, unison, filter, three-band equaliser and chorus, delay and reverb effects.

wiki.intro: Ogun is an additive generator built on the engine of the FL plugin of the same name. Each voice builds a spectrum of up to 32,767 partials from seeded random weights and turns it into wave tables, followed by a filter, a three-band EQ, chorus, delay and reverb. A new instance starts from the plugin's preset in your own FL Studio installation, so adding one needs FL Studio installed; otherwise the Add menu lists it as requiring FL Studio. The articulator curves are not editable here.
controls: Master volume, coarse pitch and fine pitch.
Modulation X and Y values. The pad sets both together.
Rendering quality. Higher settings read the wave tables with better interpolation, and settings 2 to 4 run at twice the sample rate. Export always uses 4.
Richness: how many partials the spectrum has.
Pre-decay, decay time and release time of the spectrum.
Fullness shaping and morph of the spectrum.
Seeds for the random weights of the partials.
Unison: Ord, Pan, Vol, Pitch, Phase
Unison order, and the panning, volume, pitch and phase spread of the unison voices.
Three bands, each with a level fader and Freq and Width knobs.
Ord (order), Dep (depth), Spd (speed), Del (delay), Spr (spread), Crs (cross) and Mix.
On switch, Mode (feedback mode), Tempo (tempo sync), Fb (feedback), Time, Ofs (stereo offset) and Vol.
On switch, Col (color), LC and HC (low and high cut), Pre (predelay), Size, Diff (diffusion), Dec (decay), HD (high damping) and Wet.
tips: The delay and the reverb run only while their On switches are lit.
Seed 2 set to Random is a fixed draw per channel, so it does not match an FL render.
Changing a setting rebuilds the instance.

name: Patcher
desc: A node graph of instruments, effects and VST3 or CLAP plugins joined by audio, note and control cables, used as a Channel Rack generator.

wiki.intro: Patcher is a node graph. Add instruments, effects and VST3 or CLAP plugins as nodes and join them with audio, note and control cables. Cables are delay compensated. It is also available as a mixer slot, and Patchers in FL Studio projects open as the same graph.
controls: Adds a plugin node from the picker.
Adds a plugin node from the plugin database.
Zooms the graph to show every node.
Opens the editor of a node.
Removes all cables of a node.
Switches a single cable on or off.
Sets the gain of a cable.
Hides parameter or event pins nothing is cabled to.
tips: Right-click a node, a pin or a cable to get these menus.
Extra audio outputs can go to other mixer inserts.

name: Plucked!
desc: Plucked string synthesizer using a Karplus-Strong delay line, with decay and colour knobs plus normalise, gate and widen switches.

wiki.intro: Plucked is an engine for FL Studio's Plucked. Each note excites a string modelled by a delay line, so it sounds like a plucked string. It plays imported projects and its presets.
controls: How long the string rings. 0 to 256, default 128.
Mixes noise into the excitation. 0 to 128, default 64.
Normalises the decay per pitch. On by default.
Note-off silences the voice. Off, a note rings until it has died away.
Runs a second, separately excited string for the right channel.
tips: The random seed differs per instance, so two renders of the same notes are not sample identical to FL Studio, which seeds from the clock.

name: Pocket SuperSaw
desc: Virtual analog synth with up to 12 detuned saws per voice, a sub oscillator, a 4-pole low-pass filter, three envelopes, an LFO, an arpeggiator, distortion and delay. Rebuilt from FL Studio Mobile's SuperSaw.

wiki.intro: Pocket SuperSaw is a virtual analog synthesizer with up to 8 voices. Each voice is a stack of 1 to 12 detuned saw waves with a sub-octave saw, or the SuperSync oscillator, a train of pulses that sweeps like hard sync. It is the engine that FL Studio Mobile projects (.flm) load their SuperSaw module on, and it is also in the plugin picker under Pocket SuperSaw. A new channel starts from FL Studio Mobile's defaults. The page is a plain list of knobs, one per parameter (59 in all), not FL Studio Mobile's own panel.
controls: Osc unison, Osc unison detune, Osc unison detune curve, Osc unison pan
Number of saws per voice (1 to 12), how far they are detuned (up to 100 cents), how the detune is spread across the saws, and how wide they are panned.
Osc pulse width, Osc pulse mode, Osc sub level
Pulse mode turns each saw into a pulse wave, with its width. Osc sub level is the level of the saw one octave down.
Osc re-trig phases, Osc phases offset
With re-trig on, every note starts the saws at the same phases, so the beating is the same on every note. Off: each note starts at random phases.
SuperSync mode, Osc sync, Osc sync pulse width, Osc sync attack / decay / sustain / release, Osc sync EG amount, Osc sync kbd dir
The SuperSync oscillator and its own envelope, which sweeps the sync amount.
Filter cutoff, Filter resonance, Filter kbd, Filter vel
A 4-pole ladder low-pass filter, up to 20 kHz, with keyboard and velocity tracking.
Filter EG attack / decay / sustain / release, Filter EG amount
The filter envelope. The amount is bipolar, -100 % to +100 %.
Level EG attack / decay / sustain / release, Level, Pan
The volume envelope and the output level and pan. Envelope times run from 0 to 31 seconds.
LFO shape, LFO rate, LFO mode, LFO beat, LFO amount, LFO dest, LFO fade in
One LFO per voice: Sine, Ramp, Square or Random; Free, One shot or Tempo sync. LFO dest picks Cutoff, Resonance, Pitch, Sync, Pulse width, Detune, Level or Pan.
Arp rate, Arp range, Arp mode
Arpeggiator: Off, Up, Down, Up-down, Up-down (ends twice) or Random, over up to 3 extra octaves.
Monophonic mode, Number of voices, Slide held mode, Slide time, Slide time static
Play one voice or up to 8, and how notes glide.
Transpose by -12 to +12 semitones. The pitch wheel bends by 1 to 12 semitones.
A tanh distortion and an output trim of -18 to 0 dB.
Delay time, Delay feedback, Delay mix, Delay filter
A tempo-synced stereo delay, 1/4 beat to 1 beat, with a low-pass or high-pass filter in its loop.
Mod wheel amount, Mod wheel dest
What the mod wheel moves: Cutoff, Resonance, Sync, Pulse width, Detune, Level, Pan, LFO amount or LFO rate.
tips: Every knob can be automated. The saws are band-limited, so high notes do not alias.
Start phases and the Random LFO come from a generator owned by each instance, so a render never matches a given FL Studio Mobile render sample for sample. The energy and the spectrum do.
The channel's pitch knob, fine tune, Mono and Porta and the Piano roll's slide notes act on the voices as they do on FL Studio's generators.

name: PoiZone
desc: Two-oscillator synth engine with unison, filter, LFO, envelopes, arpeggiator, step gate, chorus and tape-style delay.

wiki.intro: PoiZone is a subtractive generator built on the engine of the FL plugin of the same name: two saw or pulse oscillators with noise, hard sync and ring modulation, a 4-pole filter, an LFO, a modulation envelope and an amp envelope, then a 16-step gate, chorus, stereo tape delay and arpeggiator. It can be added without FL Studio and then starts from LYNX SHARE's own preset bank.
controls: Unison voice count (1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 12 or 16), polyphony, and the detune and pan spread of the unison voices.
Oct switches the octaver and Mono monophonic play. Held and Static choose the glide modes.
Glide time, transpose, fine tuning and master gain.
Destination of the mod wheel (Cutoff, LFO amt, Frq A, PW A or PW AB), its Amount, and Bend for the pitch bend range.
Destination (Cutoff, Frq A, Frq AB, PW A, PW AB or Pan), Amount, Rate, shape (Saw, Pulse, Tri, Sine or Rnd), Retrig and Sync (Free or 1 to 128).
Modulation envelope: destination (Cutoff, Frq A, Frq AB, PW A or PW AB), Amount, and Att, Dec, Sus, Rel.
Att, Dec, Sus and Rel of the amplitude envelope.

A / B balances the two oscillators and Noise adds noise. Each oscillator has a Saw or Sq shape and a pulse width (PW A, PW B). Ring switches ring modulation and Sync hard sync. Pitch B shifts oscillator B in semitones and Detune B detunes it.
Cutoff, Reso, Key trk (key tracking) and Vel trk (velocity tracking), with LP, BP and HP modes.
Mode (Off, Up, Down, Up-dn or Rnd), octave range 1 to 4, and Speed.
Sixteen step buttons, with Smooth, Mix and Speed.
On switch, Time L, Time R, Feedback, Mod, Low cut, High cut and Wet.
On switch, Depth, Rate and Wet.
Bend is the pitch bend, which springs back to the centre when released. Mod is the mod wheel.
tips: Changing a setting restarts the sounding voices.
Noise, drift and start phases come from generators owned by each instance, so they differ from any given FL render.

name: Sakura
desc: Physical-model synth of plucked and struck strings, with exciter, two strings, comb, resonators, modulation matrix, delay, chorus and reverb.

wiki.intro: Sakura is a physical string model rebuilt from the engine of the FL plugin of the same name. A noise or click exciter passes a low-cut and a high-cut filter and drives two strings, each with a comb, followed by resonators, chorus, reverb and delay. The model runs at an internal 48 kHz. It can be added without FL Studio and then starts from LYNX SHARE's own preset bank.
controls: Noise sets the balance between a single click and held noise. Rate sets how often the noise value changes.
Two-pole high-pass on the exciter. Cutoff runs from 32 Hz to 20.2 kHz and Res sets its resonance.
Four-pole resonant low-pass on the exciter with its own envelope. Cutoff and Res set the filter, Drive saturates it, and Attack, Decay and Sustain shape the envelope.
Decay is the feedback of the string loop, which sets how long the string rings. Inv negates the feedback.
Damp low-passes the string loop (0 is no damping). Offset damps the far node of the string harder. Sharp adds a sharpness feedback to the loop filter.
Pitch of string 2 as a multiple of string 1: 4x, 3x, 2x, 1x, 1/2x, 1/3x or 1/4x.
Level and Feedback of the comb on each string, each with an Inv switch. Comb ratio sets the comb length as a fraction of the string length.
Mix balances string 1 against string 2. Stereo separates them: centred at the middle, string 1 left and string 2 right at 0. Saturate sets the saturation inside both string loops.
Attack, Decay, Sustain and Release of the amplitude envelope.
Eight resonators, each with a feedback knob, a frequency slider and an on switch.

An envelope (A, D, S, R) and an LFO rate, plus eight slots. Each slot has a source (Envelope, LFO, Mod wheel, Pitch wheel, Aftertouch, Velocity, Key or Release), an amount knob with a negative switch, and a target such as Level, Pan, Pitch, the filter cutoffs or the string decay and damp.
On switch, Time, Sync (Off or 1/32 to 2 bars), Feedback, Speed, Depth, Blur and Wet.
Chorus has an On switch, Depth, Rate and Wet. Reverb has an On switch, Decay, Color and Mix.
tips: New parameter values apply to the next note.
The Mod wheel, Pitch wheel and Aftertouch sources read 0, because no MIDI controllers are routed to the matrix.

name: Sawer
desc: Saw-based synth engine with a sub saw, unison, filter, LFO, arpeggiator, modulation slots and chorus, phaser, delay and reverb effects.

wiki.intro: Sawer is a subtractive generator built on the engine of the FL plugin of the same name: a saw oscillator plus a sub saw, hard sync, noise, a 4-pole filter with low, band, high and notch outputs, then chorus, phaser, delay and reverb, with a six-slot modulation matrix and an arpeggiator. The oscillator cycle is read at run time from data.saw in the Sawer folder of your own FL Studio installation and is not included. When that file is not found the editor shows a notice and the channel stays silent with its settings kept. A new instance starts from the plugin's preset in your own FL Studio installation, so adding one needs FL Studio installed; otherwise the Add menu lists it as requiring FL Studio.
controls: Polyphony (4 to 24 voices) and pitch bend range (off, or 1 to 12).
Level, Pan and the A, D, S, R faders of the amplitude envelope.
Rate or Time mode, Always or Held key mode, and the glide Time.
Poly or Mono, the octaver Off or On, and Free or Sync for the unison retrigger.
1, 2, 4 or 8 voices, with Detune and Spread (pan).
Noise level, and the Sync frequency with its On switch.
Level, Phase, Harmonic (a ratio from 1/4 to 4) and Detune of the second oscillator. The switches choose Free or Sync retrigger, + or - polarity, and Saw or Pulse form.
Cutoff, Reso, Key (key tracking) and Vel (velocity tracking), with Low, Band, High and Notch modes.
A, D, S, R and Amount, sent to Cutoff, Sync, Sub phase or Pitch.
Speed, Attack, Release and Amount; Free or Sync retrigger, Hz or Beat timing, Inv, a shape (Tri, Saw, Square or S&H) and a destination (Cutoff, Sync, Sub phase, Pitch, Noise, Volume or Pan).
Chorus has a switch, Depth, Rate and Mix. Phaser has a switch, Center, Rate, Depth, Fdbk and Mix.
Delay has a switch, Left and Right times, Fdbk, Mod, LoCut, HiCut and Mix. Reverb has a switch, Decay, HiCut, Damp and Mix.
Six slots. Each has a source (Velocity, Aftertouch, Pitch wheel or a MIDI CC), an amount knob and a destination chosen from the plugin's parameters.
On switch, mode (Up, Down, Up/dn or Rnd), range 1 to 4 and a note division from 1/32 to 3/4.
tips: Modulation by aftertouch and pitch bend is not fed to the engine in this version.

name: SimSynth
desc: Classic three-oscillator synth engine with ring modulation, amplifier and filter envelopes, a resonant filter and an LFO.

wiki.intro: SimSynth is an engine for FL Studio's SimSynth. It plays imported projects and its installation presets. Three oscillators go through a filter and an amplifier, each with its own envelope.
controls: Each has a waveform choice of Pulse, Cos, Tri, Noise and Sine, plus Shape, Coarse, Fine, Level, LFO and Env knobs.
Amp: Att, Dec, Sus, Rel, Vel
Filter: Att, Dec, Sus, Rel, Env
Filter envelope and how much it drives the filter.
LFO and keyboard tracking of the filter.
Cutoff, emphasis and the high-pass and band-pass amounts.
Speed and onset delay, with Sq, Saw, Tri and S&H shapes.
Restarts the LFO on each note.
tips: Automation of its controls is not wired in this version.

name: Slicex
desc: Slicer and drum sampler with two sample decks. The regions of each deck play from their own keys, with layering, articulator envelopes and LFOs, and a filter per articulator group.

wiki.intro: Slicex loads a sample on each of two decks, A and B, cuts it into regions and plays each region from a key. It opens the settings of FL Studio's Slicex from a .flp and writes them back on export. A new instance starts with empty decks and needs no files from an FL installation. A WAV file that brings no regions of its own is sliced on its hits when it loads.
controls: Master level, Master randomness level, Master LFO level and Master pitch, minus 1200 to 1200 cents.
An X / Y pad with X and Y wheels. SMOOTH smooths the modulation.

How regions on the same key play together: All, All (gain-compensated), Velocity-mapped, Modulation X-mapped, Modulation Y-mapped, Random, Cycle or Song time-synced. SAME DECK layers regions of the same deck only.
The curve between layered regions: none, linear, balanced curve, unbalanced curve or adding.

The current region, its OUT (output track offset) and CUT (cut group), and four rows: AMP (panning and volume), FILTER (cutoff and resonance), SPEED (pitch) and START (delay and sample start). Each row has an ART group number and an amount.
Selects one of 8 articulator groups. Its FILTER has a type (LP, BP, BS, HP), a mode (OFF, x1, x2, x3) and ENV, CUT and RES wheels.
PAN, VOL, CUT, RES, SPEED, START
The target the curve editor shows.
ENV, LFO, VEL, MOD X, MOD Y, RAND
The part of the articulator shown: its envelope, its LFO, or the map from velocity, modulation X, modulation Y or randomness.
TEMPO makes the curve's time follow the tempo. GLOBAL makes the LFO phase run with the song.
Scale the envelope's attack, decay and release times and offset its sustain level.
LFO speed, tension, skew and pulse width.
Loop, Play / pause, Stop, the File, Regions, Select and Zoom menus, single or dual deck display, and the current deck, A or B.
New, Load sample... and Save sample as..., which saves the deck's WAV with its regions.
Add region..., Add marker..., Set loop, Delete, Rename all..., Set all cut groups to... and Freeze all.
Plays the keys and shows which have regions. Its menu has Assign current region to this key and Select region assigned to this key. The digit beside it sets the base octave.
Sample start covers whole length, Link velocity to volume, Loop half of regions and HQ envelopes.
tips: Drop a sample on a deck to load it. Only a WAV file gets markers from the automatic slicing, because the markers are stored in the deck's WAV.
A region's menu has Delete, Clone as region, Turn into marker, Rename..., Trigger note and Zoom on.
Notes with an even colour play deck A and notes with an odd colour play deck B. Colours 14 and 15 play reversed.
FL's Snap and View menus are not there yet, and the File and Regions menus have only the entries listed above.

name: Snare
desc: Built-in snare drum: a short sine tone with high-passed noise and a 0.22 second decay. It has no editor window.

name: Synth
desc: LYNX SHARE's own three-oscillator subtractive synth with a filter, envelopes, a tone control and a modulation page. It is the default instrument of a new project.

wiki.intro: The built-in synth of LYNX SHARE. Add it as a channel from the picker and play it from the piano roll or a keyboard. It has three oscillators, a resonant filter, an amplitude envelope and a three-band tone control, with envelopes and LFOs on a separate modulation page.
controls: Waveform choice for each of the three oscillators.
Stereo position and volume of each oscillator.
Makes the cutoff follow the note.
A pitch drop at the start of each note, useful for kicks.
Three-band tone control after the filter.
One voice at a time; a new note takes over the sounding one.
Glide from the previous note, with the glide time in beats.
Osc 3 modulates the amplitude of oscillators 1 and 2, with a ring-modulation variant.
Osc 3 shifts the phase of oscillators 1 and 2, with a decay of the amount.
tips: The Presets menu and the FL presets button load ready-made settings.
Open Modulation (envelopes and LFOs) for filter and pitch envelopes and LFOs.

name: Sytrus
desc: Six-operator FM and ring-modulation synth with a modulation matrix, three filters and unison. It plays imported FL Studio Sytrus channels and presets.

wiki.intro: Sytrus is an FM and ring modulation generator built on the engine of the FL plugin of the same name: six operators, a modulation matrix, three filter units, unison and its own effects chain. It plays Sytrus channels and presets from imported projects. A new instance starts from the plugin's preset in your own FL Studio installation, so adding one needs FL Studio installed; otherwise the Add menu lists it as requiring FL Studio. The editor shows the Main page; the operator, filter and effect pages are not editable here and keep the saved patch.
controls: Master level, master LFO and master pitch faders. Pitch runs from -24 to 24.
Attack, decay, sustain and release faders of the volume envelope.
Attack, decay, sustain and release faders of the filter envelope.
Pn, Vl, Pt, Sb, Ph, En
Unison pan, volume, pitch, sub layer, phase and envelope variation.
Modulation X and Y values. The pad sets both together.
Extra envelope accuracy, switched separately for Draft (live playback) and Render (export).
Oversampling order from 0 to 4, where each step doubles the factor, set separately for Draft and Render.
Rows are destinations: operators 1 to 6 and filters F1 to F3. Columns 1 to 6 set how much each operator modulates that row; Pan, FX and Out set the row's pan, effects send and output level.
Switches the operator columns of the matrix between frequency modulation and ring modulation amounts. Pan, FX and Out show on both.
tips: During export the engine uses the Render settings; live playback uses the Draft settings.
Chaotic FM patches do not match an FL render sample for sample.
States older than version 17 use a simpler synth conversion instead of the engine.

name: Toxic Biohazard
desc: Six-operator FM and wavetable synth with a filter, two LFOs, two effect slots and an eight-band equaliser. It plays imported FL Studio Toxic Biohazard channels.

wiki.intro: Toxic Biohazard is an FM generator built on the engine of the FL plugin of the same name: six oscillators that modulate each other through a matrix, a 4-pole filter with its envelope, two LFOs, a step sequencer, distortion, two effect slots and an eight-band EQ. Built-in waves 2 to 32 are read at run time from your own FL Studio installation and are not included; wave 0 (the preset's own spectrum) and wave 1 (a sine) play without it, and a wave display that lacks its data shows Needs FL Studio's files. It can be added without FL Studio and then starts from LYNX SHARE's own preset bank. On .flp import, a patch that needs the missing waves falls back to a simpler two-operator conversion.
controls: Transp. (transpose), Poly (polyphony), Voices (unison voices) with Detune and Spread, the Glide mode (Bend VT, Held VT, Bend ST or Held ST) and its Time.
Att, Dec, Sus and Rel of the master amplitude envelope, Vel curve, Drive (distortion) and Master (gain).
Vel, Init, Att, Dec, Sus and Rel set each oscillator's velocity response, initial level and envelope.
Osc 1 to Osc 6: Wave, Pitch, Detune, Freq ofs, Phase
Wave number (0 to 32) with a display of its shape, coarse pitch, fine detune, frequency offset and start phase. Free lets the oscillator run free and On switches it.
A 6 by 6 grid of knobs where the oscillator of the row modulates the oscillator of the column.
Mod page: Mix, Pan, LFO 1, LFO 2, Pitch mod
Per oscillator: output mix, pan and the amounts of LFO 1 and LFO 2. Pitch mod sets how much LFO 2 and the filter envelope move the pitch, and Bend is the bend range.
Eight modulation slots, each with a source, an amount and a destination parameter.
A step sequencer with up to 64 steps. Each step is a rest, a hold or a value from -24 to 24. Number of steps sets the length; Play, Swing, Dual, Ping-pong and Random are its switches.
Wave number with a display, Speed, Sync (Off or 1/16 to 4 bars) and Free.
Mode (Off, LP, BP or HP), Cutoff, Reso, Key trk, Vel trk, EG amount, LFO 1 amount and the four faders of the filter envelope.

Each slot has an On switch and a type: Delay, Chorus, Reverb, Flanger, Phaser or Lo-fi. The knobs below change with the type, for example Time, Feedback, Rate, Depth, Blur, Mix and a Sync menu for Delay.
On switch and eight band faders from 62 Hz to 8 kHz.
tips: Switching Seq Play on or off releases every held key.
Phases of free-running oscillators come from a generator owned by each instance, so they differ from any given FL render.

name: Transistor Bass
desc: Monophonic bass synth with a step sequencer, distortion, delay and reverb. It plays imported FL Studio Transistor Bass channels and programs.

wiki.intro: Transistor Bass is a monophonic bass generator built on the engine of the FL plugin of the same name: a saw or square oscillator, a 4-pole low-pass filter with accent and decay envelopes, distortion, stereo delay and reverb, and 128 programs that each hold a patch and a 16-step sequence. The recorded oscillator cycles of the 303 pulse mode are read at run time from the engine DLL in your own FL Studio installation, which must be a supported build, and are not included. When that file is not found the editor shows a notice and the channel stays silent with its settings kept. A new instance starts from the plugin's preset in your own FL Studio installation, so adding one needs FL Studio installed; otherwise the Add menu lists it as requiring FL Studio.
controls: Tuning and waveform of the oscillator. The 303 button switches to the recorded pulse cycles.
Cutoff, Reso, Env mod, Decay, Accent
Filter cutoff and resonance, how far the envelope moves the cutoff, the envelope decay and the accent amount. Notes with a velocity of 110 or more are accented.
HP (high-pass), Min dec (minimum decay), Key (key follow), LFO PW (LFO amount on the pulse width), LFO rate, PW (pulse width) and Clicks, which the plugin stores as VCA smooth.
Switch, HP, Drive, Tone and Volume.
Switch, Amount, Time, R tap (right tap), Fdbk, Tone, Stereo and a Sync button for tempo sync.
Switch, LoCut, HiCut, Pre (predelay), Pre fb (predelay feedback), Size, Diff, Decay, Damp, Width, Dry, ER (early reflections) and Wet.
Off: notes play the synth directly and a note played while another is held slides. On: a note selects the program of its key and runs that program's sequence in 16th notes until the key is released.
Number of steps the sequence plays.
The five rows of the step editor. Per step: its note and octave, whether it sounds, whether it holds into the next step, and whether it is accented.
tips: MIDI volume and pitch bend events and parameter automation are not modelled.
With the sequencer on, releasing the key stops the sequence.

name: VFX Color Mapper
desc: A Patcher note processor that sends each note to a voice output and changes its note colour, depending on the colour it arrives with.

wiki.intro: One of the VFX note processors from FL Studio's Patcher. It has no sound of its own. It reads the note colour of each incoming note, which is the same as its MIDI channel, and routes it. Use it in a Patcher between a source and instruments.
controls: The 16 incoming note colours, one row each.
The output the notes of that colour leave on.
The note colour the notes leave with.
tips: Notes from the piano roll carry the colour group they were drawn with, so you can split one pattern across instruments.

name: VFX Envelope
desc: A Patcher note processor that shapes a note's velocity, pitch, pan and modulation values over time with an envelope and an LFO per target.

wiki.intro: A VFX note processor from FL Studio's Patcher with no sound of its own. It changes properties of the notes that are sounding while they sound. It has 16 articulators, each for one note colour and key range.
controls: Velocity, pitch, pan, Mod X or Mod Y.
Switch between the two shapers of a target.
Turns the shaper on for the target.
Syncs the shape to the song tempo.
Amount of the envelope and of the LFO, negative values invert.
tips: Put it before an instrument in a Patcher to add movement to held notes.

name: VFX Key Mapper
desc: A Patcher note processor that remaps each key of an octave to other notes, with a choice of how several outputs play.

wiki.intro: A VFX note processor from FL Studio's Patcher with no sound of its own. It maps the keys you play to other notes, for example to turn single keys into chords or to move notes to a scale. Inputs are listed down one octave and outputs across.
controls: How an input mapped to several notes plays them: All, All (gain-compensated), Random, Cycle up or Cycle down.
The key the mapping is relative to.
Pitch slide setting of the mapped notes.
