tips: Outputs reach from an octave below to an octave above each input.

name: VFX Keyboard Splitter
desc: A Patcher note processor that splits the keyboard and velocity range into 16 zones, each sending its notes to its own output.

wiki.intro: A VFX note processor from FL Studio's Patcher with no sound of its own. It has 16 zones. A note plays on every zone whose level at that key and velocity is above zero, on that zone's output.
controls: Page that draws each zone's level over the keys.
Page that draws each zone's level over the velocity.
Shifts the notes of a zone, in semitones, from -48 to 48.
Sets the zone to the whole range at full level.
While on, played keys are taken and not played. Each key ends the current zone and starts the next.
tips: Manual mapping needs rising keys; a lower or equal key is ignored.
With the 16th zone started, the mapping turns off and that zone runs to the top of the keyboard.

name: VFX Level Scaler
desc: A Patcher note processor that reshapes velocity, release, fine pitch, pan or modulation values of notes with a transfer curve and optional randomness.

wiki.intro: A VFX note processor from FL Studio's Patcher with no sound of its own. Each note property has its own tab and its own curve, so you can for example compress velocities or invert pan.
controls: Velocity, release, fine pitch, pan, Mod X and Mod Y.
Slope around the centre; negative values invert.
Moves every value up or down.
Bends the curve; positive rises fast, negative starts slowly.
A random amount for each note.
Resets all controls of the shown property.
tips: A tab left at its defaults passes the value unchanged.

name: VFX Script
desc: A Patcher note processor driven by a Python script that can change, create and delay notes. Runs with LYNX SHARE's built-in Python.

wiki.intro: A VFX note processor from FL Studio's Patcher with no sound of its own. It runs a Python script on the notes that reach it. LYNX SHARE runs it with a built-in Python (pocketpy) with the modules math, random, re, time and sys. Scripts cannot open files.
controls: The controls the script defines, and its output controllers.
Messages and errors of the script.
The functions and properties a script can use.
Goes back to the script that is running.
tips: LYNX SHARE runs at most 15 scripts at once.
Click the error button to jump to the line of an error.

name: VFX Sequencer
desc: A Patcher note processor that turns held notes into arpeggios and step sequences, using a bank of 128 programs with six lanes of 64 steps.

wiki.intro: A VFX note processor from FL Studio's Patcher with no sound of its own. Held notes drive a bank of up to 128 step programs, each with six lanes of up to 64 steps. Use it in a Patcher in front of an instrument.
controls: Off, On, Thru, or on or thru from 2 keys.
How the held keys are ordered.
What plays when a step has no key.
Notes keep playing after release, until a new chord.
Several keys or octaves per step.
Taken from the lane, the keys or both.
Beat, key, first key or play.
Ignored, selects the sequence or is passed on.
Rand. vel., Rand. gate, Rand. start
tips: Use the shift buttons to move the pattern one step earlier or later.
Page lock plays only the page shown.

name: Voltage Controller
desc: Turns notes into control voltages and clock pulses for modular gear, through a DC-coupled audio interface. It makes no audible sound itself.

wiki.intro: A tool that sends the notes of a channel as control voltages for modular synthesisers. It needs a DC-coupled audio interface. Each output has its own source, offset and scale. Outputs beyond the first pair can feed mixer inserts.
controls: Sends the voltages. Off is silence, which is the default for a new one.
Voltage range of the interface: plus or minus 10 V, plus or minus 5 V or 0 to 10 V.
1 V per octave or 1.2 V per octave.
Clock pulses per quarter note, while the song plays.
Length of a pulse in samples, from 1 to 500.
The mixer insert a pair of outputs is added to.
tips: 0 V is C5 on the pitch outputs.
Offsets and scales can be automated.

name: Wave Traveller
desc: Plays a loaded sample by moving a read position along a drawn curve, with a second curve for volume. It plays imported FL Studio Wave Traveller channels.

wiki.intro: Wave Traveller is a sample generator built on the engine of the FL plugin of the same name. Each of the 120 keys holds its own patch: a position curve that moves through the sample over the note's time, a volume curve and mute switches. The key does not transpose the sample; the channel pitch changes the speed of the curve. It needs no FL Studio files. Without a sample the channel is silent, so load one or drop one on the editor.
controls: Loads the sample the curves travel through. Dropping a sample on the editor does the same.
Loads the curves of one of FL Studio's Wave Traveller presets into the current key. The list is empty when FL Studio is not installed.
Copies the current key's patch to all keys, or resets it.
Selects the key whose patch is shown. Each key plays its own curves.
Switch the curve view between the position curve (where the note is in the sample over its time) and the volume curve.
Drag a point to move it. Double click adds or removes a point. Right click sets the segment type and tension or deletes the point.
Tempo based spline: the curve lasts a number of beats. Absolute speed based spline: the curve plays the sample at a speed factor.
In tempo based mode, the beats the curve lasts (0.125 to 8). In absolute mode, a factor of the sample's own speed (0.25 to 4).
Fade in (1 to 500 ms) and fade out (1 to 1000 ms) of the note.
The part of the sample the curve spans.
A strip of mute switches along the curve. Click switches one, right click removes it.
tips: At the end of the curve the last 256 output samples play backwards with a fade out.
Samples that are not 16-bit at 44.1 kHz go through LYNX SHARE's own conversion.
Live playback uses a 6-point polynomial interpolation; export uses a windowed sinc.
